articles.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease: mechanisms, pathogenic interplay, and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a major cause of dementia, yet effective disease-modifying therapies are still limited. Although amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau pathology remain core features of AD pathogenesis, they do not fully explain how these pathological alterations drive progressive cellular dysfunction. Increasing evidence suggests that mitochondria are involved at this critical interface. In AD, mitochondrial abnormalities impair energy production, compromise organelle quality control, disrupt calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis, and alter communication with the endoplasmic reticulum and glial cells. As these defects accumulate, neurons and glia become less able to maintain metabolic stability, redox balance, and synaptic function. Mitochondrial dysfunction is therefore relevant to AD not as a single isolated lesion, but as a convergent process through which metabolic failure, oxidative stress, mitochondrial DNA damage, inflammatory signaling, and defective cellular maintenance reinforce one another. This perspective also helps explain why disease progression is difficult to reverse once mitochondrial homeostasis has been broadly compromised. At the same time, this framework also points to therapeutic opportunities, as the mechanisms driving the development and progression of mitochondrial dysfunction may be amenable to intervention. However, many mitochondria-centered strategies remain preclinical or have yielded inconsistent clinical benefit. Current evidence supports mitochondrial dysfunction as both a useful mechanistic basis for understanding AD progression and a biologically meaningful, though challenging, therapeutic target.

articles.title: Sinoatrial node dysfunction: molecular mechanisms, arrhythmogenesis, and translational pathways toward precision therapy.
articles.abstract: Sinoatrial node dysfunction (SND) is a major cause of bradyarrhythmia, chronotropic incompetence, tachy-brady syndrome, and a common indication for permanent pacemaker implantation, particularly in older adults. Although SND has diverse etiologies, this review focuses on aging-associated intrinsic SND, while considering other common causes where they inform differential diagnosis, arrhythmogenic mechanisms, or therapeutic development. Although current medical interventions provide effective rhythm support, they does not correct the molecular and tissue-level processes that drive sinoatrial node (SAN) degeneration. The review integrates current knowledge of SAN biology with mechanisms underlying SND, including fibrosis, ion-channel and calcium-clock remodeling, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, impaired β-adrenergic signaling, genetic susceptibility, and epigenetic or epitranscriptomic regulation. We further discuss how these mechanisms contribute to impaired impulse generation, SAN exit block, reduced chronotropic reserve, and increased susceptibility to atrial arrhythmia. We discuss approaches for studying the molecular and cellular mechanisms and evaluating therapeutic strategies using emerging animal models, human pluripotent stem cell-derived SAN-like pacemaker cells, organoids, assembloids, and single-cell and spatial omics platforms . Finally, we highlight translational opportunities, including senescence-directed, metabolic, antifibrotic, autonomic, gene-based, regenerative, and biological pacing strategies. A mechanism-guided classification of SND may support future precision therapies that complement conventional pacing by linking dominant rhythm phenotypes to targetable biological drivers, molecular and functional pharmacodynamic markers, and human-relevant models of pacemaker failure.

articles.title: Overview of Regulatory Guidelines Related to Methods and Models for Small Populations.
articles.abstract: This paper provides an overview of approaches and related guidelines from the EMA, FDA, and ICH that are relevant for obtaining clinical evidence for small populations to support regulatory decision making. The approaches are grouped into three categories: (1) maximizing the attainable sample size, (2) adapting the trial design to deal with a small sample size, and (3) including external information, while also examining the role of modeling. Guidelines for clinical trials, guidelines specifically for small populations, as well as guidelines that include the use of modeling to support clinical evidence were included in the review. A recurring theme throughout the guidelines is the critical importance of the clinical context, affecting both the evidentiary standard and which approaches and models are acceptable. Two key gaps were identified: (1) guidance on Bayesian approaches is limited, and (2) there is no clear guidance on how to synthesize evidence across different modalities, such as trial results and Real-World Data, from both a practical and regulatory perspective.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled RNA therapeutic design: from molecular optimization to system-level evaluation.
articles.abstract: RNA therapeutics are increasingly moving from empirical screening towards rational, computation-guided design. Recent advances in RNA language models, generative models and structure-aware learning have improved sequence representation, candidate generation and structure-constrained optimization. However, favourable molecular properties do not necessarily translate into desirable biological performance, because therapeutic outcomes also depend on modality-specific mechanisms, delivery and exposure, molecular interactions, cellular state, immune responses and network-level adaptation. Here, we review AI-enabled RNA therapeutic design through the specific lens of the interface between molecular optimization and system-level evaluation. We compare the design constraints of siRNAs, antisense oligonucleotides, aptamers, mRNAs and translation-oriented circRNAs, and examine the capabilities and current limitations of sequence-, generative- and structure-based computational models. We further discuss the data resources and perturbation representations required to connect molecular candidates with broader cellular-response models. In this context, virtual cells are considered as approximate computational frameworks for candidate prioritization and risk-oriented system-level assessment rather than complete digital replicas of living cells. Finally, we outline a conceptual generation-simulation-feedback-optimization framework for integrating molecular design with progressively higher-level evaluation. This perspective emphasizes the need for better interfaces among RNA design, pharmacological context and cellular-response modelling, rather than relying on molecular optimization alone.

articles.title: Tetrodotoxin (TTX): What do we currently know? The state of the art.
articles.abstract: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent naturally occurring neurotoxins and continues to attract considerable scientific, clinical, forensic, and regulatory attention. Historically associated with pufferfish poisoning in East and Southeast Asia, TTX has recently emerged as a global food safety concern due to its detection in an increasing number of marine and terrestrial organisms and its expanding geographical distribution, including European coastal waters. Despite decades of research, important questions regarding its biosynthesis, ecological origin, toxicokinetics, and environmental dissemination remain unresolved. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge on TTX. The chemical structure, physicochemical properties, proposed biosynthetic origin, and diversity of naturally occurring TTX analogues are discussed. Attention is devoted to the toxin's mechanism of action, which involves high-affinity binding to voltage-gated sodium channels and subsequent inhibition of sodium ion conductance, leading to neuromuscular paralysis and potentially fatal respiratory failure. Current evidence regarding toxicokinetics, tissue distribution, elimination pathways, and the suitability of different biological matrices for laboratory confirmation of exposure is also summarized. The review further examines the analytical challenges associated with TTX determination, including its high polarity, occurrence at trace concentrations, rapid elimination from blood, and frequent co-occurrence with structurally related analogues. The evolution of analytical methodologies is presented, from early bioassays and chromatographic techniques with fluorescence or UV detection to advanced liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry platforms, high-resolution mass spectrometry, capillary electrophoresis, immunochemical assays, and emerging biosensor-based approaches. Finally, current regulatory perspectives and risk assessment strategies are discussed in the context of the increasing occurrence of TTX in seafood and the growing need for harmonized monitoring programs. Collectively, this review summarizes the current state of the art, identifies key knowledge gaps, and highlights future directions in TTX research.

articles.title: Transcriptomic effects of lead on the differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into ectoderm: implication for adverse pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopmental disorders.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological studies revealed associations between maternal lead (Pb) exposure and adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes as well as neurodevelopmental disorders. However, the underlying mechanisms remained unclear, and thus was investigated at the transcriptional level in this study using human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Differentiation of hESCs to ectoderm was induced for 7 days using STEMdiff™ Trilineage Differentiation Kit containing 0 (water), 6.2 (geometric mean concentration of Pb in human maternal blood), or 118 µg Pb2+/L, in the form of lead chloride (PbCl2), followed by bulk RNA sequencing. Both doses of PbCl2 altered gene expression related to protein metabolism and trafficking, while also causing changes in genes involved in gastrulation, proliferation, DNA repair, stress response, and immune-cell development. PbCl2 at the low dose induced gene changes predicting decreased cell proliferation and increased sensory loss. Cells exposed to the high dose of PbCl2 had a distinct global gene expression profile from that of control cells with specific changes predicting increased neurodegeneration. The differences in expression of ectoderm lineage marker genes (ELMG) between control and PbCl2 treated cells did not reach statistical significance. However, expression of some genes downstream of ELMG differed markedly between control and PbCl2 treated cells. Multiple adverse outcome pathways involving WNT, IGF-1, RHO-PKN, CDK5, MAP kinase, and Ca2+ signaling, cell cycle control, protein metabolism and trafficking, DNA double strand break and repair, and immune response were detected in PbCl2 treated cells. Overall, the findings suggest that Pb exposure disrupted early ectodermal development by prioritizing genome preservation over fate execution.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Ra1 alleviates endothelial barrier dysfunction and multi-organ injury in experimental sepsis via NMMHC IIA inhibition.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) has emerged as a significant therapeutic target in vascular diseases and sepsis. However, effective interventions targeting NMMHC IIA in sepsis-induced endothelial dysfunction remain unelucidated. Here, we have assessed ginsenoside Ra1 (Ra1) as a potent NMMHC IIA inhibitor and evaluate its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in sepsis. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We used the caecal ligation and puncture model of polymicrobial sepsis in mice. Survival rate, body temperature, pathological changes, vascular permeability and plasma biochemical indicators were measured to evaluate the effects of Ra1 treatment. Molecular docking technique, cellular thermal shift assay, microscale thermophoresis assay and surface plasmon resonance were performed to confirm the binding of Ra1 with NMMHC IIA. Downstream genes affected by Ra1 were screened via RNA-sequencing and validated using western blotting and immunofluorescence. In vitro, a lipopolysaccharide-induced endothelial barrier injury model in human umbilical vein endothelial cells was established, and endothelial permeability was evaluated. KEY RESULTS: Ra1 bound strongly to NMMHC IIA, whose knockdown ameliorated sepsis-induced endothelial barrier disruption and multi-organ injury (lung, intestine, liver and kidney). Ra1 attenuated mortality, hypothermia, multi-organ injury, vascular hyperpermeability and endothelial junction disruption in septic mice. Mechanistically, Ra1 inhibited TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signalling to exert its protective effects, which were absent after NMMHC IIA was silenced, demonstrating an NMMHC IIA-dependent mechanism. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings identify Ra1 as a potential inhibitor of NMMHC IIA and provide mechanistic insight into therapeutic strategies targeting endothelial dysfunction in sepsis, which warrants further investigation in clinical studies.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection leads to altered neuro-immune biomarker profiles at birth.
articles.abstract: Maternal infection during pregnancy can induce immune-mediated biological adaptations that influence fetal neurodevelopment. Although vertical transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is uncommon, the impact of maternal infection on fetal neuroimmune signaling remains poorly characterized. We investigated whether prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with alterations in circulating neuroimmune biomarkers detectable at birth. In this case-control study, 28 women with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and 61 uninfected controls were enrolled. Maternal and cord blood samples were collected at delivery. Following an initial inflammatory screening, neuro-specific biomarkers (NfL, Tau, P-Tau217, GFAP, S100β, α-Synuclein) and PTX3 were measured. Correlation network analyses, PTX3 promoter methylation assessment, and haplotype stratification analyses were also performed. Systemic inflammatory mediators did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, neonates exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection exhibited significantly lower cord blood concentrations of GFAP, NfL, and P-Tau217 and increased α-Synuclein levels compared with controls. Tau showed a decreasing trend, whereas S100β and PTX3 remained unchanged. Network analyses revealed reduced cytokine connectivity but enhanced interactions among neuro-specific biomarkers. Although PTX3 promoter methylation was unchanged, the PTX3 h2/h2 haplotype appeared to modulate biomarker interaction patterns. To our knowledge, this is the first study to characterize a circulating neuro-specific biomarker signature in neonates prenatally exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection. This supports the utility of neuroimmune biomarker networks as translational tools to investigate the biological consequences of maternal immune activation during pregnancy.

articles.title: Mechanisms overcoming the resistance of human TRPV2 to chemical activation.
articles.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 2 (TRPV2) is a thermosensitive cation channel widely expressed across diverse cell types. There, it contributes to numerous physiological processes and plays a role in the pathophysiology of inflammation, immunity, various cancers and neuronal development. The inherent resistance of human TRPV2 (hTRPV2) to stimuli that readily activate its rodent orthologs currently limits progress in translational and clinical research on this channel. Here, we present engineered variants of hTRPV2 that were designed to enhance channel activation induced by 2-aminoethoxydiphenylborate (2-APB), cannabidiol, and the TRPV2 agonist AV2-1, thereby identifying sites that allow for the most effective channel regulation. Through a series of rational mutations and chimeric constructs, combined with electrophysiology and molecular modeling, we identified two key allosteric sites in hTRPV2 that determine the resistance of the channel to activating stimuli. We discovered that two intracellular membrane-proximal salt bridges prevent effective activation of hTRPV2: (i) one formed between residues of the putative 2-APB-binding site and the bottom of S6 helix (R533-E647), and (ii) another formed between residues from the TRP helix and the proximal N-terminus (D655-R369). We also propose possible mechanisms by which the non-conserved pore turret contributes to channel activation. Our results may facilitate the rational drug design towards potent and selective hTRPV2 ligands and help to elucidate the functions of this channel in organs or cell types of interest.

articles.title: Colonic administration of baitouweng decoction alleviates ulcerative colitis via coordinated reprogramming of arginine and tryptophan metabolism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves persistent colonic inflammation, loss of epithelial barrier integrity, and disturbed immune regulation. Although Baitouweng decoction (BTW) is widely used for intestinal inflammatory disorders, the effects and mechanisms of colon-targeted administration remain unclear. PURPOSE: This study evaluated the effects of transendoscopic enteral tubing (TET)-mediated colonic BTW administration (CBTW) in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) induced colitis and examined its association with arginine and tryptophan metabolism. METHODS: CBTW efficacy was evaluated in DSS-induced colitis rats using integrated phenotypic, histological, multi-omics, and immune profiling approaches. Candidate metabolic pathways were mechanistically validated through pharmacological inhibition of arginase activity, IDO1, and AhR signaling using BEC hydrochloride, 1-methyl-L-tryptophan, and CH-223191, respectively, combined with downstream metabolite rescue by spermidine and kynurenine. RESULTS: CBTW ameliorated DSS-induced colitis, reducing body-weight loss, DAI scores, colonic shortening, histopathological injury, mucus depletion, and barrier disruption. Multi-omics analyses revealed coordinated alterations in arginine and tryptophan metabolism. CBTW was associated with increased ARG2 expression, elevated ornithine and spermidine levels, and enhanced M2 macrophage-associated responses. It was also associated with increased kynurenine and kynurenic acid levels and enhanced AhR-related signaling, as indicated by CYP1A1 upregulation. These changes coincided with an improved Treg/Th17 balance, reduced inflammation, and enhanced epithelial barrier integrity. Pharmacological inhibition and metabolic rescue supported the functional involvement of the ARG2-associated arginine-spermidine axis and IDO1-kynurenine-AhR pathways. CONCLUSIONS: CBTW alleviated DSS-induced colitis and coordinately modulated arginine and tryptophan metabolism, providing preclinical support for its further evaluation as a TET-delivered treatment for UC.

articles.title: Antitumor potential of medicinal plants from the Brazilian Cerrado: a systematic review of experimental studies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Brazilian Cerrado harbors 12,180 cataloged angiosperm species; 7395 (60.7%) are endemic to Brazil, and its flora has been used in traditional medicine for generations. Regardless, the antitumor potential of these species has been investigated in a fragmented manner. PURPOSE: To compile and analyze experimental evidence on the antitumor effects of preparations derived from Cerrado plant species in vitro and in vivo models. METHODS: Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus, without date restrictions and limited to publications in English. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using an adapted risk-of-bias assessment tool. RESULTS: Sixty-two studies were included; 55 employed in vitro models and 12 employed in vivo models, five of which combined both approaches. The studies encompassed a broad range of malignancies, including melanoma, leukemias, glioblastoma, and breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers, and evaluated crude extracts, fractions, and isolated compounds from >40 species. The most frequently documented antitumor effects were cell viability reduction, apoptosis induction via the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, cell cycle arrest, and matrix metalloproteinase inhibition. Annona crassiflora, Campomanesia adamantium, Stryphnodendron adstringens, and Tapirira guianensis were each reported in three or more independent studies (most frequently investigated species). Relevant methodological limitations, including a widespread absence of tumor selectivity data, pharmacokinetic profiles, and experimental blinding, were revealed. No clinical trials evaluating Cerrado plant species as oncological interventions were identified. CONCLUSION: The Cerrado flora represents a relevant source of compounds with preclinical antitumor activity, but essential translational data remain absent. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO database (CRD420261372222). Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261372222.

articles.title: Xanthatin overcomes osimertinib resistance by disturbing cholesterol metabolism via targeting HMGCR protein degradation in NSCLC.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is a third-generation, irreversible EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), nevertheless, the inevitable occurrence of osimertinib resistance after a long-term administration limits its clinical application in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Xanthatin, a naturally active component from Xanthium Strumarium L., has been shown to possess multiple bioactive effects. However, whether xanthatin can ameliorate osimertinib resistance remains unclear. PURPOSE: The present study aimed to clarify the role and detailed mechanism of xanthatin in reversing osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. METHODS: Combenefit analysis, LDH release assay, and EdU staining were employed to evaluate the effect of xanthatin on osimertinib cytotoxicity in osimertinib-resistant (OR) NSCLC cells. Quantitative proteomics combined with bioinformatics and network pharmacology analysis was used to uncover the specific target of xanthatin. Xanthatin-triggered HMGCR protein degradation was assessed by bio-layer interferometry, drug affinity responsive target stability assay, cycloheximide chase assay and ubiquitination determination. The function of xanthatin on cholesterol homeostasis was measured via the detection of HMGCR activity, total cholesterol, triglycerides and lipid droplets as well as MDR1 distribution in the lipid rafts. The function of MDR1 was examined via a rhodamine 123 efflux assay. The accumulation and efflux of osimertinib were monitored using FITC-labeled osimertinib. The effect of HMGCR on the cytotoxicity of xanthatin was evaluated through a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments in HMGCR-overexpressing NSCLC OR cells. RESULTS: Xanthatin restored the sensitivity of NSCLC OR cells to osimertinib, accompanied by the induction of oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Proteomic data indicate that oxidative stress and metabolic reprogramming contribute to xanthatin-induced apoptosis in NSCLC OR cells. Through further integration with network pharmacology, we identified HMGCR (a key enzyme of cholesterol metabolism) as a potential target of xanthatin. We confirmed xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR protein (KD=6.753 μM), subsequently facilitating AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGCR. Xanthatin diminished intracellular cholesterol biosynthesis and MDR1 levels in lipid rafts. HMGCR overexpression mitigated the cytotoxicity of xanthatin and sustained cholesterol homeostasis, enabling tolerance to the combined effects of xanthatin and osimertinib. Conversely, HMGCR-deficient NSCLC OR cells were more vulnerable to osimertinib. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates for the first time that xanthatin directly binds to HMGCR and promotes AMFR-mediated K48-linked ubiquitination of HMGCR, which in turn accelerates HMGCR degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, leading to reduced cholesterol synthesis, less distribution of MDR1 in lipid rafts, ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial dysfunction-associated apoptosis, ultimately restoring osimertinib sensitivity in NSCLC cells. Therefore, xanthatin may represent a preclinical natural product candidate for the reversal of osimertinib resistance in NSCLC cells, which requires further translational verification in future studies.

articles.title: Aspirin eugenol ester attenuates alcoholic liver injury via the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway-mediated ferroptosis suppression.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcoholic liver injury (ALI) is a prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and represents a major public health burden. Previous pharmacological and pharmacodynamic studies have indicated that aspirin eugenol ester (AEE) exerts multiple pharmacological activities, including protective effects against non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. However, whether AEE can ameliorate ALI and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. PURPOSE: This study sought to explore the protective effects of AEE on ALI and to delineate the associated molecular mechanisms. METHODS: This study investigated the protective effects of AEE against ALI using both in vitro and in vivo models, with a particular focus on elucidating its molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: In cellular models, AEE significantly alleviated ethanol- and erastin-induced cytotoxicity and morphological damage, while markedly reversing abnormalities in superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, Fe2+ accumulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, 4-Hydroxynonenal levels and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, AEE attenuated ethanol-induced ferroptosis by activating the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 antioxidant axis. This result was validated in primary mouse hepatocytes. In animal models, AEE markedly improved alcohol-induced metabolic disturbances, including dyslipidemia, glucose disorders, and hepatic steatosis, while restoring hepatic redox homeostasis and ethanol metabolism through upregulation of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) and suppression of CYP2E1. Consistently, AEE enhanced NRF2 signaling and ferroptosis resistance in liver tissues, as evidenced by increased expression of SLC7A11, GPX4, ferritin, and HO-1, along with reduced expression of BAP1, Keap1 and P53. CONCLUSIONS: AEE exerts a potent protective effect against ALI by attenuating ethanol-induced ferroptosis via activation of the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 signaling pathway, thereby improving hepatic metabolic homeostasis.

articles.title: BeatVecNet classifies drug-induced contractile phenotypes from beat-gated motion vectors in micropatterned human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Assessment of electrophysiological cardiotoxicity in vitro has advanced, yet scalable assays for contractile dysfunction remain limited. BeatVecNet, an interpretable deep-learning framework, classifies drug-induced contractile phenotypes from beat-gated motion vectors in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: BeatVecNet was developed and evaluated using beat-gated motion-vector tensors derived from hiPSC-CMs recorded by label-free phase-contrast imaging at 150 fps. hiPSC-CMs were cultured on micropatterned substrates to provide a consistent contraction axis for directional motion analysis. Dense optical flow was used to derive motion vectors, which were retained as beat-gated spatiotemporal tensors rather than reduced to scalar traces. The model uses two convolutional branches to process horizontal and vertical velocity components separately and was evaluated on independent assays containing control, doxorubicin, trastuzumab and sunitinib. KEY RESULTS: BeatVecNet distinguished drug-induced contractile phenotypes with a macro-F1 of 0.916, outperforming conventional kinematic classifiers (best baseline 0.706), with the largest advantage at low doses. Branch-replacement ablation indicated non-redundant contributions of horizontal and vertical motion components, with trastuzumab classification showing greater sensitivity to horizontal-component replacement and sunitinib classification to vertical-component replacement. Phase-resolved attribution further identified temporal patterns within the beat cycle not explained by peak velocity alone. Micropatterning improved signal consistency and contractile coherence, enabling robust directional motion analysis. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: BeatVecNet extracts drug-associated contractile signatures not captured by conventional scalar analysis while providing direction- and phase-resolved interpretability at the motion-representation level. This platform complements electrophysiology-centred safety assessment and provides proof of concept for classification of subtle drug-induced contractile phenotypes.

articles.title: Cholinergic inputs to motoneurons in the spinal cord augment focal muscle spasticity in rodents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cholinergic premotor inputs to motoneurons support high levels of motor output when required. However, the possible role of these inputs in pathologically elevated muscle tone has not been characterised. To address this, we examined the modulatory effect of spinal acetylcholine (ACh) on experimental spastic paralysis. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Rats were injected with tetanus neurotoxin (TeNT, 33-100 pg, im) into gastrocnemius to induce sustained rigid hind-paw extension and resistance to passive ankle flexion. The effects of spinal ACh on experimental hypertonia were probed by lumbar intrathecal application of the AChE inhibitor neostigmine (NEO) or a muscarinic M2 receptor antagonist (AQ-RA 741). Effects of NEO on extracellular ACh were measured in the facial nucleus after TeNT (33 pg) or botulinum toxin A (BoNT/A, 2 U) injection into the rat whisker pad. The intensity of TeNT-evoked hindlimb hypertonia (10 pg, im) was assessed in mice with genetic ablation of cholinergic C bouton source interneurons (V0C interneurons). KEY RESULTS: NEO augmented the severity of TeNT-evoked hypertonia, whereas AQ-RA 741 attenuated it. Local perfusion of NEO caused a BoNT/A-sensitive increase in extracellular ACh concentration. The involvement of cholinergic C boutons was corroborated by reduced hypertonia following TeNT challenge (10 pg, im) in V0C-ablated mice. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Our results suggest that spinal cholinergic transmission, associated with vesicular ACh release and M2 signalling at C boutons, exacerbates experimental spastic paralysis. We reveal a new role for endogenous spinal ACh, with implications for developing new therapeutic approaches to treat spasticity and hyperkinetic movement disorders.

articles.title: Screening traditional Chinese medicine monomers for premature ovarian insufficiency: from network meta-analysis to the effects of a promising candidate on oxidative stress biomarkers.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Therapeutic options for premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) are limited, and the comparative efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) monomers remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate and rank the efficacy of various TCM monomers in animal models of POI and to explored the potential role of oxidative stress modulation by a promising candidate. METHODS: Eight electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, VIP, Wanfang Database, and SinoMed) were searched from inception to 3 April 2026, for randomized controlled animal trials evaluating single TCM monomers in POI models. The SYRCLE tool and CINeMA were employed to assess the risk of bias and the certainty of evidence, respectively. A frequentist network meta-analysis was conducted to compare primary and secondary ovarian function outcomes, with relative efficacy ranked by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values. Pairwise meta-analyses were then performed to evaluate the effects of a candidate monomer on oxidative stress biomarkers. Three-dimensional scatter plots were used to visualize potential trends in primary outcomes regarding the relationships among dose, treatment duration, and therapeutic efficacy. RESULTS: Thirty-two studies involving 676 animals and six TCM monomers were included. Compared with controls, all monomers significantly reduced serum follicle-stimulating hormone and increased estradiol levels. Furthermore, quercetin and icariin promoted follicular development and suppressed atresia., although the certainty of evidence was very low. Based on global mean SUCRA values, quercetin ranked first in the main analysis and emerged as a promising candidate overall. Pairwise analyses showed that quercetin increased serum superoxide dismutase and catalase while decreasing malondialdehyde levels. Exploratory three-dimensional visualization suggested a potential enhanced therapeutic trend for quercetin within the dosage range of 25-100 mg/kg over 10-30 days. CONCLUSION: Several TCM monomers improved ovarian function in POI models. Quercetin was considered a promising candidate, with its potential effect likely associated with the modulation of oxidative stress biomarkers. Given the substantial heterogeneity and very low evidence certainty, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further rigorous, standardized preclinical dose-response studies and well-designed clinical trials are warranted to facilitate the clinical translation of these findings. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261359490, identifier CRD420261359490.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of antibody-drug conjugates in pretreated HER2-positive advanced breast cancer: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have become the standard treatment for HER2-positive(HER2+)advanced breast cancer following the failure of trastuzumab or taxane. Nevertheless, there are no direct head-to-head trials comparing different ADCs. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and abstracts from major oncology conferences, and included phase III randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating HER2-targeting ADCs. We conducted a frequentist random-effects NMA, and utilized the P-score to rank the efficacy of included treatments. The outcome indicators include progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). RESULTS: Seven RCTs involving 3,160 patients and seven ADCs (T-DM1, ARX788, A166, SHR-A1811, RC48, DP303c and T-DXd) were included in our research. All ADCs showed a significant PFS benefit versus chemotherapy plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor (Chem + TKI). T-DXd showed the most favorable PFS (HR = 0.18, 95%CI: 0.13-0.25), followed by SHR-A1811 (HR = 0.22, 95%CI: 0.15-0.33) compared with Chem + TKI. SHR-A1811 showed a promising OS signal(HR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.14-0.69), followed by T-DXd (HR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.26-0.66) compared with Chem + TKI. For safety, T-DXd exhibited the highest odds for all-grade TRAEs relative to all included control treatments, with statistically significant differences identified when compared with T-DM1 and Chem + TKI., T-DM1 demonstrated better safety characteristics for grade ≥3 TRAEs, with a significantly lower odds of occurrence than SHR-A1811, ARX788, DP303c, and Chem + TKI. CONCLUSION: Included anti-HER2 ADCs significantly improve PFS over Chem + TKI, among which T-DXd and SHR-A1811 deliver notable survival benefits. Although T-DXd is associated with a higher odd of all-grade TRAEs and T-DM1 exhibits favourable grade ≥3 safety. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251234345, identifier CRD420251234345.

articles.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitors across neoadjuvant, perioperative, and adjuvant settings for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomized evidence for immune checkpoint inhibition in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer has progressed from pathological response to mature survival outcomes. We examined exploratory directional alignment across endpoints and quantified clinical yield, treatment burden, and the extent of perioperative therapy delivery. METHODS: We synthesized 20 peer-reviewed reports from 12 parent randomized trials, including 8,197 unique participants and 13 eligible randomized treatment comparisons. The parent trial was the analysis unit, and the latest compatible report replaced earlier estimates for each time-to-event outcome. Direct randomized comparisons were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models. We reconstructed cumulative event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) evidence, estimated absolute differences, performed exploratory trial-level cross-endpoint analyses, and pooled the proportion of experimental-arm patients who started postoperative study treatment. RESULTS: Across seven trials, treatment initiated before surgery reduced EFS events by 41% (HR, 0.59; 95% CI: 0.53-0.66; I2 = 12%). Five trials showed a 32% reduction in death (HR, 0.68; 95% CI: 0.58-0.80; I2 = 0%). Per 100 randomized patients, preoperative-start therapy produced 31 additional major pathological responses (95% CI: 24-39), 22 additional pathological complete responses (95% CI: 16-27), and 4 additional patients who underwent or attempted curative-intent surgery (95% CI: 1-7). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events increased by approximately 4 per 100 patients (95% CI: 0-8). In exploratory analyses, larger pCR improvements tended to accompany lower EFS HRs (Spearman ρ = -0.67; p = 0.098; k = 7), and EFS and OS estimates were directionally aligned (ρ = 0.95; p = 0.051; k = 4). In six perioperative trials, 69.7% (95% CI: 65.5%-73.7%) of randomized experimental-arm patients started postoperative study treatment. CONCLUSION: ICI-containing strategies initiated before surgery improve pathological response, EFS, and OS in resectable NSCLC. Approximately 70% of patients assigned to perioperative experimental arms started postoperative study treatment; this descriptive treatment-delivery finding does not establish whether postoperative ICI can be safely omitted. Prospective response- and residual-risk-guided randomized trials are required.

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of Traditional Chinese Medicine classical prescriptions for angina pectoris: a network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of classical prescriptions from Shang han Lun (Treatise on Febrile Diseases) and Jin gui Yao lue (Synopsis of the Golden Chamber) combined with conventional biomedicine in the treatment of angina pectoris of coronary heart disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eight commonly used Chinese and English databases were searched for relevant clinical studies published before 25 December 2024. Revman 5.4 and Stata14.0 software were used for data analysis. RESULTS: A total of 131 studies involving 11,292 participants (5,660 in intervention groups and 5,632 in control groups) were included. Most classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed favorable associations with improvements in angina pectoris efficiency, electrocardiogram (ECG) efficiency, and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome outcomes compared with conventional treatment alone. Subgroup analyses showed partially different patterns of relative efficacy among prescriptions, with LGZG demonstrating more consistent performance in stable angina pectoris, while other prescriptions showed variable rankings in unstable angina pectoris. For lipid-related and inflammatory outcomes, results were inconsistent across studies, and current evidence remains insufficient to support robust comparative conclusions among classical prescriptions. Regarding safety outcomes, GZFL combined with conventional biomedical therapy showed a relatively favorable safety profile, while other classical prescriptions demonstrated comparable rates of adverse events to conventional therapy. CONCLUSION: Classical prescriptions combined with conventional biomedical therapy may be associated with improvements in clinical outcomes of angina pectoris, with an overall acceptable safety profile observed across most intervention. However, due to limitations in study quality, heterogeneity, and indirect comparisons, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further high-quality, multicenter randomized controlled trials are required to confirm these observations. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251029216.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of lecanemab monoclonal antibody in the treatment of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lecanemab is a novel therapy for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but comprehensive evidence is lacking. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety in AD. METHODS: Registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251146867). PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for English-language RCTs. Efficacy and safety were evaluated using the risk difference with a Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effects model. Study quality and sensitivity were assessed using Cochrane risk-of-bias and leave-one-out methods. Primary outcomes: mean changes in Alzheimer's Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS), Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB), Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog), and amyloid burden on positron emission tomography (PET). Secondary: adverse events including amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema (ARIA-E), ARIA with hemorrhage (ARIA-H), death, treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), headache, dizziness, and urinary tract infection. RESULTS: A total of five articles involving 8 clinical trials were included. Based on the fixed-effect model, lecanemab treatment significantly improved cognitive performance on ADCOMS (SMD -0.1999, 95% CI [-0.2831, -0.1167], I2 = 0%, P < 0.00001), CDR-SB (SMD -0.1853, 95% CI [-0.2683, -0.1024], I2 = 0%, P < 0.0001), ADAS-Cog (SMD -0.1821, 95% CI [-0.2670, -0.0973], I2 = 0%, P < 0.0001) and amyloid burden on PET (SMD -1.1872, 95% CI [-2.2474, -0.1270], I2 = 96%, P = 0.03). Sensitivity analysis indicated stability. However, lecanemab was associated with an increased risk of TEAEs (MH RR 1.0730, 95% Cl [1.0296, 1.1183], I2 = 0%, P = 0.0008) and an increased risk of headache (MH RR 1.3617, 95% Cl [1.0243, 1.8103], I2 = 0%, P = 0.03). Sensitivity analysis indicated that both results were stable. The lecanemab group showed no significant differences in the risks of death, dizziness, or urinary tract infection compared with the control group. In addition, the lecanemab group showed a significantly increased risk of ARIA-E (MH RR 5.9948, 95% CI [3.9047, 9.2037], I2 = 86%, P < 0.00001) and ARIA-H (MH RR 1.7490, 95% CI [1.3896, 2.2014], I2 = 41%, P < 0.00001). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of the TEAE finding, while the headache result should be interpreted with caution due to the limited number of studies. After excluding Honig et al. (OLE) 2021 via leave-one-out, results became stable, likely due to its open-label design. CONCLUSION: Lecanemab slowed cognitive decline versus placebo in mild-to-moderate AD by ADCOMS, CDR-SB, and ADAS-Cog. High heterogeneity in PET amyloid burden warrants future RCTs. Nevertheless, lecanemab was associated with an increased risk of TEAEs and headache. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251146867.

articles.title: Highly potent, brain-penetrant EP2 receptor antagonists for the treatment of permanent focal cerebral ischaemia in male and female mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cerebral ischaemia is a leading cause of death in older adults and imposes a substantial global economic burden. Recent studies indicate that inhibiting the Gαs-coupled EP2 receptor reduces ischaemic brain injury by modulating neuroinflammation. However, these findings derive from the transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model, which represents only a small subset of large-vessel occlusion (LVO) cases with successful recanalisation. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We characterised the pharmacokinetic parameters of selective EP2 antagonists CJ-18, CJ-19 and CJ-21 that we recently developed. We evaluated their therapeutic efficacy in mice subjected to permanent MCAO (pMCAO), a model that more accurately reflects the majority of LVO cases, and assessed the impact of EP2 inhibition on brain injury and inflammation. Finally, we examined the effects of EP2 inhibition in neuron-glia mixed cultures exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) without reoxygenation. KEY RESULTS: After systemic administration in mice, new compounds exhibited favourable plasma half-lives and brain penetration. In the pMCAO model, treatment with EP2 antagonists significantly reduced brain infarction in both male and female mice, in a dose-dependent manner, whilst improving sensorimotor performance without affecting muscle strength. These benefits were accompanied by reduced neuronal death, lowered pro-inflammatory cytokines and attenuated reactive gliosis within the ischaemic penumbra. In addition, EP2 inhibition by CJ-18 conferred marked neuroprotection in neuron-glia co-cultures exposed to prolonged OGD, preserving neurite integrity and postsynaptic density. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This proof-of-concept study supports our drug-like EP2 receptor antagonists, particularly CJ-18, as potential treatments for permanent focal cerebral ischaemia.

articles.title: High-resolution pressure myography reveals pressure-dependent local contractile and geometric dynamics in the renal pelvis and ureter.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Coordinated peristalsis between the renal pelvis and ureter is critical for effective urine transport. However, intraluminal pressure impact on upper urinary tract (UUT) contractility and pharmacologic responsiveness remains poorly understood due to absence of suitable investigative methods. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: This study introduces the first application of high-resolution pressure myography to UUT, establishing a novel ex vivo platform enabling simultaneous, intraluminal pressure-controlled local measurement of renal pelvic contraction frequency and amplitude and ureteral inner diameter, outer diameter, and wall thickness. To define contribution of specific Ca2+ signaling pathways, we pharmacologically examined Cav1.2 L-type, Cav3.x T-type, and ryanodine receptor channels, as well as sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) and neuronal involvement. KEY RESULTS: Elevating intraluminal pressure from 4 to 20 mmHg increased renal pelvic contraction frequency, while amplitude markedly decreased. Ureteral wall thinning was the main structural adaptation. Nifedipine reduced renal pelvic contraction amplitude and frequency and suppressed ureter peak contraction, all with reduced efficacy under high-pressure conditions. Ni2+ affected renal pelvic contractility only at high concentrations and had no effect on ureteral dynamics. Ryanodine did not alter measured parameters, and Na+ and N-type Ca2+ channels were not involved. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: High-resolution pressure myography reveals pressure-dependent local contractile and geometric responses in UUT, including altered contraction dynamics, ureteral geometric remodeling, and specific Ca2+ channel contributions. Cav1.2 channels modulate both amplitude and frequency, with wall thinning as principal acute structural adaptation. Reduced drug efficacy at high pressure highlights necessity to investigate possible pressure-adapted therapies in obstructive uropathy.

articles.title: Unbound Intrinsic Formation Clearance of 6β-Hydroxycortisol Is a Useful Biomarker of CYP3A4 Activity during Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy results in multiple physiological changes that impact drug disposition. For example, hepatic CYP3A activity and renal transporter-mediated clearance increase in late pregnancy, but the time course of these changes across pregnancy is not known. Endogenous biomarkers offer a minimally invasive approach to characterize pharmacokinetic changes during pregnancy and postpartum. The goal of this study was to determine whether 6β-OH-cortisol formation clearance (CLf,OHCOL) can be used as a biomarker of hepatic CYP3A activity during pregnancy. Thus, we measured cortisol, cortisone, and 6β-OH-cortisol in plasma and urine from 47 women during late pregnancy and postpartum and calculated the CLf,OHCOL, unbound fraction (fu), unbound intrinsic CLf (CLf,u,int,OHCOL), and renal clearance (CLr). CLf,OHCOL increased 1.3-fold in late pregnancy while cortisol fu decreased significantly. CLf,u,int,OHCOL increased 1.8-fold, corresponding to a 2.1-fold increase in hepatic CYP3A activity. The increase in CLf,u,int,OHCOL was observed in CYP3A5 expressors and in CYP3A5 nonexpressors. In late pregnancy, the increase in CLr,cortisol and CLr,OHCOL exceeded the calculated increase in filtration clearance, suggesting increased transporter-mediated secretion. The decreased fu of cortisol during pregnancy was captured by a model incorporating increased expression of corticosteroid binding globulin (CBG) and increased binding affinity of cortisol to CBG. These data suggest that CLf,u,int,OHCOL is a robust biomarker of CYP3A activity during pregnancy and could be used in future studies to characterize the time course of changes in CYP3A activity across gestation and postpartum. Further, CLr,cortisol and CLr,OHCOL may be biomarkers of kidney OCT and MATE activity and could be used to evaluate kidney transporter activity during pregnancy.

articles.title: Veligrotug: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Veligrotug (veligrotug-vvze; LUMVOA™) is a monoclonal antibody insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) inhibitor that was developed by Viridian Therapeutics for the treatment of thyroid eye disease (also known as Graves ophthalmopathy/orbitopathy or thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy). In June 2026, veligrotug was approved by the US FDA for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of disease activity or duration, based on positive results from two multinational phase III clinical trials. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of veligrotug leading to this first approval for thyroid eye disease.

articles.title: Ischemic myocardium-targeted NAD+ nanotherapy mitigates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury remains a major cause of cardiomyocyte loss and adverse remodeling following acute myocardial infarction, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. Although nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) plays a central role in mitochondrial function and redox homeostasis, its therapeutic application is limited by poor membrane permeability and inefficient restoration of intracellular NAD+ pools. Here, we developed a cardiac-targeted lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticle (LN-DPC) that enables efficient intracellular delivery of NAD+ to ischemic myocardium. The nanoparticale integrates boronate-guanidine-mediated NAD+ encapsulation with an ischemic myocardium-homing peptide (CSTSMLKAC), achieving stable loading, controlled release, and preferential accumulation in injured cardiac tissue. In vitro, LN-DPC enhanced cellular uptake and restored intracellular NAD+ levels, leading to improved mitochondrial function, reduced reactive oxygen species generation, and alleviation of calcium overload under OGD/R conditions. In vivo, the nanoparticles preferentially accumulated in the injured myocardium, attenuated early inflammation, significantly reduced infarct size, improved cardiac function, and markedly limited chronic fibrosis. Mechanistically, NAD+ delivery restored SIRT3 expression, improved mitochondrial homeostasis, and suppressed HMGB1-RAGE signaling to mitigate secondary myocardial injury; pharmacological SIRT3 inhibition attenuated the protective effects of LN-DPC both in vitro and in vivo, supporting a functional contribution of SIRT3 to LN-DPC-mediated cardioprotection. Collectively, this work establishes targeted NAD+ delivery as an effective strategy to restore metabolic homeostasis and protect against ischemia-reperfusion injury, and provides a nanomedicine platform for metabolic intervention in cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Artemisitene targets GLIS3 to inhibit the NF-κB-TNF signaling pathway and suppress bladder cancer cell growth.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artemisia annua, a medicinal and edible herb best known for Artemisinin, exhibits broad pharmacological activities and considerable clinical value. However, its therapeutic potential in bladder cancer remains largely unexplored. PURPOSE: Here, we systematically investigated the anti-bladder cancer efficacy of Artemisitene (ATT) in vitro and in vivo and delineated its underlying mechanisms. METHODS: Using cell-based and animal models, we found that ATT robustly suppressed bladder cancer cell growth. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic sequencing, combined with MST assays and transient transfection, revealed the mechanism of ATT inhibiting the progression of bladder cancer. In addition, we analysed single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets and performed virtual knockout experiments to investigate the expression pattern and potential functional role of the ATT target gene GLIS3 across different pathological stages of bladder cancer. RESULTS: GLIS3 expression was higher in tumour than in adjacent nontumor tissues in BLCA patients and was further elevated in intermediate/late stages (T3-T4) compared with early stages (T1-T2). Consistently, single-cell RNA-seq data showed that GLIS3 levels in epithelial cells were higher in T3-T4 than in T1-T2 BLCA. Moreover, in virtual GLIS3 knockout in BLCA epithelial cells negatively regulated TNF and NF-κB signalling pathways. ATT directly interacts with GLIS3 and destabilizes the protein, consequently suppressing the transcription of NF-κB and TNF. Mutation of GLIS3 at Arg-404 and Pro-411 markedly weakened its interaction with ATT and partly abrogated the pharmacological effects of ATT. Moreover, GLIS3 knockdown enhanced the inhibitory effect of Gem on bladder cancer cells, while ATT further potentiated Gem-mediated suppression of BLCA by downregulating GLIS3 expression. CONCLUSIONS: ATT binds to GLIS3 and decreases its protein stability, thereby suppressing the transcription of NF-κB and TNF, inducing apoptosis in bladder cancer cells, and inhibiting cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for developing ATT as a potential therapeutic agent or dietary supplement for bladder cancer and expand the medicinal value of Artemisia annua derivatives.

articles.title: Kaempferide promotes melanogenesis through miR-145-associated glutathione depletion with partial ROS contribution.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the pathological link between vitiligo and both oxidative stress and melanin dysregulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS)-modulating therapies show limited efficacy. Kaempferide, a compound from Vernonia anthelmintica (L.) Willd, promotes glutathione (GSH)-dependent melanogenesis, yet its mechanism of action in vitiligo treatment remains to be fully elucidated. PURPOSE: This study aimed to elucidate whether kaempferide-induced melanogenesis is associated with GSH depletion and the underlying regulatory mechanism. METHODS: B16F10 cells, primary melanocytes from C57BL/6 J mice, and zebrafish larval models were used to investigate the role of GSH/thiol homeostasis in kaempferide-induced melanogenesis using biochemical, fluorescence-based, transcriptomic, miR-145-5p mimic transfection, and connectivity-mapping approaches. RESULTS: Kaempferide increased melanogenesis in cells and zebrafish and reduced intracellular thiol/GSH levels, accompanied by an increase in ROS. Further, it also reduced the expression of GSH-metabolic genes and proteins. NAC attenuated, whereas BSO potentiated, kaempferide-induced melanogenic responses, supporting GSH depletion as a major biochemical event. Transcriptomic analysis showed decreased miR-145 and increased Mest expression, and miR-145-5p mimic attenuated both kaempferide-induced melanogenesis and the accompanying reduction in thiol/GSH levels. CMap analysis further provided hypothesis-generating associations between kaempferide-responsive signatures and miR-145-associated regulatory networks. CONCLUSIONS: Kaempferide-induced melanogenesis is a GSH-dependent process with miR-145-associated regulation whereas ROS contributes partially and appears to act in a secondary manner.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta-Analyses.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to May 2, 2026. Randomized controlled trials and prospective comparative cohort studies evaluating systemic immunomodulatory or biologic therapies for NIU were included. The primary efficacy outcome was treatment failure. Safety outcomes included mortality, urinary tract infection, upper respiratory tract infection, injection-site reactions, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Random-effects pairwise meta-analysis and frequentist network meta-analysis were performed using risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Seven studies including 992 participants were included; six were randomized controlled trials and one was a prospective cohort. In the pairwise meta-analysis, adalimumab significantly reduced treatment failure compared with placebo (RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.58-0.78; p < 0.0001; I² = 28.1%). The mortality estimate was inconclusive (RR, 3.80; 95% CI, 0.42-34.15), with three deaths in the adalimumab groups and none in the placebo groups. Adalimumab was associated with a higher risk of injection-site reactions than placebo (RR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.73-4.12). Network meta-analysis showed no significant differences for most safety outcomes, including upper respiratory tract infection, ocular hypertension, macular edema, and headache. Infliximab showed an imprecise urinary tract infection signal versus placebo (RR, 40.98; 95% CI, 1.82-922.17), based on sparse events and one nonrandomized comparison. CONCLUSION: Adalimumab provides the most consistent evidence for reducing treatment failure in NIU. Comparative safety estimates, particularly for infliximab, remain uncertain and hypothesis-generating. Larger, long-term, head-to-head trials are required.

articles.title: Efsubaglutide Alfa: A Comprehensive Pharmacological Review.
articles.abstract: Efsubaglutide alfa (also known as supaglutide) is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) engineered as a GLP-1 analogue fused to a human immunoglobulin G2 (IgG2) fragment crystallisable (Fc) domain. This narrative review summarises published and publicly available evidence on efsubaglutide alfa pharmacology, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, dose-exposure-response relationships, drug-drug interaction potential, and clinical efficacy and safety in type 2 diabetes (T2D) and overweight/obesity. Efsubaglutide alfa has prolonged exposure (terminal half-life approximately 182-215 h) and low steady-state fluctuation, but dosing-interval selection should not be inferred from half-life alone. Available population pharmacokinetic and exposure-response analyses indicate that steady-state trough concentration is most informative for glycaemic response, whereas average and peak concentrations contribute to interpretation of weight response and gastrointestinal tolerability. Across available studies, predominantly conducted in Chinese populations, efsubaglutide alfa shows class-consistent improvements in glycaemic control and body weight, with gastrointestinal adverse events as the main tolerability limitation. Exploratory every 2-week dosing and post-discontinuation glycaemic durability findings remain hypothesis-generating. No head-to-head comparative trials dedicated cardiovascular or renal outcome trials, or large globally diverse datasets are yet available; therefore, the current evidence should be interpreted as a clinical pharmacology synthesis rather than a comparative positioning claim.

articles.title: Preclinical Evidence and Mechanisms of Icariin on Bone Health in Ovariectomized Rodent Models of Osteoporosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Osteoporosis, particularly postmenopausal osteoporosis, is a major global health concern, and current drugs often come with serious side effects. Herba Epimedii has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to strengthen bones. Icariin, its principal flavonoid, has shown osteoprotective potential in preclinical studies, yet a comprehensive evaluation of its efficacy remains lacking. AIM OF THE STUDY: To systematically evaluate the preclinical efficacy of icariin on bone density, microarchitecture, biomechanics, turnover markers, and its underlying mechanisms in ovariectomized (OVX) rodent models. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261366889). A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 16, 2026, to identify preclinical studies on icariin in OVX rodents. Effect sizes were pooled using random-effects models, and methodological quality was assessed using SYRCLE's Risk of Bias tool. RESULTS: Twenty-six studies (708 animals) were included. Icariin significantly increased femoral BMD (SMD = 1.91, 95% CI: 1.36-2.46) and lumbar spine BMD (SMD = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.80-1.63). Trabecular microarchitecture improved substantially, with increased BV/TV (SMD = 3.24), Tb.Th (SMD = 2.90), Tb.N (SMD = 2.53), and decreased Tb.Sp (SMD = -3.06), all P < 0.001. Biomechanical strength was enhanced (femur maximum load: SMD = 2.87, P = 0.002). Serum ALP (SMD = -1.55, P = 0.002), OCN (SMD = -2.87, P = 0.02), and CTX-I (SMD = -2.29, P < 0.001) were significantly reduced; TRACP-5b reduction was significant only at >100 mg/kg (SMD = -1.34, P < 0.001). Mechanistically, icariin modulates OPG/RANKL, Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, and Nrf2/HO-1 pathways. CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates that icariin effectively ameliorates OVX-induced bone loss in rodents, improving BMD, microarchitecture, biomechanics, and turnover markers through multiple pathways. These findings support icariin as a promising candidate for PMOP management, warranting clinical translation.

articles.title: Psychoneuroimmunology of Glioblastoma: How Emotional States Shape Tumor Biology.
articles.abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

articles.title: Conformational allocation of mitofusin 2 in neuronal mitochondrial dynamics: Mechanisms and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Neurons must sustain functional mitochondria far from the cell body. Mitofusin 2 (MFN2), a dynamin-like large guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase), coordinates outer mitochondrial membrane remodeling with axonal transport, bioenergetic support, inter-organelle communication, and stress-responsive quality control. Studying these activities separately obscures how disruption of one protein produces diverse neuronal phenotypes. We propose a testable conformational-allocation framework in which molecular state distributions and transition kinetics bias MFN2 participation across cellular outputs. Integrating structural and functional evidence, we distinguish experimentally resolved mechanisms from working models. Variants associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A (CMT2A) are compared by the molecular step or functional output affected. Fusion loss alone does not capture this mechanistic diversity. Structure-guided docking supports local compatibility at a shallow, conformationally conditional C-terminal surface, without establishing native accessibility, affinity, or therapeutic response. CMT2A provides the strongest context for intervention, combining causal genetics, direct mitofusin engagement studies, and multiscale rescue. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) provides secondary preclinical evidence, whereas Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases remain exploratory. The mitofusin pathway is chemically tractable, but paralog selectivity and state-dependent target engagement remain unresolved. A state- and variant-informed strategy may better match intervention to the affected output than indiscriminate enhancement of fusion.

articles.title: Antidepressants and Cognitive Function in Major Depressive Disorder: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Implications for Precision Treatment.
articles.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a core feature of major depressive disorder (MDD) and significantly impairs functional recovery. This review summarizes current evidence on the effects of antidepressants on cognitive function and discusses the underlying mechanisms. Antidepressants may exert their effects through multiple mechanisms, including modulation of monoaminergic neurotransmission, enhancement of neuroplasticity, and regulation of stress and inflammatory pathways. Available studies indicate that antidepressants differ in their cognitive benefits, with vortioxetine showing the most consistent procognitive evidence. Duloxetine, bupropion, and some augmentation strategies may also improve specific cognitive domains, though the evidence is limited. Importantly, cognitive improvement may result from direct drug effects on cognition or indirectly via alleviation of depressive symptoms, highlighting the need for mediation analyses in future research. In patients with late-life depression, vortioxetine and duloxetine have shown relatively clear benefits, and augmentation with cognitive enhancers has demonstrated some potential. The long-term cognitive protective effects of antidepressants remain unconfirmed. Immuno-metabolic depression subtypes, high-dose-related adverse effects, and comorbidity with anxiety and sleep disorders may constitute important sources of residual cognitive deficits. Emerging treatments such as ketamine, psychedelic compounds, and interventions targeting the gut-brain axis may offer new opportunities for addressing cognitive dysfunction in MDD. Current evidence is limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneous cognitive assessments. Future research should prioritize large, randomized controlled trials with cognition as the primary endpoint, using standardized assessment tools. A better understanding of the cognitive profiles and mechanisms of antidepressants may support precision medicine strategies and promote functional recovery in patients with MDD.

articles.title: Epigenetic insights into anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury: A systematic review of DNA methylation as a potential biomarker.
articles.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major clinical challenge that may cause acute liver failure, chronic liver disease, and treatment discontinuation. DNA methylation, a key epigenetic mechanism regulating gene expression, has emerged as a potential biomarker of DILI susceptibility; however, clinical evidence is largely confined to anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATDILI). This systematic review evaluated associations between DNA methylation patterns and DILI risk, with emphasis on ATDILI. Searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase identified eight eligible case-control studies published between 2014 and 2024. ATDILI-associated hypermethylation was reported in N-acetyltransferase-2 (NAT2), cytochrome P450 family-2 subfamily E member-1 (CYP2E1), cytochrome P450 family-2 subfamily D member-6 (CYP2D6), cytochrome P450 family-1 subfamily A member-1 (CYP1A1), glutathione S-transferase pi-1 (GSTP1), hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF1α), and 5-aminolevulinate synthase-1 (ALAS1). Global hypomethylation of repetitive elements, including LINE-1, SINE, and ALU, was also associated with increased ATDILI risk. Genome-wide analyses identified potential markers in tetratricopeptide repeat, ankyrin repeat, and coiled-coil containing-1 (TANC1), solute carrier family-8 member A-2 (SLC8A2), proline-serine-threonine phosphatase-interacting protein-2 (PSTPIP2), and adenylate kinase-2 (AK2). These findings support DNA methylation as a potential biomarker of ATDILI susceptibility and personalized risk assessment. However, because all evidence derives from case-control studies, causal and temporal relationships remain uncertain. Prospective longitudinal studies, epigenome-wide analyses, multi-omics integration, mechanistic validation, and large-scale replication are needed to confirm these associations and establish their predictive and clinical utility.

articles.title: Bioactive compounds from Perilla frutescens modulate multiple cell death pathways and signaling networks in cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Perilla frutescens, an edible medicinal plant from East Asia, produces diverse bioactive phytochemicals with anticancer activity, including perillaldehyde (PAH), rosmarinic acid (RA), luteolin, apigenin, and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA). These compounds exert multi-target anticancer effects through apoptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis. PAH triggers ferroptosis in gastric cancer via the System Xc-/GSH/GPX4 axis and P62-Keap1-Nrf2 pathway, while inducing protective autophagy in colorectal cancer through SRD5A1 and PI3K/AKT modulation. RA directly binds KRAS(G12C) and suppresses NSCLC via KRAS/AKT/ERK, and inhibits stress-induced TNBC metastasis through Src inactivation. Perilla leaf extracts activate Hippo-YAP/TAZ signaling in breast cancer. ALA-rich perilla seed oil (PSO) mitigates tumorigenesis in colitis-associated colorectal cancer models and restores gut microbial homeostasis. This review synthesizes current molecular evidence on perilla compounds in cancer therapy, focusing on apoptosis-autophagy-ferroptosis crosstalk. The multi-target characteristics position perilla-derived compounds as adjuvant cancer therapy candidates, though bioavailability and clinical translation still challenges remain.

articles.title: B7-H3-mediated immune regulation in cancer: biological functions and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: B7-H3 (CD276), a member of the B7 family of immunoregulatory ligands, has emerged as an important molecule at the intersection of tumor biology and cancer immunology. Although initially identified as a regulator of T-cell responses, accumulating evidence supports its predominantly immunosuppressive role. B7-H3 is highly expressed across diverse malignancies, including brain, prostate, lung, breast, colorectal, and pediatric cancers, while showing limited expression in most normal adult tissues. Its tumor-associated expression, including tumor vasculature, makes B7-H3 an attractive therapeutic target. Beyond immune regulation, B7-H3 promotes tumor progression through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms involving PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling, angiogenesis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, and metabolic reprogramming. Within the tumor microenvironment, B7-H3 suppresses T-cell and natural killer cell activity and promotes immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while its expression can be regulated by metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms. These multifaceted functions have stimulated the development of diverse B7-H3-targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR T-cell and Vδ1 T-cell therapies, nanobody-based platforms, and bispecific or trispecific immune cell engagers. Early clinical studies have demonstrated promising antitumor activity, although important challenges regarding efficacy, safety, tumor heterogeneity, and patient selection remain. In this review, we summarize the molecular regulation and biological functions of B7-H3, critically evaluate the current development of B7-H3-targeted therapies, and discuss key challenges and future directions for translating B7-H3-directed strategies into effective cancer treatments.

articles.title: Predictive biomarkers for precision treatment in rheumatoid arthritis: are we there yet?
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting approximately 1% of the global population and is associated with a substantial reduction in both life expectancy and quality of life. Although current treatments, primarily disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, have been shown to suppress inflammation, clinical responses vary widely between individuals, reflecting the heterogeneity of the disease. Consequently, identifying reliable biomarkers to predict therapeutic response has become a key priority for improving clinical management. In this focused review, we summarise recent advances in the discovery of predictive biomarkers for RA and compare their reported specificity and sensitivity using published data. We also highlight key limitations in the existing literature that undermine reproducibility in this field. Coordinated efforts across the rheumatology community to address these challenges will be essential to translate biomarker research into personalised treatment strategies for RA.

articles.title: Integrated counter current separation and omics approaches for discovery of bioactive compounds from medicinal plants.
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants provide an important source of structurally varied bioactive metabolites with medicinal potential; however, their effective extraction, characterization, and standardization present considerable analytical challenges. Counter-current separation (CCS) methods, such as centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) and high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC), represent advanced liquid-liquid chromatographic approaches that minimize irreversible adsorption of samples. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar using pre-defined search terms related to counter-current separation, six omics domains, artificial intelligence/machine learning, molecular networking, network pharmacology, regulatory systems, and industrial translation. We screened relevant studies using pre-defined eligibility criteria and thematically synthesized them according to methodological development, analytical integration, evidence maturity, regulatory relevance, and translational potential. These methods enable the effective purification of bioactive natural compounds, ensuring high recovery rates. Simultaneously, the development of metabolomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, genomics, lipidomics, and glycomics has significantly advanced the research on natural products, enabling detailed molecular profiling and systems-level biological interpretation. This review critically considers the use of CCS in combination with multi-omics technologies for the discovery of bioactive compounds from medicinal plants. Special attention is paid to solvent-system design, AI-aided process optimization, molecular networking, chemometric analysis, and bioactivity-guided fractionation strategies. In addition, the use of CCS in quality control, phytopharmaceutical standardization, and industrial-scale production is discussed. Integration of CCS with omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and network-based analytical approaches offers a complementary platform for the enhancement of the discovery, prioritization, isolation, and characterization of bioactive natural products. These integrated workflows can facilitate candidate identification, structural characterization, mechanistic investigation and biological validation in early translational research. However, it should be kept in mind that the identification of a bioactive compound or fraction is not the same as drug discovery or therapeutic development. Further pharmacological, toxicological, pharmacokinetic, manufacturing, regulatory and clinical investigations are required for a purified natural product or botanical preparation to advance toward therapeutic development.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-based nanoformulations for cancer therapy: antitumor mechanisms, challenges, and future directions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-derived compounds have anticancer potential because of their multi-component, multi-target actions and generally favorable toxicity profiles. Clinical translation, however, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic metabolism, and insufficient tumor-selective delivery. This review critically evaluates recent TCM-based nanoformulations developed to address these limitations and improve the therapeutic performance. METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and EQUATOR guidance, PubMed and Web of Science databases were searched for original studies published during the previous 5 years using terms including "TCM," "nanoformulation," and "anticancer." After screening 387 records, 81 studies covering 50 representative TCM compounds were included and assessed for the preparation methods, antitumor mechanisms, and translational barriers. RESULTS: Relative to free compounds, nanoformulations frequently improved solubility, stability, apparent bioavailability, or the targeting efficiency of TCM constituents.
