Reported mechanisms included apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, ferroptosis, immunogenic cell death, and tumor-microenvironment remodeling across breast, lung, colorectal, and other cancer models. Nevertheless, most evidence was derived from in vitro experiments or small animal studies, and direct cross-study comparison was limited by heterogeneous formulations, doses, models, and endpoints. CONCLUSION: TCM-based nanoformulations represent a promising strategy for integrating traditional herbal medicine with modern cancer therapy. Despite these promising findings, substantial challenges remain in standardization, reproducibility, pharmacokinetics, long-term safety, manufacturing, and clinical validation. Future studies should prioritize head-to-head comparisons, quantitative biodistribution, clinically relevant models, and scalable manufacturing.

articles.title: Microbiota-based PBPK model: new approach methodology for assessing the kinetics of drugs and chemicals.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota plays an important role in metabolising environmental chemicals and drugs. It affects the susceptibility of the host to toxicity by modifying metabolism, which can be captured by in-vitro assays and translated using in silico models. In-silico models like physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models can predict the concentration-time profile of compounds across different tissues and organs. Despite the recognized importance of gut microbiota in shaping absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) profiles for a wide range of compounds, PBPK models do not include gut microbiota either due to the unavailability of data or to reduce model complexity. This inclusion becomes of utmost importance when metabolism by gut microbiota shape the ADME profile. In this review, we outline the key strategies and considerations for integrating gut microbiota into PBPK models as part of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), covering the essential equations, parameterization approaches, and in-vitro-to-in-vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) methods required for model development and validation. We also focus on the limitations of the IVIVE methodologies including population-level variability modelling, and the emerging application of machine learning for microbial parameter inference. We further discuss extended compartmentalization, as well as the integration of genome-scale metabolic (GSM) network models to capture microbial pathway diversity. The review also highlights the broad applications of microbiota-based PBPK models, including personalized medicine, translational modelling, compound-microbiota interactions, and the compound-microbiota-diet axis. Additionally, we examine the current regulatory landscape, identifying existing gaps in PBPK guidelines with respect to microbial metabolism, and propose directions for developing harmonized reporting frameworks. Finally, we discuss future directions including multi-omics integration, bidirectional gut-liver signalling. Together, this review provides a practical roadmap for building microbiota-informed PBPK models that improve kinetic predictions and advance personalized risk assessment.

articles.title: Lactylation in liver fibrosis: from molecular mechanisms to targeted therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) represent central driving events in liver fibrosis. Lactylation, a lactate-mediated post-translational modification (PTM), is proposed to converge on histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18La) through the HK2-KAT8 positive feedback loop, the IGF2BP2-N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-aldolase A (ALDOA) cascade, and the HKDC1-ORMDL3 pathway, potentially driving pro-fibrotic transcriptional programs in a synergistic manner. H3K18La does not operate in isolation; its site-specific competition with acetylation, cascade amplification with m6A methylation, cooperation with G9a/DNMT1-mediated methylation, and antagonism with ubiquitination form a PTM interaction network. Therapeutically, interventions targeting lactate-metabolizing enzymes (HK2, LDH), lactylation writers (KAT8), and specific lactylation sites (PGK1-K353 interfering peptides) have demonstrated anti-fibrotic potential in preclinical models. Natural products including curcumol, limonin, and salidroside exhibit multi-target regulatory advantages. Muscle-derived SORBS3 lactylation-mediated trans-organ signaling and lactylation gene-based molecular subtyping expand the systemic dimensions of lactylation. This narrative review proposes a working hypothesis positioning H3K18La as a metabolic-epigenetic convergence node and outlines future directions including site-specific interventions, cell type-resolved lactylomics, and molecular subtyping-driven clinical trials, providing an integrated framework from basic research to translational applications for liver fibrosis.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into the potential role of botanical drugs and plant-derived metabolites in mitigating oxidative stress in varicocele.
articles.abstract: Varicocele (VC) is a prevalent male urogenital disorder associated with scrotal discomfort, impaired semen quality, and endocrine dysregulation, in which oxidative stress (OS) is repeatedly implicated as a key pathogenic axis linking venous stasis, hypoxia, hyperthermia, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and germ-cell injury. This review critically evaluates experimental and clinical evidence on defined botanical drugs and plant-derived metabolites investigated in VC or VC-relevant OS models, with an emphasis on mechanistic plausibility and translational limitations. Across in vivo VC models, toxin-/heat-/hypoxia-induced spermatogenic injury models, and selected clinical studies, multiple interventions have been reported to improve semen parameters, testicular histology, and redox indices (e.g., ROS, MDA, SOD/CAT/GPx, GSH/GSSG), alongside modulation of apoptosis and stress responses. Reported molecular nodes converge on redox- and stress-responsive pathways, including Keap1-Nrf2-ARE/HO-1, PI3K-Akt, MAPK/JNK-p38, HIF-1-related signaling, ER-stress responses, mitochondrial apoptosis (e.g., Bax/Bcl-2/caspases), and, in some models, ferroptosis-related regulation. However, the overall evidence base is constrained by heterogeneity in models and endpoints, limited extract/compound chemical characterization and pharmacological standardization, frequent reliance on in silico predictions, small or non-randomized clinical cohorts, and incomplete reporting of taxonomic and product quality details. Future work should prioritize rigorously designed, adequately powered clinical trials with standardized outcomes, well-defined interventions, and mechanism-aligned biomarkers to clarify which botanical drugs/metabolites offer clinically meaningful benefit as adjuncts in VC management.

articles.title: Revolutionizing transdermal drug delivery evaluation: the evolution from traditional models to skin organoids and the integration of artificial intelligence.
articles.abstract: This review examines the evolution of evaluation systems for transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) alongside recent advances in skin organoids (SkOs). We discuss the potential of SkOs as in vitro models, with particular attention to their structural complexity and their ability to recapitulate appendage-associated transport pathways more effectively than traditional animal models and reconstructed human epidermis (RHE). We also summarize current fabrication strategies, physiological validation, and the main translational limitations of SkOs. In addition, we discuss how artificial intelligence (AI), computer vision, and digital twin technologies may help address current challenges in standardization and quality control. Self-assembling SkOs derived from induced pluripotent stem cells represent a promising candidate advance for future TDDS evaluation. Although limitations in maturation remain, the integration of SkOs with AI may support the development of a more standardized, high-throughput, and predictive platform for transdermal drug delivery research.

articles.title: The ameliorative effect of active ingredients of traditional Chinese medicine on male reproductive injury: A review.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Due to their unique advantages of multi-target synergy and holistic regulation, traditional Chinese medicines (TCM) show promising clinical applications in enhancing male reproductive function. The 'Qianjin Fang' and 'Compendium of Materia Medica' document the use of Wuzhi Yanzong Wan, Cistanche, Cuscuta, and Epimedium for over a thousand years in the preservation of male reproductive health. AIM OF THIS REVIEW: This article provides a systematic review of research progress on the use of active components in TCM (including flavonoids, polyphenols, terpenoids, alkaloids, and polysaccharides) and related formulas in improving male reproductive damage. These compounds improve male fertility by regulating multiple signaling pathways. Furthermore, this review outlines future research directions and potential applications in this field, aiming to lay a theoretical foundation for the clinical treatment of male reproductive health using TCM and the development of novel therapeutic interventions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The relevant literature on the effects of active ingredients in TCM and related formulas on improving male reproductive damage was retrieved from multiple databases, including Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PubMed, etc. RESULTS: Active components of TCM (such as icariin, hypericin, and quercetin) and their compound formulations (such as Guilu Erxian Jiao and Wuziyan Zongwan) can improve male reproductive damage by modulating core pathological cascades-including oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and endocrine disruption-and restoring the physiological microenvironment essential for normal spermatogenesis. CONCLUSION: Extensive experiments have been performed to investigate the effects of active ingredients and herbal formulas on improving male reproductive dysfunction, revealing that TCM has the potential to combat male reproductive dysfunction through multi-level, multi-target mechanisms. However, there is a lack of reviews addressing the causes of male reproductive dysfunction and related treatment approaches. Therefore, this review aims to summarize current research progress in the use of TCM to combat male reproductive dysfunction, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for future preclinical validation and clinical application in the treatment of male reproductive dysfunction.

articles.title: Protein degraders targeting JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway are emerging therapeutic modalities for human cancers.
articles.abstract: JAK/Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling axis plays an important role in tumor progress. Several JAK/STAT3 inhibitors have entered into clinical trials. However, development of JAK/STAT3 inhibitors faces multiple challenges including low selectivity. Targeted protein degradation (TPD) emerges as a distinct therapeutic modality that holds promise for depleting pathogenic "undruggable" proteins. Proteolysis‑targeting chimera (PROTAC) degraders are a key family of molecules designed to mediate the selective degradation of target proteins. Currently, JAK/STAT3 degraders represent a promising strategy to inhibit JAK/STAT3 signaling. Although there were occasional reports on the development of JAK/STAT3 degraders in recent years, a comprehensive review on the recent progresses of the degraders targeting the whole JAK/STAT3 pathway is missing. Here, we systematically summarized the most recent advances of this field. Specifically, we first introduced the components of JAK/STAT3 pathway and its role in tumorigenesis. We also discussed various aspects of PROTACs including its principle, classification and advantages over small-molecule inhibitor. Then, we focused on the most recent progress of protein degraders targeting JAK/STAT3 pathway, including the degraders of the upstream SHP2, BCR-ABL1 and c-SRC s, JAK degraders, STAT3 degraders (including PROTACs and small-molecule natural products) and the downstream c-Myc degraders, Cyclin D1 degraders, MMP9 degraders, VEGF degraders, and protein degraders of BCL2, BCL-XL and MCL-1. Lastly, we discussed potential opportunities and challenges in the development of JAK/STAT3 degraders. We hope this review will provide theoretical basis for future drug design of novel JAK/STAT3 degraders.

articles.title: Role of the RAGE signaling pathway in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: The receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE), a multi-ligand receptor of the immunoglobulin superfamily, plays a pivotal regulatory role in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. This review summarizes the regulatory mechanisms governing RAGE expression; the dynamic alterations of its major ligands-advanced glycation end products (AGEs), high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), and the S100 protein family-during myocardial I/R; and the multifaceted pathological mechanisms by which RAGE-mediated downstream signaling pathways, including activation of the MAPK and JAK/STAT cascades and suppression of the pro-survival PI3K/AKT pathway, exacerbate myocardial injury in the setting of I/R. Furthermore, this review synthesizes RAGE-targeted therapeutic strategies, such as small-molecule inhibitors and soluble RAGE (sRAGE), and discusses their prospects for clinical translation, thereby providing a theoretical framework for myocardial protection strategies centered on the RAGE signaling pathway.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Target-Specific RNA-Based Lipid-Lowering Therapies: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: RNA-based therapies target distinct pathways involved in lipid metabolism and may therefore exhibit differential pharmacological effects according to their molecular targets. However, comparative evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of these target-specific therapies remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of PCSK9-, APOC3-, and ANGPTL3-targeting RNA-based therapies in patients with hyperlipidemia or hypertriglyceridemia. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing inclisiran, olezarsen, plozasiran, or zodasiran with placebo. Treatment effects were expressed as mean differences (MDs) or risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and pooled analyses were stratified according to molecular target. Sixteen randomized controlled trials involving 6,982 participants were included. PCSK9-targeting therapy produced the greatest reductions in LDL-C (MD -53.01 mg/dL, 95% CI -57.56 to -48.45), ApoB (MD -39.59 mg/dL, 95% CI -43.33 to -35.85), and non-HDL-C (MD -44.62 mg/dL, 95% CI -47.73 to -41.51), whereas APOC3-targeting therapies produced the greatest reduction in triglycerides (MD -52.26 mg/dL, 95% CI -56.50 to -48.02). Total adverse events, serious adverse events, and adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were comparable between RNA-based therapies and placebo. Overall, these findings indicate that RNA-based lipid-lowering therapies exhibit target-specific pharmacological effects, with PCSK9 inhibition predominantly reducing atherogenic lipoproteins and APOC3 inhibition producing greater triglyceride lowering. Although the overall safety profile was comparable with placebo, differences in individual adverse outcomes and the limited availability of long-term clinical outcome data highlights the need for further investigation.

articles.title: Lactylation as a potential epigenetic and metabolic modulator of cuproptosis in health and disease: Current evidence and hypotheses.
articles.abstract: As a lactate-derived post-translational modification, lactylation plays a vital role in connecting cellular glycolysis with the regulation of cuproptosis, a unique form of cell death triggered by copper overload. The article explores the growing relationship between lactylation and cuproptosis, highlighting the potential for lactate metabolism to influence cellular responses to copper toxicity. We further discuss the potential roles of lactylation writers, erasers and readers in modulating key cuproptosis-related proteins, such as FDX1, DLAT and CTR1, through the specific actions of molecular players including METTL16, NAT10, and NUDT21 across transcriptional regulation, alternative polyadenylation (APA), and m6A modification pathways. Further analysis of the lactate paradox involves exploring the roles lactate plays in various tumor microenvironments and disease contexts. Clinically, this proposed metabolic-epigenetic interplay could be targeted with lactate metabolism inhibitors or copper ionophores to potentially provide synergistic therapeutic strategies for cancer and metabolic diseases. This metabolic-epigenetic interplay could shed light on disease progression and open up new possibilities for precision medical approaches.

articles.title: Shisanwei Qinglan Powder attenuates ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury in association with reduced NF-κB signalling and caspase activation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Shisanwei Qinglan Powder (SQP) is a marketed Tibetan medicinal formula traditionally used for gastrointestinal disorders associated with "peigen mubu", including epigastric distension and pain, gastritis, and ulcer-related symptoms. However, experimental evidence for the complete formula, its systemically exposed constituents, and the mechanisms underlying gastric mucosal protection remains limited. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to characterise the serum-associated constituents of SQP and evaluate its protective effects and molecular responses in acute ethanol-induced gastric mucosal injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Chemical profiling and serum pharmacochemistry were performed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Network pharmacology and gastric-tissue transcriptomics were integrated to prioritise treatment-associated pathways. Pharmacological effects were evaluated in mice receiving SQP prophylactically before anhydrous ethanol challenge and in GES-1 cells receiving SQP after ethanol-induced injury, using viability, migration, apoptosis, macroscopic lesion, histological, oxidative-stress, and inflammatory measurements. The IKKβ/IκBα/NF-κB axis and caspase-8/caspase-3 activation were assessed by immunohistochemistry and western blotting. Selected compound-target pairs were further evaluated by molecular docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations. RESULTS: Thirty-two distinct serum-associated constituents were tentatively identified, and 185 targets were shared between SQP- and gastric ulcer-related datasets. Under the post-injury cell-intervention paradigm, SQP improved viability and migration, corrected oxidative and cytokine imbalances, and reduced total apoptosis from approximately 21.9% to 7.9% at 20 μg/mL. Under the prophylactic animal paradigm, SQP alleviated haemorrhage, erosion, and glandular disruption, and 0.52 g/kg significantly reduced both the ulcer index and damaged area. RNA sequencing identified 1,533 differentially expressed genes between the high-dose SQP and model groups, with enrichment in TNF, NF-κB and apoptosis-related pathways. In both models, SQP reduced phosphorylation of IKKβ, IκBα and NF-κB p65, suppressed caspase-8 and caspase-3 cleavage, and decreased gastric TUNEL positivity. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used for computational prioritization of the TNF-bicuculline and CASP3-kaempferol pairs; these analyses indicated structural feasibility under the simulated conditions but did not establish direct binding or target engagement. CONCLUSION: SQP showed prophylactic gastroprote ctive effects in mice and post-injury protective and reparative effects in ethanol-injured GES-1 cells. Across these distinct experimental paradigms, the observed effects were associated with attenuation of oxidative stress, IKK/NF-κB-related inflammation, and caspase-8/caspase-3-associated apoptotic responses.

articles.title: Tibetan medicine Anzhi Jinghua San alleviates chronic atrophic gastritis: attenuation of LysoPC-induced Bcl-2 suppression and inhibition of pyroptosis and apoptosis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Anzhi Jinghua San (AZJHS), a traditional Tibetan medicine formula officially recorded in the Drug Standards of the Ministry of Health of the People's Republic of China (Tibetan Medicine, Volume 1, 1995 edition), has shown clinical efficacy against chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG), but its molecular mechanism needs further exploration. AIM OF THE STUDY: To decipher the therapeutic compounds and mechanisms of AZJHS against CAG using an integrative multi-omics approach. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A CAG rat model was induced by N-methyl-N'-nitro-N-nitrosoguanidine (MNNG), irregular feeding, ranitidine, and sodium salicylate, followed by AZJHS treatment for four weeks. Serum gastric function markers, inflammatory cytokines, gastric mucosal histopathology, ultrastructure, and apoptosis and proliferation were evaluated. Serum pharmacochemistry, network pharmacology, proteomics, and metabolomics were integrated to identify absorbed components, key targets, and differential metabolites. Candidate targets were validated in gastric tissues by western blotting and RT-qPCR. Component-target binding was assessed by molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), microscale thermophoresis (MST), and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). Cytoprotective effects and underlying mechanisms were further examined in MNNG-exposed GES-1 cells. RESULTS: AZJHS treatment increased serum pepsinogen I (PG I) and pepsinogen II (PG II), decreased gastrin-17 (GAS-17), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and interleukin-6 (IL-6), alleviated histopathological and ultrastructural damage, and restored the proliferation-apoptosis balance. Multi-omics analysis identified Bcl-2 as a candidate target within the NOD-like receptor signaling pathway. AZJHS restored Bcl-2 expression, suppressed the NLRP1/Caspase-1/gasdermin D (GSDMD)/interleukin-18 (IL-18)/interleukin-1β (IL-1β) pyroptotic cascade, and attenuated mitochondrial apoptosis (Bax/Caspase-9/Caspase-3). Metabolomic profiling revealed that AZJHS reversed the glycerophospholipid disturbances associated with CAG, notably reducing lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC), and Spearman analysis identified LysoPC 18:1 as the metabolite most negatively correlated with Bcl-2. Apigenin was identified as an active constituent of AZJHS that directly binds Bcl-2 by molecular docking, SPR, MST, and CETSA. In MNNG-exposed GES-1 cells, apigenin reduced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-18, IL-1β, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels, upregulated Bcl-2, suppressed downstream pyroptotic and apoptotic pathways, and reversed LysoPC 18:1-induced Bcl-2 downregulation and activation of these pathways. CONCLUSION: AZJHS ameliorates CAG, with restoration of glycerophospholipid homeostasis, upregulation of Bcl-2, and suppression of NLRP1-mediated pyroptosis and mitochondrial apoptosis. Apigenin, a bioactive component of AZJHS, directly binds Bcl-2 and attenuates LysoPC-induced Bcl-2 suppression. These findings suggest that the metabolism-inflammation-cell death axis may be a therapeutic target for CAG in Tibetan medicine.

articles.title: Artemisia vulgaris and sabinene ameliorate gastric ulceration and its recurrence through modulation of acid secretion, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cytokines: an in vivo and in silico study.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL IMPORTANCE: Artemisia vulgaris L., popularly known as mugwort, is traditionally used to treat gastric disturbances, yet the mechanistic basis of its antiulcer effects is largely unexplored. AIM OF THE STUDY: The study evaluated the gastroprotective, healing, and anti-recurrence effects of the hydroalcoholic extract of A. vulgaris (HEAv) and its constituent sabinene, and their underlying pharmacological mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Phytochemical analysis of HEAv used LC-MS, LC-MS/MS, and LC-ESI-IT-MSn. Gastroprotective activity of HEAv (3, 10, or 30 mg/kg) and sabinene (3 mg/kg) was assessed in ethanol- and piroxicam-induced ulcers, beyond pyloric ligation. Healing and recurrence were assessed via acetic acid-induced and IL-1β-triggered ulcers, the latter monitored by ultrasonography. Oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, histology, network pharmacology, and molecular docking/dynamics were evaluated, along with acute toxicity in mice. RESULTS: Chemical analysis identified 36 compounds in HEAv, predominantly phenolics and flavonoids. HEAv and sabinene showed gastroprotective effects, corroborated by mucosal protection and modulation of oxidative stress and inflammatory parameters. In addition, HEAv increased gastric pH, compared to omeprazole. Moreover, HEAv and sabinene reduced ulceration in both the healing and recurrence models, accompanied by increased GSH and CAT activity, and reduced LPO, MPO, and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and IL-17A). No acute toxicity was observed. Network pharmacology identified inflammatory signaling as a key target of HEAv constituents, and docking and dynamic molecular assays confirmed favorable, stable interactions between phenolic compounds and sabinene with H+/K+-ATPase and IKKβ, supported by favorable MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA binding energies. CONCLUSION: HEAv and sabinene exert gastroprotective and healing effects by modulating acid secretion, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cytokines, as suggested by in silico analyses. Nonetheless, further studies are warranted to validate the predicted molecular targets and to elucidate additional pharmacological pathways.

articles.title: hnRNPU regulates the sorting of exo-miR-125a-5p in colon epithelial cells and its role in realgar-induced central nervous system toxicity.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Elucidating the mechanisms underlying realgar-induced toxicity is essential for the early prevention and treatment of arsenic-related adverse effects and for reducing the associated healthcare burden. AIM OF STUDY: Owing to its poor solubility, realgar preferentially accumulates in the intestine after oral administration. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which realgar regulates exosomal miR-125a-5p (exo-miR-125a-5p) sorting in colonic epithelial cells and to investigate the role of exo-miR-125a-5p in realgar-induced central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A chronic realgar-exposed mouse model was established and combined with AAV9-mediated hnRNPU knockdown, miR-125a-5p-enriched exosome administration, and probiotic intervention. Complementary in vitro studies were performed using YAMC cells subjected to hnRNPU silencing or co-treatment with realgar and L-cysteine sulfinic acid (LCSA). Small RNA sequencing, 16S rDNA sequencing, quantitative proteomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), miRNA pull-down, fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), Western blotting, and other molecular biological approaches were integrated to systematically investigate the molecular mechanism underlying realgar-regulated exo-miR-125a-5p sorting in colonic epithelial cells and its contribution to realgar-induced CNS toxicity. RESULTS: Realgar exposure induced dose-dependent colonic injury, altered the exosomal miRNA profile of colonic epithelial cells, and significantly reduced the secretion of exo-miR-125a-5p. Mechanistically, the RNA-binding protein hnRNPU directly bound mature miR-125a-5p, enhanced its post-transcriptional stability, and promoted its nuclear retention, thereby limiting its loading into exosomes. Realgar-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis reduced the abundance of Lactobacillus and the level of its metabolite, LCSA, resulting in aberrant upregulation of hnRNPU. The consequent reduction in circulating exo-miR-125a-5p relieved repression of the STAT1 signaling pathway, leading to activation of the microglial STAT1-NLRP3 inflammasome axis and exacerbation of realgar-induced CNS toxicity. CONCLUSION: Realgar induces both colonic and central nervous system toxicity. Mechanistically, realgar disrupts gut microbial homeostasis, depleting Lactobacillus-derived LCSA, which promotes hnRNPU expression and enhances the nuclear retention of mature miR-125a-5p. This process suppresses miR-125a-5p sorting into exosomes, reduces circulating exo-miR-125a-5p levels, and consequently activates the microglial STAT1-NLRP3 inflammasome pathway, thereby aggravating CNS toxicity. These findings identify a previously unrecognized gut microbiota-metabolite-RNA-binding protein axis governing exosomal miRNA sorting and establish exo-miR-125a-5p as a critical mediator linking intestinal injury to neuroinflammation. This study provides new mechanistic insights into realgar-induced colonic and CNS toxicity and expands our understanding of gut-brain axis-mediated toxicological mechanisms.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory and Early Osteogenic Potential of a 96% Ethanol Extract of Drynaria bonii.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Drynaria bonii H. Christ rhizome is traditionally used in Vietnamese medicine for fractures and musculoskeletal disorders. However, the effects of extraction solvent on chemical composition and biological activities relevant to the inflammatory and early mineralization phases of bone repair remain insufficiently defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study compared 30%, 70%, and 96% ethanol extracts of D. bonii (DB30, DB70, and DB96, respectively) to identify a lead extract for further fracture-healing-oriented investigation. METHODS: Rhizome extracts prepared with 30%, 70%, and 96% ethanol were profiled by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-QTOF-MS/MS). TNF-α inhibition was evaluated in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages; acute anti-inflammatory activity was assessed in carrageenan-induced mouse paw edema; and calcium-associated staining was evaluated in canine mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) cultures using Alizarin Red S (ARS). Acute oral toxicity was assessed at 5000 mg/kg, and selected constituents were isolated from DB96. The four NMR-characterized constituents were subsequently evaluated by molecular docking against IκB kinase β (IKKβ). RESULTS: The extracts showed distinct qualitative LC-MS/MS profiles, with DB70 displaying a broader curated phenolic/flavonoid profile and DB96 showing a different compositional pattern. DB96 produced the strongest TNF-α inhibition (IC50 = 32.05 μg/mL), compared with DB70 (63.73 μg/mL), whereas DB30 did not reach 50% inhibition at 100 μg/mL. DB96 also showed the largest numerical paw-edema inhibition among the extract groups at 1 and 24 h; however, statistical comparisons were performed only against the disease-control group and not among active treatment groups. In canine MSC cultures, DB96 at 50 μg/mL showed the highest descriptive normalized ARS-positive area among the extracts (12.0 ± 2.1%), although staining remained weak relative to the positive control and did not establish complete osteogenic differentiation. Betulin, ursolic acid, rutin, and kaempferol were isolated from DB96 and independently identified by NMR from a preparative DB96 batch. Among these constituents, ursolic acid and betulin showed the most favorable predicted IKKβ docking profiles, with binding energies of -8.52 and -8.41 kcal/mol, respectively. No mortality or overt acute toxicity was observed for any of the three extracts after a single oral dose of 5000 mg/kg. CONCLUSION: The findings support DB96 as the lead extract among the three preparations for subsequent mechanistic and bone-repair-oriented investigation. Docking provided complementary mechanistic support for possible interactions of selected DB96 constituents with IKKβ, but did not establish direct target inhibition. Direct fracture-healing efficacy, definitive osteogenic differentiation, quantitative constituent enrichment, and repeated-dose safety remain to be established.

articles.title: ShenqiYichang decoction enhances colorectal cancer immune efficacy via IDO1 mediated reduction of Treg infiltration.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: ShenqiYichang decoction (SQYCD) is a traditional Chinese formula indicated for colorectal cancer (CRC). Studies have shown that SQYCD potentiates antitumor immunity and enhances the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of SQYCD in enhancing ICIs efficacy against microsatellite stability (MSS) CRC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An in vivo CT26 tumor-bearing mouse model was established. The antitumor efficacy of SQYCD alone and in combination with ICIs was evaluated, and Treg infiltration was detected by immunofluorescence. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics were used to screen potential targets of SQYCD for MSS CRC. In vitro, MSS CRC cell lines were used for CCK-8 to assess cell proliferation. A CT26-Treg co-culture system was used to analyze Treg proportion by flow cytometry. Western blot, qRT-PCR, ELISA, and Co-IP assays were used to assess the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT axis and IDO1-PI3K interactions. UPLC-Q-TOF/MS and molecular docking were subsequently employed to identify the key absorbed components involved in the IDO1-PI3K pathway regulated by SQYCD. RESULTS: In vivo, SQYCD alone did not affect the proliferation of MSS CRC cells but inhibited Treg infiltration. When combined with ICIs, SQYCD enhanced the efficacy of ICIs, significantly inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and further reducing Treg infiltration. Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis suggested IDO1 as a potential target of SQYCD in MSS CRC. In vitro, SQYCD-containing serum did not reduce MSS CRC cell proliferation but decreased Treg proportion in the CT26-Treg co-culture system. SQYCD also promoted IL-2 levels while downregulating IL-10 and TGF-β levels. Mechanistically, SQYCD suppressed the IDO1/Kyn pathway and p-AKT expression. Additionally, components of SQYCD significantly reduced the IDO1-PI3K interaction. LC-MS and molecular docking results suggested that esculetin, glycitin, and hydroxygenkwanin may be the active components of SQYCD that reduce the IDO1-PI3K interaction. CONCLUSION: SQYCD reduces Treg infiltration by inhibiting both the IDO1/Kyn/p-AKT and the IDO1-PI3K interaction, consequently enhancing the efficacy of ICIs.

articles.title: Maternal cannabis use during pregnancy associates with alterations in placental endocannabinoid- and steroid-homeostasis and morphology.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal cannabis use associates with adverse pregnancy outcomes including preeclampsia. Human data on cannabis-associated disruption of the placental endocannabinoid system (ECS) are lacking. METHODS: We studied placentas from women with frequent cannabis use throughout pregnancy and non-exposed controls. Ex vivo dual-sided cotyledon perfusion was used to assess maternal and fetal release of cannabinoids, ECS-related lipid mediators, prostaglandins, and steroids by LC-ESI-MS/MS. Placental gene expression was quantified by RT-qPCR and placental histopathology was compared in cannabis users, non-smoking controls and tobacco-exposed pregnancies. RESULTS: The major cannabis-component Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) was detectable in placental tissue and released maternally and fetally. Cannabis use was associated with altered placental release of ECS-related lipids, including enhanced fetal release of N-acylethanolamines and loss of normal maternal-fetal release polarity for several lipid mediators. Cannabis-exposed placentas showed lower tissue concentrations of cortisone, membrane phospholipids, and selected mono- and diglycerides, suggesting reduced substrate availability for endogenous ECS lipid generation. Maternal cortisol release was increased, while HSD3B1 expression was upregulated without corresponding increases in progesterone content. Histopathological analyses showed reduced placental weight, umbilical cord length, and maximal placental diameter, with increased marginal or peripheral cord insertion, accelerated maturation, ischemia, and chorioamnionitis in cannabis-exposed placentas. CONCLUSIONS: Cannabis use during pregnancy is associated with placental accumulation and fetal-side release of THC, altered ECS-related lipid signaling, disturbed steroid profiles, and placental structural abnormalities. These findings may help explain previously reported associations between prenatal cannabis exposure and placental dysfunction and warn against cannabis use during pregnancy.

articles.title: Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone Increases Dorsal Premammillary Nucleus Neuron Activity and Darting Behavior.
articles.abstract: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is classically recognized for its role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis; however, it also functions as a central neuromodulator influencing arousal, locomotion, and autonomic processes. Despite these established roles, the circuit-level mechanisms through which TRH modulates behavior remain poorly defined. The dorsal premammillary nucleus (PMd) is a hypothalamic structure implicated in high-imminence defensive states, yet whether TRH directly engages PMd circuits is unknown. Here, we assessed the role of TRH as a modulator of PMd neuronal activity and behavioral output using in situ hybridization, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays in male and female mice. TRHR mRNA was co-localized with a subset of PMd CCK-positive neurons. TRH increased firing rate in a subset of PMd neurons in brain slices, revealing functional activation of a subset of the population. This finding was corroborated by calcium imaging that showed increased activity following TRH exposure. In vivo, intrahypothalamic administration of TRH produced darting and behavioral effects. Together, these findings identify a subpopulation of PMd neurons that serve as a functional hypothalamic target of TRH signaling associated with rapid locomotor behavioral output.

articles.title: Expression of Concern: In Vivo/In vitro metabolic profiling and evaluation of key metabolites of QO-83, a novel KCNQ channel opener with antiepileptic potential [Biochemical Pharmacology 242 (2025) 117381].
Cellular level investigation of skin permeation using stimulated Raman scattering microscopy and in-silico modelling.
articles.abstract: This study presents a novel approach combining stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy with mechanistic modelling to quantify the disposition and permeation of topically applied compounds in skin. The dermal delivery of 4-cyanophenol and caffeine was investigated using SRS microscopy, generating high-resolution images resolving their distribution within the stratum corneum (SC) lipid matrix and corneocytes. The imaging data revealed distinct permeation pathways, with 4-cyanophenol preferentially localising within the intercellular lipid matrix and caffeine within the corneocyte-rich regions. Depth-resolved SRS imaging provided concentration profiles across the SC, showing a monotonic decrease in 4-cyanophenol concentration, whereas caffeine exhibited depth-dependent transport behaviour. These experimental concentration profiles were modelled using a two-dimensional mechanistic model with calibration to reveal the diffusion, partition and deposition behaviour within the lipid and corneocyte domains. For 4-cyanophenol, the optimised permeability was consistent with literature-reported values and baseline model predictions, while for caffeine, optimisation substantially improved permeability predictions. Simulations further captured formulation-dependent effects predicting 1.3-fold and 1.5-fold increases in SC uptake of 4-cyanophenol and caffeine, respectively, in propylene glycol relative to aqueous vehicles. Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of combining SRS microscopy with inverse mechanistic modelling to derive transport parameters directly from skin imaging data and reveal dermal drug disposition and permeation. To our knowledge, this represents the first application of SRS-derived depth profiles to inform mechanistic modelling of skin permeation.

articles.title: 3D printing of a microfluidic chip-generated liposome-loaded hydrogel scaffold for accelerated wound closure and reduced fibrotic remodeling in burn wounds: an in vivo study.
articles.abstract: Growth factor-based therapies for burn wound healing are limited by rapid clearance, poor bioavailability, and inadequate efficacy of single agents. Here, we report a 3D printed chitosan hydrogel scaffold loaded with PEGylated liposomes encapsulating TGF-β3 and cationic lipoplexes carrying miR-132 mimic for localized co-delivery. The optimized formulation exhibited favorable printability and rheological properties, and liposome incorporation modulated swelling, accelerated degradation, and altered the tensile profile while maintaining scaffold structural integrity, as confirmed by SEM, DSC, and FTIR. Release studies, based on total analytically quantified cargo without verification of molecular integrity, showed that encapsulation extended TGF-β3 release to 96.64 % over 312 h compared with free TGF-β3, whereas cumulative miR-132 release from the lipoplexes remained limited to 9.84 % over 312 h, indicating strong retention within the delivery system. In a murine burn wound model, the dual-loaded scaffold accelerated wound closure between days 7 and 15, reduced the COL1/COL3 ratio, IL-1α and RASA1 expression compared with the burn control. Consistent with our previous in vitro findings, the combined treatment produced favorable modulation of fibrosis-related molecular responses; however, its superiority at the tissue level was not confirmed by the day-21 histological and immunohistochemical assessments. These findings demonstrate that combining a 3D-printable hydrogel with miR-132/TGF-β3 localized co-delivery system provides an early macroscopic benefit and downstream molecular/biological responses, supporting its further investigation as a localized strategy for pro-regenerative burn wound healing and modulation of fibrotic remodeling.

articles.title: Compatibility of PVC after irradiation: spectroscopic evaluation.
articles.abstract: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) is extensively used in advanced therapies due to its flexibility, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility. This study investigates the equivalency of three ionizing radiation sterilization technologies (gamma rays, X-rays, and electron beam) at 50 and 100 kGy on three medical-grade PVC formulations. A comprehensive analytical approach combining Electron Spin Resonance (ESR), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), colorimetry, and High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) was employed. ESR revealed persistent polyenyl radicals (up to 60 days) influenced by ageing rather than irradiation technology or dose. FTIR-PCA demonstrated dose-dependent carbonyl growth (1708 cm⁻¹) from additive oxidation whereas PVC backbone signatures remained stable. Statistical analysis established that differences among technologies remain within acceptable equivalence margins. These findings confirm that gamma, X-ray, and e-beam irradiation preserve the chemical integrity of PVC formulations for medical device applications.

articles.title: Dihydroquercetin derived from Huanglong Decoction improves acute pancreatitis and related intestinal damage through STAT3/ERK/ZBP1 pathway.
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an inflammatory disorder frequently associated with systemic complications, yet the therapeutic potential of Huanglong Decoction (HLT) in severe AP remains unclear. This study investigated the protective effects of HLT and its candidate bioactive constituent dihydroquercetin (DHQ) against AP. Through integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses, DHQ was identified as a candidate active compound of HLT, and STAT3/ERK signaling was predicted to be involved in its therapeutic mechanism. These predictions were further validated using in vitro and in vivo models. HLT dose-dependently protected pancreatic acinar cells through modulation of this pathway. DHQ reduced ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial function, and suppressed necrotic cell death in vitro. In vivo, DHQ alleviated pancreatic and multi-organ injury and improved survival, accompanied by inhibition of STAT3/ERK signaling and ZBP1-mediated necroptosis. These results suggest that DHQ, the primary active constituent of HLT, markedly ameliorates SAP and multi-organ injury, likely by downregulating STAT3/ERK and ZBP1-mediated necroptosis pathways, positioning it as a compelling therapeutic candidate for SAP and HTG-AP.

articles.title: Biased 5-HT1A agonist NLX-101 improves executive function under NMDA receptor hypofunction and preferentially enhances cortical ERK2 phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: Cognitive inflexibility and working memory deficits are major contributors to functional impairment in neuropsychiatric disorders and remain insufficiently addressed by current treatments. NLX-101, a preferential postsynaptic 5-HT1A receptor biased agonist, engages cortical serotonergic signaling and ERK1/2-related pathways, offering a mechanistically distinct approach to improving prefrontal cortex-dependent cognition. Here, we examined whether NLX-101 counteracts executive function deficits induced by NMDA receptor blockade in BALB/c mice. Working memory was assessed using the 8-arm radial maze, whereas cognitive flexibility was evaluated in a touchscreen-based visual discrimination/reversal learning task. Repeated oral administration of NLX-101 improved MK-801-induced working memory deficits and enhanced reversal learning performance, particularly during the later phase of contingency updating. These behavioral effects were accompanied by preferential enhancement of ERK2 phosphorylation in the prefrontal cortex, consistent with the biased signaling profile of NLX-101. In the touchscreen task, NLX-101 produced clearer improvement than vortioxetine under the dosing and timing conditions used here. Together, these findings identify NLX-101 as a promising pharmacological tool for improving executive dysfunction associated with impaired glutamatergic transmission and support further investigation of biased cortical 5-HT1A receptor signaling as a therapeutic strategy for cognitive symptoms in neuropsychiatric disorders.

articles.title: Piperlongumine alleviates colitis by promoting β-catenin proteasomal degradation to inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis.
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder characterized by diffuse mucosal inflammation confined to the colon and rectum. Long pepper is a widely used condiment for stews and barbecues and is known for its potential nutritional and medicinal value. Piperlongumine (PPL), the major active component of long pepper, represents a promising anti-inflammatory agent. However, the precise mechanism by which PPL regulates colitis remains unclear and requires further elucidation. In this study, we found that PPL interfered with NLRP3 inflammasome assembly in mouse and human macrophages and inhibited inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis. Mechanistic exploration revealed that PPL impaired NLRP3-ASC complex assembly and subsequent inflammasome activation largely by promoting β-catenin proteasomal degradation and reducing β-catenin abundance, with a minor contribution from a β-catenin-independent pathway. Most importantly, PPL alleviated pathological features of dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis, including colorectal shortening, body weight loss, occult blood, and decreased neutrophil infiltration. In summary, PPL is a food-derived ingredient with anti-inflammatory properties that ameliorates colitis by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis.

articles.title: LncRNA SNHG4 sponges miR-let-7d-5p to drive rare earth-induced pulmonary epithelial-mesenchymal transition via HMGA2.
articles.abstract: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a pivotal biological event in the progression of rare earth pneumoconiosis, and inhibiting EMT represents a critical strategy to reverse or delay this disease. Our previous study revealed that plasma microRNA let-7d (miR-let-7d) levels are significantly lower in patients with rare earth pneumoconiosis than in healthy individuals, yet its role in rare earth-induced EMT remains uncharacterized. Herein, we established a neodymium oxide (Nd2O3) induced pulmonary fibrosis mouse model and found that Nd2O3 exposure triggered pulmonary EMT, accompanied by markedly reduced microRNA let-7d-5p (miR-let-7d-5p) expression and elevated levels of long non-coding RNA SNHG4 (lncRNA SNHG4) and high-mobility group AT-hook 2 (HMGA2). Dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed that miR-let-7d-5p directly targets both lncRNA SNHG4 and HMGA2. Mechanistically, overexpression of miR-let-7d-5p decreased HMGA2 expression and alleviated Nd2O3-induced EMT. Conversely, knockdown of lncRNA SNHG4 upregulated miR-let-7d-5p, downregulated HMGA2, and mitigated Nd2O3-induced EMT. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Nd2O3 upregulates lncRNA SNHG4, which acts as a sponge for miR-let-7d-5p to promote HMGA2 expression, thereby driving EMT and subsequent pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: Cysteine 66 in human butyrylcholinesterase is not free, but is blocked by a variety of sulfhydryl reactive molecules.
articles.abstract: The 340 kDa butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) tetramer in human plasma is best known for its protective role against the toxic effects of organophosphorus pesticides and nerve agents. Each subunit is stabilized by 3 internal disulfide bridges plus one disulfide bridge between 2 subunits. These disulfide bridges account for 7 of the 8 cysteines known to be in BChE, leaving 1 cysteine that appears to be free. A free cysteine could disrupt structure and function by disulfide interchange. However, mass spectrometry analysis of purified human plasma BChE shows that the potentially free Cys66 is not free. Instead, it is covalently modified by sulfinic acid or persulfide, sulfonic acid, nitrosothiol, and thiomethyl. The absence of a dominant adduct suggests adducts are formed adventitiously from electrophiles in plasma or liver. The Cys66 adducts explain why Cys66 is unreactive with iodoacetic acid and mercury under physiologic conditions. Adducts are released from Cys66 by treatment with 10 mM dithiothreitol at 100˚C, allowing carbamidomethylation of Cys66. The adducts on Cys66 serve to protect BChE from disulfide interchange.

articles.title: Macrophage-membrane-camouflaged lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles for target-specific biofilm penetration and eradication of methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) biofilms present a formidable therapeutic challenge due to the dense extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix that restricts antibiotic penetration. Here, we engineered biomimetic macrophage-membrane-camouflaged lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (M-LPHNs) designed for targeted delivery and enhanced eradication of MRSA biofilms. M-LPHNs were prepared via emulsification-sonication followed by extrusion-mediated cell membrane coating, yielding monodisperse core-shell spherical structures (∼150 nm, PDI < 0.20) with high colloidal stability in serum. The biomimetic coating imparted a negative surface potential (-28 mV) matching native macrophage membranes and sustained high drug encapsulation efficiencies for vancomycin (78.6%) and daptomycin (84.2%). In vitro susceptibility microdilution assays demonstrated a 4-fold reduction in minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC90) for M-LPHNs compared to free antibiotics. Time-kill kinetics revealed rapid bactericidal activity, achieving >3-log10 kill within 4 h and complete clearance (<10 CFU/mL) at 12 h without secondary regrowth. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy, alongside Live/Dead CLSM assays, confirmed that M-LPHNs induce localized plasma membrane disruption, wall thinning, and intracellular leakage. Quantitative flow cytometry confirmed 92.4% calcein leakage, while in silico molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated lipid acyl chain disordering and membrane nanopore formation. Cytotoxicity assays confirmed high biocompatibility in Caco-2 cells (>92% viability) and negligible hemolysis (<1.8%). M-LPHNs represent a promising biomimetic nanomedicine platform for overcoming matrix barriers in recalcitrant MRSA biofilm infections.

articles.title: β-Hydroxybutyrate alleviates intestinal aGVHD via remodeling gut microbiota-bile acid axis and inhibiting TLR4-NF-κB-driven Th1/Th17 differentiation.
articles.abstract: The intestine is a major target organ in acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD), and its microbial homeostasis critically influences disease pathogenesis and progression. Emerging evidence indicates that beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) can remodel the gut microbiota and dampen pro-inflammatory immune activity. To investigate the therapeutic potential of BHB in aGVHD, we first reanalyzed publicly available transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data from patients with aGVHD, which revealed that genes involved in ketone body metabolism and transport were significantly decreased in intestinal tissues. We then used a murine model of aGVHD to evaluate the therapeutic effects of BHB by clinical scoring and intestinal histopathological examination. To define the immunological and microbial mechanisms, we integrated flow cytometry and ELISA for Th1/Th17, intestinal tissue-resident T and circulating T cells assessment, and with multi-omics analyses, including fecal 16S rRNA sequencing, fecal metabolomics, and intestinal transcriptomics. We further explored whether BHB directly regulates T-cell migration and differentiation and therefore assessed its effects on Th1 and Th17 differentiation in vitro. BHB treatment reduced the clinical score of aGVHD, alleviated intestinal injury in mice, and showed effects similar to those of methotrexate (MTX). BHB also corrected gut microbial dysbiosis, enriched Akkermansia muciniphila, and ameliorated bile acid metabolism dysregulation. Moreover, BHB inhibited intestinal T cell migration and Th1/Th17 differentiation both in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, transcriptome sequencing suggested that suppression of the TLR4-NF-κB pathway may underlie these anti-inflammatory effects. In summary, BHB effectively alleviates intestinal damage in aGVHD mice, likely through coordinated microbial, metabolic, and immunological regulation, and may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for aGVHD.

articles.title: Inhibition of the MEK-ERK signaling pathway reverses acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC attributed to AXL overexpression.
articles.abstract: Osimertinib, a third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI), is the standard first-line treatment for patients with EGFR-activating mutation of late-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the emergence of acquired resistance limits its efficacy in real use. The overexpression of anexelekto (AXL) is known to be associated with acquired resistance to osimertinib. However, the specific mechanisms of AXL-mediated resistance are not well explained, nor of the specific therapeutic approaches in patients for this. In this study, we identified that activation of MEK-ERK pathway played a key role in AXL-driven acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC. Inhibition of the MEK-ERK activation restored osimertinib sensitivity in AXL-driven resistant tumor cells. The combination use of MEK inhibitor with osimertinib reversed the aquierd osimertinib resistance in vitor and in vivo. Our findings provide preclinical mechanistic support for potential use to targeting MEK-ERK signaling in AXL-associated osimertinib resistance and forfurther validation in patient-derived and clinical models.

articles.title: Orai3 deficiency drives atrial remodeling and fibrillation susceptibility via Orai channel remodeling and SOCE hyperactivation.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Atrial remodeling is the pathological substrate for atrial fibrillation (AF), yet no targeted therapies exist. The Orai3 calcium channel regulates cardiac homeostasis, but its role in atrial remodeling remains unexplored. METHODS: Wild type and Orai3 knockout rats were subjected to Angiotensin II infusion or acetylcholine‑calcium chloride injection to model atrial fibrosis and AF. Cardiac function, Orai channel related protein expression and co-localization, SOCE activity, and downstream signaling were evaluated by echocardiography, histology, immunofluorescence, calcium imaging, and western blotting. RESULTS: Orai3 deficiency exacerbated Ang II induced atrial dilation, fibrosis, and ultrastructural damage, with transcriptomic analysis revealing enrichment of extracellular matrix pathways. Mechanistically, Orai3 loss was associated with reduced Orai1/Orai3 co-localization and enhanced Orai1/STIM1 co-localization, driving SOCE hyperactivation. This aberrant Ca2+ signal bidirectionally upregulated TGF-β and suppressed Cx43 effects reversible by SOCE inhibition or Orai3 overexpression. Orai3 has been proposed to function as a molecular rheostat that down tunes STIM1 mediated gating when in complex with Orai1, its loss removes this brake, unleashing pathological SOCE. Consequently, Orai3 deficient rats exhibited increased AF susceptibility, with disrupted Cx43 distribution, shortened gap junctions, and impaired STAT3 mediated Cx43 transcription. CONCLUSIONS: Orai3 acts as an endogenous protective brake against atrial cardiomyopathy. The Orai3-SOCE-TGF-β/Cx43 axis links calcium dyshomeostasis to both fibrotic and electrical remodeling, positioning Orai3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for AF.

articles.title: Evaluation of hydrogen sulfide inhibition as an adjunct to gemcitabine and BCG therapy in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: High production of hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), an endogenous gasotransmitter, has been suggested to promote chemoresistance in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), resulting in high recurrence rate and limited long-term success of current therapies. The present study investigated the therapeutic potential of targeting H₂S production through pharmacological inhibition of the H₂S-producing enzyme cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) using DL-propargylglycine (PAG) in both in vitro and in vivo models of NMIBC. METHODS: In vitro, human bladder cancer cells (5637 & T24) were treated with 20, 60, and 100 mM PAG and proliferation was measured using a CCK-8 assay over 72 h. Migration was also measured using a scratch wound-healing assay in cells treated with 100 mM PAG. 5637 cells were treated with 1 μM gemcitabine (GEM) with or without 100 mM PAG. After 24 and 48 h, cell viability, H2S and ROS levels, and qPCR of H₂S-producing enzymes were measured. In vivo, male C57BL/6 mice received 0.05% N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl)nitrosamine (BBN) for 12 weeks to induce bladder tumours. Tumor burden was measured by MRI before and after 6 weeks of weekly intravesical saline, PAG, GEM, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), or combination therapy. RESULTS: In vitro, treatment of human bladder cancer cells with PAG significantly attenuated cell proliferation and migration. Exposure to GEM increased CBS and CSE expression at 24 and 48 h (p < 0.05). Also, GEM treatment significantly increased intracellular H₂S levels while co-treatment with PAG markedly suppressed this response (p < 0.05), leading to enhanced GEM cytotoxicity, mediated by increased ROS production. In vivo, GEM + PAG was associated with reduced tumour growth compared with either treatment alone, while the addition of BCG exhibited the lowest overall tumour growth. CONCLUSIONS: PAG attenuated human bladder cancer cell proliferation and migration, enhanced the cytotoxic effects of GEM, and was associated with reduced tumour growth when combined with GEM and BCG. Our findings warrant further investigation of targeting H₂S-producing enzymes and intracellular H2S production as a novel pharmacological approach to enhance the cytotoxic effects of GEM in the treatment of NMIBC.

articles.title: Acid-responsive nanoparticles with microneedles for anti‑inflammatory sonodynamic therapy of gouty arthritis.
articles.abstract: The pathological microenvironment of acute gouty arthritis (AGA) features local tissue acidification and the release of a storm of pro-inflammatory cytokines. To address this dual challenge, we engineered an acid-responsive curcumin-loaded nanoparticles microneedle system (Cur-PNPs@MN) that delivers curcumin with pH-triggered release and anti-inflammatory activity. This integrated platform combines a hyaluronic acid (HA)-based dissolving microneedle for localized transdermal delivery of acid-degradable PCADK (poly (cyclohexane-1,4-diyl acetone dimethylene ketal)) curcumin nanoparticles (Cur-PNPs), which are designed for pH-triggered curcumin release at the pathological site. Together, they deliver curcumin, a dual-function agent acting both as an anti-inflammatory compound and a nanoenhanced sonosensitizer. In vitro, the system exhibited acid-responsive drug release and also promoted macrophage uptake, achieving significant curcumin accumulation within 1 hour and saturation by 4 hours. Moreover, it could generate potent ultrasound-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS). The ROS generation capability of Cur-PNPs was 1.47-fold higher than that of Cur‑aggregates, resulting in anapoptosis rate of 29.9% in M1 macrophages. In vivo, the chemo-sonodynamic therapy (Cur-PNPs@MN+Ultrasound (US)) in a rat AGA model significantly alleviated joint swelling and inflammatory infiltration, while drastically suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines, with IL-1β decreasing from 170.3 to 67.3 pg/mL, TNF-α from 20.8 to 5.9 pg/mL, and IL-6 from 140.9 to 48.2 pg/mL, and achieved therapeutic efficacy comparable to conventional drugs. This work demonstrates a synergistic chemo‑sonodynamic strategy by coupling pH-triggered curcumin release with ultrasound-enhanced ROS generation. This acid-responsive therapeutic strategy enhances anti-inflammatory efficacy and reduction of M1-associated inflammatory responses, offering an effective approach for AGA therapy.

articles.title: Acute anxiogenic effects of psilocybin and the related tryptamine, norbaeocystin, in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Psychedelics are considered to be promising therapeutic agents that could effectively treat several psychological disorders. However, these compounds can exert acute adverse effects that limit their practicality. OBJECTIVES: Across three experiments, the present study examined the acute and delayed effects of psilocybin (PSIL) and its putatively non-hallucinogenic analog, norbaeocystin (NOR), on anxiety-like behavior and the influence of the female estrous cycle on acute response to the compounds. METHODS: In Experiment 1, rats were treated with PSIL or NOR (0.3-1 mg/kg) and tested on the elevated plus maze (EPM) or open field 30 min later. In Experiment 2, male and female rats were treated with 1 mg/kg PSIL or NOR and tested on the EPM 24 h later. In Experiment 3, we tracked the female estrous cycle to determine whether it was associated with the acute effects of PSIL or NOR on EPM behavior and the acoustic startle response (ASR). RESULTS: In Experiment 1, both PSIL and NOR exerted acute anxiogenic effects in males, while only the highest dose of PSIL increased anxiety-like behavior in females. In Experiment 2, neither PSIL nor NOR impacted EPM behavior the next day. In Experiment 3, PSIL, but not NOR, had acute anxiogenic effects on EPM behavior, effects that were independent of estrous stage. Females treated with PSIL during diestrus exhibited some signs of greater ASR habituation. CONCLUSIONS: PSIL and NOR exerted transient dose- and sex-specific effects on anxiety-like behavior, which may inform their use as novel therapeutics.

articles.title: Drug repurposing of riluzole attenuates acquisition, accelerates extinction, and prevents reinstatement of ethanol-induced conditioned place preference.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is associated with persistent drug-related memories that lead to relapse. Glutamatergic dysregulation plays a critical role in the acquisition, extinction, and reinstatement of alcohol. Riluzole, a glutamate-modulating agent, has been suggested to influence these processes; however, its effects on ethanol-related contextual learning are not fully defined. METHODS: Male Swiss albino mice (25-30 g) were used in a biased conditioned place preference (CPP) model to evaluate the effects of riluzole on ethanol-induced acquisition, extinction and reinstatement in mice. Animals were conditioned with ethanol (2.0 g/kg, i.p). Riluzole (3, 10, or 30 mg/kg, i.p.) was given 30 min before ethanol administration. Extinction and reinstatement phase was conducted by using separate cohort. The ability of riluzole to prevent reinstatement was then assessed using a low priming dose of ethanol (0.5 g/kg, i.p.). CPP was quantified as the time spent in the drug-paired compartment. RESULTS: Ethanol produced a strong CPP and confirmed the successful acquisition of drug-context associations. Riluzole did not significantly alter acquisition at low doses (3 and 10 mg/kg), but a modest effect was observed at the highest dose (30 mg/kg). During extinction, riluzole facilitated a time-dependent reduction in CPP. Riluzole 10 and 30 mg/kg, increased extinction learning. In the reinstatement phase, ethanol pre-treatment significantly induced CPP, whereas riluzole reduced this effect at 10 and 30 mg/kg and showed no significant reducing effect at 3 mg/kg. CONCLUSIONS: Riluzole attenuated ethanol-induced CPP, facilitated extinction, and reduced reinstatement in a dose and phase-dependent manner. These findings demonstrate that riluzole influences multiple phases of ethanol-associated conditioned behavior and support its further investigation as a potential pharmacological strategy for alcohol use disorder.

articles.title: Extracellular vesicle-mediated preconditioning of osteoblasts by ER+ breast cancer cells: implications for the bone metastatic niche.
articles.abstract: Breast cancer metastasis to bone most commonly occurs in late-stage disease and remains a major contributor to morbidity, reduced quality of life, and mortality, particularly in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) tumors. Intercellular communication between tumor cells and bone-resident cells plays a critical role in promoting tumor invasion and development of metastatic bone lesions. Historically, tumor-bone interactions have been viewed largely through the lens of soluble factor-mediated signaling, particularly in the context of osteoclast-driven bone resorption and osteolytic lesion formation. However, the majority of bone metastases exhibit a mixed lytic and sclerotic phenotype, reflecting the combined involvement of osteoclast- and osteoblast-mediated remodeling. Here, we investigate how ER+ breast cancer-derived extracellular vesicle-enriched conditioned media influence osteoblast behavior and signaling in vitro, positioning osteoblasts as key intermediaries in bone metastatic progression. We first show that ER+ T47D cells release significantly higher EVs than MCF10A non-tumorigenic breast epithelial cells. Next, we demonstrate that osteoblasts actively internalize T47D-derived EVs by 24 h, resulting in significant alterations in their proliferation and signaling profiles associated with chemotaxis and vascular-associated pathways. Finally, we show that conditioned media from T47D EV-preconditioned osteoblasts did not significantly enhance breast tumor cell proliferation or overall motility outcomes. However, despite similar mean motility metrics between conditions, migration behavior exhibited distinct population-level distributions. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ER+ breast cancer-derived EVs drive selective reprogramming of osteoblast signaling and function as an important component in tumor-bone niche conditioning.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes following a traditional Chinese medicine foot bath preparation for lower-limb edema and sleep disturbance: a single-center retrospective study of 2,000 patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical outcomes and documented adverse events following treatment with a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) foot bath preparation in patients with lower-limb edema and sleep disturbance. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study included 2,000 patients treated at Lanzhou Second People's Hospital between May 2017 and May 2022. All patients had varying degrees of lower-limb edema, peripheral circulatory dysfunction, and sleep disturbance. Patients received a standardized TCM foot bath preparation consisting of stir-fried peach kernel (10 g), bush cherry seed (15 g), Chinese angelica root (10 g), and safflower (10 g). The preparation was administered once daily for 20 sessions, comprising two consecutive 10-day treatment courses. Clinical outcomes were assessed by comparing ankle circumference, ABI, and PSQI values before and after treatment. RESULTS: Using the routine record-based classification, 1,120 patients (56.0%) were classified as "markedly effective," 770 (38.5%) as "effective," and 110 (5.5%) as "ineffective." The combined proportion was 94.5%; however, this classification is not internationally validated and is reported descriptively rather than as evidence of effectiveness. After treatment, ankle circumference and PSQI scores were significantly lower than baseline values (both P < 0.01), whereas ABI values were significantly higher (P < 0.05). Mild local adverse reactions, including transient redness and dryness, were observed in a small proportion of patients. CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective observational study, post-treatment changes were observed in lower-limb edema, peripheral circulation, and sleep quality.

articles.title: Selective behavioral and prefrontal transcriptomic correlates of acute clozapine exposure in socially isolated mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clozapine is an effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but acute molecular responses to clozapine remain incompletely characterized. Social isolation rearing produces schizophrenia-relevant behavioral abnormalities and permits joint evaluation of housing and drug exposure. OBJECTIVE: To characterize behavioral and prefrontal transcriptomic correlates of an acute clozapine challenge in socially isolated mice, reassess previously prioritized Ank3 and Nrxn1, and provide external cellular-context hypotheses for candidate genes. METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice were evaluated in a four-group housing-by-drug design using open-field, novel-object recognition and prepulse-inhibition tests. For a reproducible transcriptome-wide audit, 11 publicly retrievable prefrontal cortex libraries were re-quantified using a factorial DESeq2 model with false-discovery-rate control. Historical pairwise prioritization, network analysis, machine-learning screening, molecular docking and molecular-dynamics simulations were treated as exploratory analyses. Adult wild-type prefrontal cortex single-cell RNA-seq data were used for cellular localization, CellChat analysis and virtual knockout, whereas an embryonic cortical reference was used separately for CellOracle transcription-factor perturbation. RESULTS: Acute clozapine showed its clearest behavioral effect on isolation-associated hyperlocomotion, whereas recognition memory was not improved and prepulse-inhibition results varied by stimulus intensity. The primary DESeq2 analysis identified 56 housing-by-drug interaction genes at FDR <0.05; Lamb2 was the strongest FDR-supported transcriptomic signal. Nrxn1 showed directionally opposite changes in historical pairwise contrasts but did not reach FDR significance in the factorial model, whereas Ank3 showed no corresponding factorial support. In adult prefrontal cortex single-cell data, Lamb2 was concentrated in endothelial cells, while Ank3 and Nrxn1 were broadly detected in neuronal populations. Virtual Ank3 and Nrxn1 knockout profiles contained 16 and 15 significant non-target genes, respectively, with five shared genes and no significant reciprocal candidate effect. Embryonic CellOracle analyses identified model-dependent upstream transcription-factor sensitivity of Ank3 and Nrxn1. CONCLUSION: These findings define selective behavioral and prefrontal transcriptomic correlates of an acute clozapine challenge rather than generalized behavioral rescue or clinical treatment-response prediction. Lamb2 was the strongest FDR-supported signal in the primary model, whereas Ank3 and Nrxn1 remain exploratory computational candidates. The external single-cell and virtual-perturbation analyses provide testable cellular and regulatory hypotheses, not evidence of direct binding, causal regulation or clozapine-induced effects in vivo.

articles.title: Sanguinarine ameliorates rheumatoid arthritis by activating the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway to induce apoptosis and suppress inflammation in fibroblast-like synoviocytes.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with progressive joint damage, functional disability and systemic comorbidity. Available therapies are not satisfactory, including low rates of remission and about 30% of patients with poor response to first-line treatment. Thus, more effective therapeutic strategies are urgently needed. Sanguinarine, a benzophenanthridine alkaloid primarily isolated from Sanguinaria canadensis and other members of the Papaveraceae family, has been documented to possess notable anti-bacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anti-neoplastic properties. Nevertheless, its potential utility as a targeted therapeutic modality for RA has yet to be systematically investigated. METHODS: Here, we demonstrate that sanguinarine can effectively ameliorate the development of adjuvant-induced arthritis in rats and decrease arthritis scores, attenuate the inflammatory response, and prevent bone and joint damage. RESULTS: Flow cytometry and ELISA both confirmed its anti-inflammatory activity, reducing the levels of PGE2, TNF-α, IL-1, and IL-6. In human fibroblast-like synoviocytes from RA patients (HFLS-RA), sanguinarine triggered cell apoptosis accompanied by elevated intracellular ROS, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and activation of caspase-3, and activated the Hippo/YAP pathway both in vitro and in vivo. DISCUSSION: These results suggest that sanguinarine ameliorates RA by activation of the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway to induce apoptosis and suppress inflammation, highlighting its potential as a novel therapeutic candidate for RA.

articles.title: A smart MMP-9-responsive hydrogel releasing quercetin for psoriasis therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoriasis is an autoimmune disease characterized primarily by chronic inflammation, with suboptimal clinical therapeutic outcomes. Quercetin, a bio-safe plant secondary metabolite, exerts anti-inflammatory effects by modulating multiple signaling pathways and holds promise as a therapeutic candidate for psoriasis. METHODS: Our preliminary studies demonstrated that silk protein (SF) derived from silkworm cocoons exhibits excellent biocompatibility and can form hydrogels, serving as an ideal drug carrier for skin applications. We loaded quercetin into the SF hydrogel system and systematically investigated the therapeutic efficacy of this composite formulation (QSF) against imiquimod-induced psoriasis models through in vitro and in vivo experiments. RESULTS: The hydrogel exhibited desirable enzyme-responsive properties. When exposed to an in vitro microenvironment containing 10 nM MMP-9, the hydrogel network rapidly disintegrated, achieving a cumulative quercetin release of 58.26% ± 7.64% within 24 h. The enriched quercetin in lesion tissues markedly reduced the positive expression levels of IL-17, TNF-α, and IL-1β, with inhibition rates of 32.14%, 20.25%, and 33.71%, respectively, which effectively interrupted the inflammatory cascade and obviously alleviated skin desquamation and pruritus. DISCUSSION: Collectively, the fabricated QSF hydrogel presents anti-inflammatory and symptomatic relief effects, providing a feasible strategy and experimental basis for the development of novel topical preparations for psoriasis treatment.

articles.title: LKB1 promotes lung adenocarcinoma cell senescence by suppressing the O-GlcNAc glycosylation-mediated activation of telomerase.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Telomeres are crucial for maintaining genomic integrity and stability, making them promising anticancer therapy targets. O-GlcNAc glycosylation is unique and involved in most cellular functions. In most cancers, there is a positive correlation between the degree of tumor malignancy and O-GlcNAc glycosylation levels. However, the relationship between O-GlcNAc glycosylation and telomerase in lung adenocarcinoma remains unclear. We thus investigated the O-GlcNAc-mediated regulation of telomerase activity. METHODS: Protein and mRNA expression levels were detected via western blotting and RT-qPCR, respectively. Telomerase activity, telomere length, and telomere-induced injury foci were detected using telomeric repeat amplification protocol, telomere restriction fragment, and Q-FISH assays, respectively. Cell senescence and proliferation were detected using SA-β-gal staining and EdU assays. IHC and H&E staining were used to detect p53, PCNA, and BCL-2 protein levels in the transplanted tumor tissues and their effects on organs in transplanted tumor-bearing mice. RESULTS: Our findings revealed that LKB1 reduces the overall activity of O-GlcNAcylation and telomerase, resulting in the shortening of telomeres, increased senescence and apoptosis, and decreased tumor cell growth. Insights into the underlying mechanisms have shown that LKB1-AMPK influence the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP), potentially via the phosphorylation of GFAT1. In vivo studies revealed that using both O-GlcNAc and telomerase inhibitors together led to the senescence of tumor cells and hindered their growth, suggesting a viable treatment method for clinical lung adenocarcinoma. DISCUSSION: O-GlcNAc glycosylation promotes telomerase activity and inhibits tumor cell senescence, thereby maintaining telomere lengths in lung adenocarcinoma tumor cells. LKB1 inhibits telomerase activity via the HBP, which may depend on GFAT1 phosphorylation by LKB1. Telomerase inhibitors coupled with O-GlcNAc inhibitors significantly inhibit tumor growth in mice, suggesting clinical lung adenocarcinoma treatment strategies.

articles.title: Profiling crystal engineered ligands for targeting treatment resistant androgen receptors.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the principal contributors to health burden in the aging male population. PCa develops through dysregulation of androgen receptor (AR) signaling pathways.
