Despite improvements in diagnostic techniques and interventions, no pharmacological measures with long term efficacy have been established once PCa advances to castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). To circumvent this issue, tetra-aryl cyclobutanes (CBs) have been proposed as structurally distinct compounds with a mechanism of action differing from traditional androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI). METHODS: Here, we apply principles of crystal engineering and solid state synthesis to expand the class of CBs through strategic derivatization. The synthesis of the CB occurs quantitatively, producing no side products. We demonstrate how head-to-tail stacking interactions of halo-pyrimidine rings can be exploited to stack and align unsymmetrical alkenes to undergo [2 + 2] photodimerization to generate the CB in the solid state. We examine the structure-function relationships of CBs in vitro by profiling AR mediated transcriptional activity, receptor translocation, and cell viability. Moreover, we explored putative binding interactions of ClCB and BrCB ligands across distinct AR mutants (wild-type, T877A, and F877L/T878A) using molecular docking. RESULTS/DISCUSSION: In total, our data suggest that CBs have unexploited therapeutic potential in CRPC and that green chemistry and crystal engineering principles offer a unique route to generate these drug candidates.

articles.title: Efficacy, mechanisms, and influence factors of small molecule targeted therapy in treating rheumatoid arthritis: a multi-dimensional clinical, immunological, and ultrasonographic study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (tsDMARDs) show promise for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but multi-dimensional efficacy evaluation needs further study. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to comprehensively assess tsDMARDs' efficacy in RA and explore factors linked to treatment response. METHODS: 123 consecutive active RA patients treated with tsDMARDs for ≥6 months at Suzhou Ninth People's Hospital (January 2023-December 2024) were retrospectively analyzed; 120 were included after exclusions. Clinical efficacy was appraised using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP), Clinical Disease Activity Index (CDAI), American College of Rheumatology 20/50/70 (ACR20/50/70), and the overall effective rate. Immunological parameters included erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA). Musculoskeletal ultrasound parameters consisted of synovial hypertrophy score assessed by gray-scale ultrasound (GSUS) and synovial vascularity grade assessed by power Doppler ultrasound (PDUS). Correlations between parameters were analyzed, and multivariate logistic regression pinpointed independent risk factors of favorable therapeutic response. RESULTS: Among 120 patients, patients were stratified into effective (n = 78) and non-effective (n = 42) groups, with comparable baseline characteristics (all P > 0.05). After 6 months, the effective group showed significantly greater improvements in DAS28-CRP, CDAI, ESR, CRP, RF, ACPA, GSUS, and PDUS (all P < 0.001). Positive correlations were present between immunological/ultrasound parameters and disease activity scores. Multivariate logistic regression identified reduced PDUS signal, lower CRP, and improved DAS28-CRP as independent predictors of favorable response. CONCLUSION: tsDMARDs effectively improve joint symptoms, reduce disease activity, and enhance articular function in RA patients, potentially supporting personalized therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: A non-destructive methodological framework for modernizing legacy clinical reporting systems for AI-driven pharmacoinformatics: a SAS case study.
articles.abstract: Legacy clinical reporting pipelines bottleneck drug development and pharmacovigilance: they encode regulatory-grade analytical logic but produce opaque output with no machine-readable intermediate layer, resisting integration with artificial intelligence (AI). Existing modernization approaches force a choice between full rewrites that abandon validated logic and incremental refactoring that preserves structural barriers to AI access. We present a non-destructive framework that achieves AI-driven pharmacoinformatics readiness without altering legacy source code. A metadata layer - a bridge map, a typed Intermediate Representation (IR), and an orchestrator - wraps existing reporting components, re-exposes their outputs as structured data consumable by large language models (LLMs), and enables optional incremental consolidation of selected components while the remainder operates unchanged. On a 558-component industrial SAS reporting library (373,000 lines of code), the framework demonstrated immediate AI readiness under coexistence mode with the legacy library unchanged. Where consolidation was elected, the modernized core achieved a 92% reduction in consolidated-core SAS lines of code (excluding the Python and YAML layers). Parity validation on 14 report types from an internal Phase III study cleared an 80% cell-level triage-admission gate on 11 of 14 reports (mean across all 14 report types 82.7%, best 99.2%); the three remaining reports differed in table-layout geometry rather than in computed values. A public benchmark on CDISC CDISCPilot01 data achieved 100% regression-consistency against frozen reference outputs across 5 reports (4,764 cells, 0 mismatches) - a reproducibility benchmark rather than independent validation. In a proof-of-concept study with a single large language model, the IR illustrated the feasibility of table summarization, adverse-event anomaly detection (a pharmacovigilance signal-detection example), and trial configuration generation - feasibility rather than validated performance. The framework offers a regulation-aware path to AI-integrated clinical trial reporting intended to reduce modernization overhead without interrupting ongoing regulatory submissions. Its regulatory-traceability features are design properties rather than validated compliance: no formal Installation/Operational/Performance Qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) has been performed. All results derive from a single case study; the methodology is designed to be reusable across organizations and library scales, pending multi-site empirical validation.

articles.title: Frequency, causes, and duration of drug shortages in South Korea, 2018-2024: a nationwide descriptive analysis of regulatory reporting data and temporal patterns across the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Drug shortages threaten treatment continuity and health-system resilience, yet empirical evidence from South Korea remains limited. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide, retrospective descriptive analysis of 868 drug products (1,054 shortage reports) officially reported to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) between January 2018 and February 2024. Shortages were characterized by frequency, reported cause (six categories), and duration, and compared between reportable and non-reportable drugs. Duration analyses were restricted to 360 temporary supply disruptions. To examine COVID-19-related temporal patterns, temporary supply disruptions during 2018-2023 were grouped into pre-COVID-19 (2018-2019), COVID-19 (2020-2021), and later COVID-19 (2022-2023) periods, defined a priori around the WHO pandemic declaration. Continuous variables were summarized as median (interquartile range, IQR) and categorical variables as counts (%). Analyses were descriptive; no causal inference was intended. RESULTS: A directly substitutable product with the same active ingredient, strength, and dosage form was available for only 269 of 868 drugs (31.0%). Cause structures differed by event type: internal supply issues predominated among temporary supply disruptions (183/396 cause attributions, 46.2%) and business decisions among permanent discontinuations (418/720, 58.1%). Among temporary supply disruptions, regulatory constraints showed the longest durations (median 104 days; IQR 63.3-328) and the largest share lasting ≥366 days (25.0%). Products with ≥2 reported drug shortages were more frequent among orphan drugs (23.3%) and withdrawal-prevention drugs (21.1%), whereas Korean essential drugs showed a widely dispersed duration distribution (median 48 days; IQR 29.8-233.8; 25.6% > 180 days). The numbers of temporary supply disruptions were 53, 106, and 178 in the pre-COVID-19, COVID-19, and later COVID-19/recovery periods, respectively. While internal supply issues remained the leading reported cause throughout (69.8%, 53.4%, and 39.5%), the relative contribution of raw-material supply disruptions (11.3%-26.7%) and increased demand (9.4%-23.1%) grew. CONCLUSION: The patterns observed are consistent with structural vulnerabilities related to market incentives, regulatory processes, and API import dependence, with raw-material and demand-related causes becoming more prominent in the later study periods. Potential policy responses, each requiring separate evaluation, include supply diversification, domestic API production, cost-compensation for economically vulnerable essential medicines, and a risk-based early-warning system with severity-tiered responses.

articles.title: Machine-learning phenotyping and exploratory medication-outcome associations in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a multicohort retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The marked clinical and pathophysiological heterogeneity of HFpEF has repeatedly undermined uniform treatment strategies. Consequently, identifying distinct phenotypes and medication-associated patterns across phenotypes may inform future precision-medicine research. METHODS: In this multicohort retrospective study, patients with HFpEF were included from MIMIC-IV (derivation cohort, n = 2,511), the MIMIC-III CareVue subset (internal validation cohort, n = 1,524), and the Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University (external application cohort, n = 340). Unsupervised K-prototypes clustering was used to derive phenotypic groups, with K = 2 evaluated as a lower-resolution sensitivity solution. All phenotype-stratified medication analyses were exploratory. In the derivation and internal validation cohorts, overlap weighting was the primary weighted analysis and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was a sensitivity analysis; external medication estimates were reported descriptively because adequate within-group covariate balance was not achieved. A TabPFN phenotype-assignment classifier was developed after recursive feature elimination, evaluated in internal validation against independently reclustered labels aligned by prespecified one-to-one Hungarian assignment on cluster-profile distances, and applied without refitting in the external cohort. RESULTS: The primary three-cluster solution identified clinically interpretable but partially overlapping cardiorenal-metabolic, hypertensive-pulmonary, and low-blood-pressure/arrhythmia profiles. K = 2 had a higher mean silhouette width than K = 3 (0.083 versus 0.060), whereas both solutions showed high median resampling stability (ARI, 0.940 versus 0.924). A graded 365-day mortality difference was observed across the three clusters in the derivation cohort, but between-cluster survival differences were not statistically significant in the internal validation or external application cohorts. In the derivation and internal validation cohorts, no weighted cluster-specific medication association remained statistically significant after FDR correction, and all medication-by-cluster interaction tests were nonsignificant. External medication estimates were descriptive and were not used for confirmatory inference. The fixed TabPFN classifier achieved one-versus-rest AUCs of 0.951-0.969 in internal validation (10-bin multiclass ECE = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Routinely collected ICU data supported an exploratory framework for describing overlapping HFpEF phenotypes and reproducibly assigning machine-derived labels. The analyses did not establish phenotype-specific medication effects, and the classifier should be regarded as a research tool pending prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analysis reveals the mechanism of astragalus complanatus flavonoids against liver fibrosis in rats.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Astragali Complanati Semen (ACS) is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb conventionally applied to tonify the liver and kidney. As the primary bioactive ingredients of ACS, Astragalus complanatus flavonoids (ACF) exert hepatoprotective and anti-fibrotic effects. This study aimed to elucidate the antifibrotic mechanisms of ACF through integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses combined with experimental validation. METHODS: A CCl4-induced rat model of LF and TGF-β1-activated hepatic stellate cell (HSC) model were established to evaluate the antifibrotic effects of ACF. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses were performed to identify differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), differentially expressed metabolites (DMs), and associated signaling pathways. Key molecular targets were validated using quantitative real-time PCR and Western blotting, while pharmacological inhibitors were employed to investigate the involvement of the FAK/AKT signaling pathway in ACF-mediated inhibition of HSC activation. RESULTS: Compared with the LF model group, ACF treatment significantly ameliorated liver function indicators, relieved histopathological injury and collagen deposition, decreased serum fibrosis markers, downregulated the protein levels of Col I, Col IV and α-SMA, and reduced oxidative stress and inflammatory response. Proteomic screening uncovered 401 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), which were primarily enriched in extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction, focal adhesion and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways. Protein-protein interaction analysis further pinpointed FN1, CD44, ITGAV, FAK and AKT1 as core target proteins. In vitro experiments demonstrated that ACF blocked TGF-β1-triggered HSC activation, lowered the expression of α-SMA and ITGAV, and inhibited the phosphorylation of FAK and AKT. Pharmacological blockade of either FAK with PF-562271 or AKT with MK2206 strengthened the anti fibrogenic activity of ACF, verifying that the FAK/ AKT axis mediates the anti-HSC activation effect of ACF. Metabolomic analysis identified 108 differentially expressed metabolites (DMs), mainly enriched in glutathione metabolism, primary bile acid biosynthesis and carbohydrate metabolism. Integrated multi-omics analysis confirmed close correlations between DEPs and DMs within ECM-receptor interaction, PI3K/AKT signaling and primary bile acid biosynthesis pathways. Specifically, glycochenodeoxycholic acid, dulcitol and chenodeoxycholate showed strong correlations with coretarget proteins. CONCLUSION: ACF achieves comprehensive anti-LF effects via suppressing FAK/AKT1 signaling to restrain HSC activation, while coordinately modulating pivotal metabolic pathways.

articles.title: Hepatoprotective Formula 919 ameliorates hepatic steatosis and metabolic disturbance in NAFLD with involvement of AMPK signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation and metabolic dysregulation, while effective therapeutic options remain limited. Hepatoprotective Formula 919 (HF919), a traditional Chinese herbal formulation, has shown hepatoprotective effects, but its mechanisms in NAFLD remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of HF919 on hepatic steatosis and metabolic disturbance in NAFLD and the possible involvement of AMPK-associated metabolic regulation. METHODS: Candidate absorbed constituents of HF919 were characterized by UPLC-HRMS and prioritized by in silico screening based on predicted oral bioavailability and drug-likeness. Network pharmacology, public human liver transcriptomic analyses, and molecular docking were integrated to examine disease-relevant candidate targets and pathways. The in vivo effects of HF919 were evaluated in a high-fat diet-induced NAFLD rat model using histological, biochemical, molecular, and immunohistochemical analyses. Fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiling was additionally performed as an exploratory metabolic analysis. RESULTS: HF919 alleviated hepatic steatosis, reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, and improved serum and hepatic lipid-related indices in HFD-induced NAFLD rats. HF919 treatment increased hepatic p-AMPK abundance and Ppara expression and reduced the expression of Tlr4, Nfkb2, and Tgfb1. Hepatic F4/80-positive staining was significantly reduced, accompanied by increased expression of the macrophage-associated genes Mertk and Arg1. Public liver transcriptomic analyses showed lower AMPK- and fatty-acid-oxidation-associated transcriptional features in NASH and in more severe histopathological categories, supporting the disease relevance of these metabolic alterations. Integration of HF919-predicted targets with disease-related transcriptomic changes identified metabolic and injury-related candidate pathways, while molecular docking showed favorable predicted docking scores for selected ligand-target pairs. Exploratory SCFA analysis showed shifts in several fecal SCFAs toward the control-associated pattern and associations with selected hepatic metabolic and molecular parameters. CONCLUSION: HF919 ameliorated hepatic steatosis and metabolic abnormalities in HFD-induced NAFLD rats. The accompanying increase in hepatic p-AMPK abundance and Ppara expression, together with disease-context evidence from human liver transcriptomic datasets, supports the possible involvement of AMPK-associated metabolic regulation. Changes in selected injury-related and macrophage-associated markers and fecal SCFA profiles provided additional secondary or exploratory observations. Further mechanistic studies are needed to establish the causal contribution of AMPK signaling to the effects of HF919.

articles.title: Pharmacist's role in managing drug-drug interactions in people with HIV receiving antiretroviral therapy or HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis: A focus on polypharmacy and transitions of care in the United States.
Modelling nano-particle-PEG-NLS complexes for nucleus-targeted drug delivery: revisiting the multi-dynein nano-cargo transport on microtubules.
articles.abstract: Efficient transport to the nuclear envelope is a prerequisite for many nucleus-targeted drug delivery strategies. We develop an enhanced, energy-based simulation of spherical nanoparticle (NP) complexes hauled by multiple dynein motors via flexible polymer linkers, aimed at deriving design rules for nucleus-directed delivery. The model extends prior work by treating dynein as a semi-flexible polymer and enforcing path-wise steric exclusion along full stepping trajectories. Event propensities follow a Monte-Carlo scheme with energies that couple linker entropy, dynein bending, and binding enthalpy; post-event mechanical relaxation uses gradient descent. We compare our model results to recent motility assays of spherical NPs decorated with polyethylene-glycol (PEG) polymers, each ending with a nuclear-localisation-signal (NLS) peptide that can recruit dynein from the cytoplasm. With standardised biophysical parameters, the model captures the observed dependence on motor number: longitudinal velocity decreases with dynein load, whereas run-distance and run-time increase. For mean NP-bound motors between 1 and 6, the model results lie within the experimental 95% confidence intervals. A systematic scan of polymer contour length, for a 20 nm radius cargo hauled by six motors, reveals a clear optimum of the run-time and run-length at about 40 nm length, despite a reduction in velocity. Similar results, for different cargo sizes and motor loading, can be obtained using our model-based computer code. They can provide a quantitative basis for tuning linker contour length (and, secondarily, motor loading by tuning PEG-NLS density) when engineering NP vehicles that exploit native microtubule transport for nucleus-directed delivery.

articles.title: Effects of vitamin B1/B6/B12 complex on methotrexate-induced hepatorenal toxicity in a short-term acute rat model.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of vitamin B1/B6/B12 complex supplementation on methotrexate (MTX)-induced hepatorenal injury in a short-term, single-dose acute rat model. Male Wistar rats were assigned to control, MTX, low-dose (MTX + VB-L), and high-dose (MTX + VB-H) vitamin B complex groups. A single MTX (20 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally on day 7. Vitamin B1/B6/B12 was administered intraperitoneally daily at 16/16/0.16 or 32/32/0.32 mg/kg on days 1-14. Samples were collected on day 14. Serum AST, ALT, urea, and creatinine, hepatic, and renal thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) and total thiol (TT), and histopathological changes were evaluated. MTX significantly increased AST, urea, creatinine, hepatic and renal TBARS, and multiple histopathological scores compared with controls. Compared with MTX alone, AST and hepatic TBARS were significantly lower only in the MTX + VB-H group, whereas creatinine and renal TBARS were significantly lower in both treatment groups. Renal TBARS was significantly lower in MTX + VB-L than in MTX + VB-H. Neither the treatment group differed significantly from the MTX group in ALT, urea, TT, or any hepatic or renal histopathological parameter. Vitamin B complex co-administration was associated with improvements in selected biochemical markers and lower TBARS levels, without statistically significant histopathological improvement. The absence of a vitamin-only group limits distinction between MTX-specific attenuation and independent formulation effects. Further preclinical studies are required before clinical implications can be established.

articles.title: The global surge of cocaine use disorder: a 30-year burden analysis from the GBD 2021.
articles.abstract: Cocaine use disorder (CUD) represents a growing global health challenge with an inadequately characterized epidemiological profile. Utilizing data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study across 204 countries or territories (1990-2021), this study assessed age-standardized incidence (ASIR), prevalence (ASPR), mortality (ASMR), and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) rates. Key trends were analyzed using Estimated Annual Percentage Change (EAPC). Additional analyses included frontier mapping against the Socio-demographic Index (SDI), decomposition to identify driving factors, and ARIMA modeling for future projections. Findings revealed that global cocaine production tripled between 2009 and 2023, coinciding with a rising CUD burden: ASMR increased by 114% from 1990 to 2021, with males experiencing a faster mortality increase compared to females. High-income and Latin American regions bore the highest burden-the USA led in ASIR and ASMR, while Spain saw declines after 2005 due to stringent policies. SDI strongly correlated with ASIR (ρ = 0.59), and high-SDI regions had higher DALYs than low-SDI areas. Projections indicate accelerating ASMR and DALY rates in high-income countries by 2036. CUD imposes an escalating and inequitable global burden, disproportionately affecting males, high-income populations, and the Americas. Addressing this crisis requires targeted interventions and improved surveillance of evolving use patterns and comorbidities.

articles.title: Combined rituximab and magnesium acetyl taurate therapy attenuates neurodegeneration via ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling modulation in methylmercury-induced amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-like neurotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor neuron degeneration, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulation of intracellular signaling pathways. The present study investigated the neuroprotective potential of rituximab (RTXMB), alone and in combination with magnesium acetyl taurate (MACT600), against methylmercury (MLMC5)-induced ALS-like pathology in adult Wistar rats through modulation of the ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling pathway. ALS was induced by oral administration of MLMC5 (5 mg/kg) for 21 days. RTXMB (50 and 100 mg/kg) and MACT600 (600 mg/kg) treatments were administered from day 22 to day 42. Behavioral assessments, neurochemical estimations, ELISA, Western blotting, hematological analysis, gross morphology, and histopathological evaluations were performed. MLMC5 exposure produced significant impairments in locomotion, muscular strength, cognition, and emotional behavior, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokines, glutamate excitotoxicity, apoptotic markers, methylmercury accumulation, and dysregulation of ERK/c-JNK/P38MAPK signaling. Moreover, MLMC5 caused marked demyelination, neuronal degeneration, neurotransmitter imbalance, skeletal muscle damage, and hematological dysfunction. RTXMB treatment significantly attenuated these pathological alterations in a dose-dependent manner, with RTXMB100 showing greater neuroprotective efficacy. Combined administration of RTXMB100 and MACT600 demonstrated the most pronounced therapeutic effects by restoring antioxidant defenses, suppressing neuroinflammation and apoptosis, normalizing neurotransmitter levels, preserving myelin integrity, and improving neuronal morphology. The findings suggest that RTXMB, particularly in combination with MACT600, exerts potent neuroprotective effects against ALS-like pathology via modulation of MAPK signaling pathways and may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ALS management.

articles.title: Mapping the knowledge landscape and identifying frontiers of mitochondrial dysfunction in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a four-decade bibliometric and visualized analysis.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been recognized as a central pathogenic event and is under active investigation as a candidate therapeutic target in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). This study aims to employ multi-tool bibliometric analysis to systematically map the four-decade intellectual landscape of this field, thereby identifying emerging research hotspots and outlining priority-setting directions for future pharmacological investigation. Because publication and citation metrics quantify scholarly attention rather than therapeutic efficacy, the pathways highlighted here reflect research trends and priority-setting signals, not established therapeutic targets. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus up to March 18, 2026. Following rigorous data cleaning, 837 publications were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package to visually evaluate publication trends, knowledge networks, and evolving research hotspots. Cumulative publication output exhibits sustained exponential growth (R2 = 0.997), accelerating significantly post-2010. China and the USA dominate global productivity, though institutional collaboration networks reveal pronounced regional clustering. Notably, publication hubs have transitioned significantly from traditional critical care journals to molecular and pharmacological journals, consistent with a shifting emphasis of scholarly attention toward molecular and pharmacological research themes. Keyword and citation burst analyses suggest that the research frontier has evolved from broad physiological observations to specific subcellular executioners. Mitochondria-mediated programmed cell death (apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis) and oxidative stress have become the most prominent bibliometric hotspots and candidate pharmacological targets. The field of SA-AKI research has shown a pronounced, publication-driven shift from clinical phenotyping to the target-driven molecular deconstruction of mitochondrial damage; we emphasize that this result reflects research priorities, not proven therapeutic efficacy of these targets. To overcome current translational bottlenecks and off-target effects of existing agents, future drug development should transition from isolated in vitro models toward clinical multi-omics validation. Developing innovative targeted delivery systems (such as engineered nanomaterials and exosomes) and multi-target synergistic therapies will need rigorous empirical testing to determine whether they can precisely mitigate the complex SA-AKI "mitochondrial storm".

articles.title: Global Malat1 deletion in two genetic mouse models reveals sex-dependent effects on select ethanol-related behaviors.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a widespread psychiatric condition, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its development remain poorly understood. While prior studies have largely focused on protein-coding genes, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) remain underexplored in AUD. Malat1, a highly abundant and evolutionarily conserved lncRNA, is elevated in post-mortem brain tissue of human AUD subjects and rodents chronically exposed to ethanol; however, its causal contribution to AUD-relevant behaviors remains unknown. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated two complementary global Malat1 knockout mouse models to assess its role in ethanol intake and related phenotypes. Constitutive knockout selectively attenuated acute functional tolerance rate and every-other-day two-bottle-choice (EOD-2BC) ethanol intake in females. These results were supported by an inducible adult conditional global knockout model, which reduced EOD-2BC ethanol consumption in females without altering taste preference. Together, our findings provide the first causal evidence that Malat1 regulates select ethanol-related behaviors in a sex-specific manner, supporting further investigation into its underlying mechanisms in AUD.

articles.title: UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) is a novel positive regulator of MyD88-driven inflammation in sepsis.
articles.abstract: Excessive activation of MyD88 in sepsis drives uncontrolled cytokine production, leading to multi-organ injury and high mortality. However, the mechanisms that regulate MyD88 activation and link it to glycosphingolipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) as a novel positive regulator of MyD88-mediated signaling and a potential biomarker for sepsis. UGCG expression was elevated in septic patients and LPS-stimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis showed that UGCG knockdown broadly suppresses inflammatory pathways. Functionally, UGCG deficiency selectively impaired MyD88- but not TRIF-dependent signaling and reduced cytokine production. Pharmacological inhibition of UGCG using the FDA-approved drug N-butyl-deoxynojirimycin (NB-DNJ) suppressed inflammatory gene expression, immune cell infiltration, and lung injury in an LPS-induced murine sepsis model. Mechanistically, UGCG interacts with the MyD88 TIR domain to promote MyD88 protein stability, while UGCG deficiency is associated with impaired ligand-triggered MyD88 oligomerization. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized UGCG-MyD88 axis that directly links UGCG to innate immune signaling independently of its enzymatic activity, and highlight UGCG as a promising therapeutic target for sepsis.

articles.title: Polylactic acid nanoplastics induce kidney injury by activating the TRPM2-mediated mitophagy pathway.
articles.abstract: Polylactic acid nanoparticles (PLA NPs) are widely used biodegradable plastics, but their potential health risks remain unclear. This study explores whether PLA NPs induce renal cell apoptosis through a mitochondrial pathway involving transient receptor potential melastatin 2 (TRPM2) and mitophagy. Adult male C57BL/6 mice were orally exposed to 0.1, 1, and 10 mg/kg/day PLA NPs for 28 consecutive days. PLA NPs caused dose-dependent kidney injury, with the high-dose group (group H, 10 mg/kg/day) showing the most severe renal apoptosis and functional impairment. In group H, renal calcium ion (Ca2+) levels, mitophagy, and TRPM2 expression were significantly elevated. To investigate the mechanism, TRPM2-KO mice (group KH) and mitophagy inhibitor Mdivi-1-treated mice (group Md) were orally administered 10 mg/kg/day PLA NPs daily. Compared with group H, both group KH and group Md showed reduced renal injury, as evidenced by decreased apoptosis and restored mitochondrial function. These results indicate that PLA NPs induce oxidative stress, activate the TRPM2 channel, cause calcium overload and excessive mitophagy, and ultimately trigger renal cell apoptosis. This study provides a theoretical basis for targeted treatment of kidney diseases caused by PLA NPs.

articles.title: Halogenated Disinfectants Inhibit Human and Rat 17β-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase 1 Activity and Disrupt Estradiol Synthesis: Implications for Endocrine Disruption.
articles.abstract: Halogenated disinfectants are widely used in medical, household, and industrial settings, but their inhibitory effects on 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 1 (17β-HSD1), a key enzyme catalyzing estrone-to-estradiol (E2) conversion, remain unclear. We evaluated nine compounds for inhibition of human placental and rat ovarian 17β-HSD1 using enzymatic assays, kinetic analysis, BeWo cell E2 production assays, 3D quantitative structure-activity relationship (3D-QSAR), molecular docking, molecular dynamicssimulations (MDS), absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) prediction, and network toxicology. Six compounds inhibited human 17β-HSD1, with half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 0.78-14.90 μM; potency followed hexachlorophene > bithionol > bromochlorophene > fenticlor > dichlorophene > chlorophene. Rat 17β-HSD1 was inhibited by these six compounds and by triclosan, with IC50 values of 6.13-54.77 μM. Kinetic analysis indicated mainly mixed/noncompetitive inhibition. In BeWo cells, fenticlor decreased E2 production at ≥ 1 μM, dichlorophene at 10 and 20 μM, and bromochlorophene and hexachlorophene at 20 μM, whereas chlorophene and bithionol were inactive up to 20 μM. The 3D-QSAR model and descriptor analysis suggested associations of inhibition with hydrophobicity, aromatic features, molecular size and halogenation. Docking and 100-ns MDS supported stable binding of active compounds near the nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH)-binding region, particularly for hexachlorophene. Network toxicology placed HSD17B1, which encodes 17β-HSD1, within preeclampsia-related estrogen and steroidogenic pathways. These findings indicate that halogenated disinfectants may disrupt estrogen homeostasis through direct 17β-HSD1 inhibition and warrant further evaluation for reproductive and placental endocrine toxicity.

articles.title: Maternal CuO NPs exposure induces vascular damage in offspring via ferroptosis and cuproptosis: the regulatory role of GSH.
articles.abstract: With extensive applications in industrial, agricultural, and biomedical fields, copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) have attracted increasing concerns over their environmental exposure and potential health risks. Maternal nanoparticles exposure affects fetal development and leads to long-term health consequences in offspring. However, the developmental vascular toxicity and underlying mechanisms of CuO NPs on offspring remain unclear. In this study, pregnant rats were exposed to CuO NPs from gestation to lactation. CuO NPs induced histopathological damage and collagen deposition in the offspring aorta, indicating vascular structural damage. Moreover, alterations associated with ferroptosis and cuproptosis were observed in the offspring aorta. In vitro, CuO NPs induced oxidative stress and promoted the ubiquitination-dependent degradation of xCT in HUVECs, accompanied with intracellular glutathione (GSH) depletion. GSH depletion was associated with impaired GPX4-mediated antioxidant defense, increased DLAT aggregation, and loss of Fe-S cluster proteins. These findings supported the involvement of ferroptosis and cuproptosis related responses and suggested a potential interaction between these two processes. Furthermore, Fer-1, TTM, and GSH alleviated CuO NPs-induced alterations, whereas erastin, elesclomol, and BSO exacerbated these processes, further supporting an association between ferroptosis and cuproptosis. These findings suggested that vascular injury in offspring was associated with maternal CuO NPs exposure, accompanied by ferroptosis and cuproptosis related alterations, while GSH might serve as an important regulatory factor in their interaction. This study provides critical insights into the vascular toxicity risks in offspring after maternal nanoparticles exposure and highlights the potential role of GSH in nanoparticle-induced developmental cardiovascular injury.

articles.title: Ligustilide enhances TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer to accelerate the reactivation of TECs in sleep deprivation induced postpartum mouse.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Danggui) has been widely used by puerperae in China for postpartum recovery for more than a thousand years. Its key active ingredient, ligustilide (LIG), has been documented to exert thymus-repairing effects; however, its role and underlying mechanisms in postpartum thymic regeneration impairment remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: During the puerperium, the acutely atrophied maternal thymus gradually returns to its non-pregnant state. However, frequent sleep deprivation (SD) resulting from neonatal breastfeeding often slows down the thymus recovery process. This study investigated the efficacy and underlying mechanism of LIG, an active ingredient of A. sinensis, against SD-induced thymic regeneration disorder (SDTRD) in postpartum mice. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Postpartum SD was induced by automated disturbance; a progesterone-estrogen withdrawal (PE) model followed by a 7-day high-dose steroid treatment. LIG (1 mg/kg) was administered during regeneration. Thymic architecture (H&E), thymic epithelial cells (TEC) localization (immunofluorescence), and thymocyte subsets (flow cytometry) were quantified. Spleen sjTREC, thymic cytokines, and transcripts for mitochondrial biogenesis/function were measured by qPCR. TEM assessed mitochondrial ultrastructure. Dual-color mitochondrial tracing combined with a thymocyte-iTECs co-culture system and a bone-marrow-cell thymic homing assay mapped intercellular mitochondrial transfer. Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) were disrupted with cytochalasin D; Rho-GTPase activation (including Cdc42) was evaluated. RESULTS: Postpartum mice with SD showed damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and reduced mitochondrial biogenesis in TECs, leading to TECs dysfunction and interruption of postpartum thymic regeneration. LIG significantly restored the abnormal spatial localization of TECs, improved the reticular framework of cortical TECs (cTECs), promoted thymocyte development, and increased output of CD4+ T-cells. Mechanistically, LIG may facilitate the formation of F-actin-dependent TNTs between thymocytes and TECs, mediating mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to dysfunctional TECs. This process may rely on Rho GTPase signaling pathways (Cdc42 activation) to regulate F-actin polymerization. CONCLUSIONS: LIG may promote F-actin-dependent TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to TECs, thereby reactivating TECs, restoring the thymic microenvironment, rescuing thymocyte development and export, and ultimately ameliorating SD-induced postpartum thymic regeneration. These findings provide new experimental evidence for the development of LIG as a preventive and therapeutic intervention for defective postpartum thymic repair.

articles.title: Si-Shen-San Attenuates Alzheimer's Disease Pathology and Cognitive Deficits Through Multi-Target Regulation of Astrocyte Function and Synaptic Plasticity.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder pathologically characterized by cognitive decline, amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic dysfunction, and astrocyte dysregulation. The constituent herbs of the traditional Chinese medicine formula Si-Shen-San (SSS) have been used to ameliorate cognitive impairment. However, the comprehensive chemical profile, core bioactive constituents, and underlying mechanisms of action of SSS remain to be fully elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to systematically investigate the therapeutic potential of SSS against AD and to clarify its multi-faceted mechanisms of action, with a focus on astrocyte-mediated neuroprotection, synaptic repair, and modulation of core AD pathologies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole/time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q/TOF-MS) was used to characterize the chemical constituents of SSS extract and SSS-containing serum. In vivo, 3×Tg-AD mice were orally administered SSS. And cognitive function, AD-related pathology, synaptic integrity, and astrocyte-associated molecular changes were evaluated using behavioral, histological, biochemical, ultrastructural, and electrophysiological approaches. In vitro, an astrocyte-conditioned medium paradigm was used to examine whether SSS-induced changes in astrocytes were associated with protection of HT22 neurons against glutamate-induced injury. RESULTS: UHPLC-Q/TOF-MS tentatively annotated 525 and 318 compounds in the SSS extract and drug-containing serum. In 3×Tg-AD mice, SSS improved cognitive performance, reduced hippocampal 6E10- and ThS-positive Aβ-like immunoreactivity and tau phosphorylation at Thr231 and Ser404, and preserved synaptic structure and function. The reduction in tau phosphorylation was accompanied by changes in GSK-3β signaling. SSS treatment was also associated with reduced astrocyte reactivity, increased GLT-1 expression, and restoration of astrocyte-associated homeostatic markers. In vitro, conditioned medium derived from SSS-treated C8-D1A astrocytes alleviated glutamate-induced injury in HT22 neurons and was accompanied by activation of neuronal CREB-BDNF signaling. CONCLUSION: SSS ameliorated cognitive deficits and multiple AD-related pathological alterations in 3×Tg-AD mice. These effects were associated with restoration of astrocyte-related homeostatic features, improved glutamate regulation, preservation of synaptic integrity, and activation of CREB-BDNF signaling. These findings provide an experimental foundation for SSS as a potential therapeutic strategy for AD and highlight astrocyte homeostasis as a promising target for future drug development.

articles.title: Safflower yellow alleviates sciatic nerve crush injury in rats: associated with TRPV1-pERK signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) clinically resembles the traditional Chinese medical "Bi" and "Blood-Stasis" syndromes. Carthamus tinctorius L. (safflower) is a classic blood-activating and stasis-resolving herb commonly prescribed for PNI, whereas the protective effect of its major active component safflower yellow (SY) against PNI remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the efficacy and potential mechanisms of SY in ameliorating PNI using a rat sciatic nerve crush (SNC) model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 10): Sham, SNC model, SNC + SY 20 mg/kg, and SNC + SY 40 mg/kg. All rats were sacrificed 15 days after SNC surgery. RESULTS: SY intervention significantly promoted sciatic nerve functional recovery, alleviated mechanical allodynia, reversed denervation-induced gastrocnemius atrophy, and ameliorated histopathological damage in SNC-injured nerve tissues. Mechanistically, SY suppressed neuroinflammation, as evidenced by reduced CD68-positive macrophage accumulation and decreased levels of tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, prostaglandin E2, and cyclooxygenase-2, restored oxidative balance by regulating superoxide dismutase and malondialdehyde contents in injured nerves. Moreover, SY upregulated nerve regeneration markers (growth-associated protein 43, myelin basic protein, β3-tubulin). Molecular docking revealed strong binding of SY to transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) (-7.7 kcal/mol); molecular dynamics simulation verified stable complex formation (RMSD 0.38 ± 0.03 nm). Biological validation demonstrated that SY markedly inhibited SNC-induced upregulation of TRPV1-pERK1/2 in sciatic nerve and dorsal root ganglion. CONCLUSIONS: SY alleviates peripheral nerve damage, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, promotes nerve repair in SNC rats, and is associated with modulation of TRPV1-pERK1/2 signaling, revealing a novel neuroprotective role of SY for PNI.

articles.title: Jingfang Baidu San Alleviates Feng-Han (Wind-Cold) Syndrome-Associated Lung Injury in Mice Through Macrophage Functional Regulation and Dectin-1-Associated Immune Remodeling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jingfang Baidu San (JF) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine(TCM)formula that has been widely used in clinical practice for hundreds of years. While its efficacy in treating Feng Han (wind-cold, FH) common cold has garnered increasing attention, its underlying mechanism of action remain incompletely understood. AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of JF on wind-cold common cold and to elucidate its molecular mechanism. METHODS: A mouse model of wind-cold syndrome (FH) was established by exposing mice to wind and cold stress for 7 consecutive days. The therapeutic effects of orally administered JF were initially evaluated by assessing behavioral manifestations, body weight, and rectal temperature. Lung histopathology was subsequently examined using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. To investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of JF on FH, transcriptomic sequencing of lung tissues was performed to identify key differentially expressed genes and associated regulatory networks. Inflammatory cytokine levels in serum and lung tissues were further quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), while the expression and localization of key molecular targets and related proteins were validated by immunofluorescence staining, immunohistochemistry, and Western blotting. RESULTS: JF significantly ameliorated the major pathological manifestations in FH model mice, as evidenced by body weight recovery, reduction of elevated rectal temperature, and improvement of behavioral abnormalities including lethargy, hypoactivity, and respiratory abnormalities. Histopathological analysis further confirmed that JF markedly alleviated lung tissue injury and reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α in serum and lung tissue. At the mechanistic level, through transcriptomic analysis combined with in vivo validation, we identified Dectin-1 Clec7a as a potential macrophage-related regulatory node associated with the efficacy of JF in treating FH. JF treatment restored the expression of macrophage-associated Dectin-1, while attenuating macrophage-associated inflammatory responses and tissue remodeling responses. In conclusion, the protective effect of JF against FH-related lung injury is associated with the regulation of macrophage Dectin-1, inhibition of NF-κB activation, and attenuation of TGF-β-related responses, inflammatory responses, and abnormal extracellular matrix remodeling. CONCLUSION: The protective effects of JF against FH-induced lung injury were associated with modulation of macrophage Dectin-1 expression, suppression of NF-κB activation, and attenuation of TGF-β-related signaling, accompanied by reduced inflammation and amelioration of aberrant extracellular matrix remodeling. These findings suggest that Dectin-1-mediated macrophage regulation may contribute to the protective effects of JF. Further genetic and pharmacological studies are needed to establish the causal roles of Dectin-1, NF-κB, and TGF-β-related signaling pathways in mediating the effects of JF.

articles.title: Modified Danzhi Xiaoyao San ameliorates depression-associated dry eye by modulating sphingolipid metabolism across the liver, hippocampus, and lacrimal gland.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Modified Danzhi Xiaoyao San (MDZXYS) originates from Xue Ji's "Internal Medicine Abstract" (Ming Dynasty), which derived from the Song Dynasty Taiping Huimin Heji Jufang Xiao-Yao Powder by adding Moutan Cortex and Gardeniae Fructus. It is traditionally used to soothe the liver, relieve depression, and clear stagnant heat associated with liver-qi stagnation transforming into fire. Grounded in the theory that "the liver opens into the eyes," liver-soothing and heat-clearing strategy has long been applied to treat ocular diseases. Previous studies have reported beneficial effects of Danzhi Xiaoyao San and related modified formulas on depression and dry eye; however, the metabolic basis of their effects across multiple tissues remains incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the therapeutic effects of MDZXYS in a rat model of depression-associated dry eye and characterized associated changes in sphingolipid metabolism across multiple tissues. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A rat model of depression-associated dry eye was established by combining chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) with benzalkonium chloride (BAC) eye drops. low- and high-dose MDZXYS were orally administered, with venlafaxine as the positive control. Evaluations included assessments of depression-like behaviors, tear secretion, tear film break-up time (TBUT), and corneal fluorescein staining. Histopathology, ELISA for inflammatory cytokines, targeted lipidomics, and Western blotting for Sptlc2 and nSMase were performed on hippocampal, hepatic, lacrimal gland, and serum samples. RESULTS: MDZXYS attenuated hippocampal neuronal abnormalities in the CA1, CA3, and DG regions and increased BDNF expression. It also improved pathological changes in the liver and lacrimal glands and preserved conjunctival goblet cells. MDZXYS increased tear secretion, prolonged TBUT, and reduced corneal fluorescein staining. Behavioral assessments showed increased sucrose preference and locomotor activity, together with reduced immobility time. MDZXYS also reduced the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α and increased IL-4 levels in the liver, serum, and lacrimal glands. Lipidomic profiling and KEGG enrichment analysis showed that differentially altered metabolites across the hippocampus, liver, lacrimal gland, and serum were significantly enriched in the sphingolipid metabolism pathway. Among the altered sphingolipid metabolites, Cer(d18:1/20:1), Cer(d18:1/22:1), Cer(d18:1/24:1), HexCer(18:1/24:1), SM(d18:1/16:0), and SM(d18:1/20:1) showed significant associations with depressive-like behaviors and dry eye-related phenotypes. MDZXYS treatment partially reversed these disease-associated sphingolipid alterations. Western blotting further revealed tissue-specific changes in sphingolipid metabolism-related protein expression: MDZXYS increased nSMase and decreased Sptlc2 expression in the hippocampus, whereas both proteins were upregulated in the lacrimal gland. CONCLUSIONS: MDZXYS improved inflammatory, behavioral, and ocular abnormalities and was associated with tissue-specific changes in sphingolipid metabolism across the hippocampus, liver, and lacrimal gland. MDZXYS treatment was accompanied by tissue-specific changes in Sptlc2 and nSMase expression and partial normalization of disease-associated sphingolipid alterations. These findings support the involvement of sphingolipid dysregulation in depression-associated dry eye and suggest that MDZXYS modulates sphingolipid metabolism in a tissue-specific manner. The observed cross-tissue associations provide an exploratory metabolic context for these findings but do not establish directional or causal relationships among tissues.

articles.title: Enzymatically degalactosylated xyloglucan in situ gels for topical delivery of triamcinolone acetonide.
articles.abstract: Thermoresponsive in situ gelling systems are attractive platforms for topical ocular delivery because they can be administered as liquids and rapidly form gels at the ocular surface, thereby increasing residence time and sustaining drug release. This study investigated whether enzymatic degalactosylation of tamarind-seed xyloglucan could be used to develop thermoresponsive hydrogels for the delivery of triamcinolone acetonide (TA). Degalactosylation kinetics, monitored by monosaccharide analysis and oligosaccharide profiling, showed rapid initial galactose removal followed by a plateau near 50%. This structural evolution modified xyloglucan oligosaccharide motifs and induced thermoresponsive gelation after substantial degalactosylation. Among the modified samples, Deg50-XG showed the most suitable thermal transition. At 3.0% (w/v), it gelled at 35°C within about 68 s and formed the strongest elastic network. Contact with simulated tear fluid was found to be a second, independent gelation trigger: at an identical polymer concentration of 1.5% (w/v), the sol-gel transition shifted from 36.4°C in water to 25.7°C, i.e. from above to well below ocular surface temperature, and an elastic network with a storage modulus approximately three orders of magnitude higher was formed at 35°C. In vitro release studies showed that increasing polymer concentration slowed TA release and reduced dissolution efficiency, consistent with denser hydrogel networks. Kinetic analysis indicated that the relative contribution of network relaxation and erosion to drug transport increased with polymer concentration, while release remained consistent with a matrix containing dispersed, poorly soluble drug. These results show that controlled enzymatic tailoring of xyloglucan can be used to tune gelation behavior and drug-release performance in dually thermo- and ion-triggered thermoresponsive in situ gelling systems for sustained topical delivery of TA.

articles.title: Food-associated pharmacokinetic differences and variability of a rosuvastatin/ezetimibe fixed-dose combination in replicated bioequivalence studies.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND /OBJECTIVES: Rosuvastatin/ezetimibe fixed-dose combinations target cholesterol synthesis and intestinal absorption, but pharmacokinetics may differ by analyte, endpoint, and fasted/fed state. This study characterized food-associated pharmacokinetic differences, reference-product within-subject variability, and bioequivalence decision pathways. METHODS: Data were integrated from two independently conducted, single-center, randomized, open-label, single-dose, two-sequence, four-period, fully replicated crossover bioequivalence trial parts in healthy Chinese adults (ChiCTR2500110429). Free and total ezetimibe and rosuvastatin were evaluated in fasted and fed states. Bioequivalence was assessed separately in each trial part, while exploratory food-associated comparisons used reference-product data averaged across replicated periods within participants. RESULTS: Food-associated patterns differed by analyte and endpoint. Fed-to-fasted geometric mean ratios (GMRs) for free ezetimibe were 258.8% for maximum plasma concentration (Cmax), 125.9% for area under the concentration-time curve from time zero to the last measurable concentration (AUC0-t), and 127.1% for area under the concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-∞). For total ezetimibe, the Cmax GMR was 152.4%, whereas AUC shifts were smaller than the free ezetimibe. Rosuvastatin GMRs were 47.7%, 59.2%, and 60.8% for Cmax, AUC0-t, and AUC0-∞, respectively. Within-subject coefficients of variation (CVW%) differed by analyte, endpoint, and state. All primary endpoints met average bioequivalence (ABE) or reference-scaled average bioequivalence (RSABE) criteria in both states. No serious or grade ≥ 2 adverse events or adverse-event-related withdrawals occurred. CONCLUSIONS: Food-associated pharmacokinetic differences were analyte- and endpoint-dependent, whereas formal bioequivalence was demonstrated in both states. These findings support separate interpretation of food-associated pharmacokinetics, reference-product variability, and bioequivalence in multi-analyte fixed-dose combination evaluation.

articles.title: A dual-functional nanosuspension-in-matrix mini-tablet system for enhancing oral bioavailability and prolonging antiplatelet response of ticagrelor.
articles.abstract: Ticagrelor (TCG) is an oral P2Y12 receptor antagonist with limited aqueous solubility, which can restrict its dissolution and oral absorption. In this study, a ticagrelor nanosuspension-loaded sustained-release mini-tablet (TCG-NSP@SMT) was developed to combine nanosuspension-based dissolution enhancement with matrix-mediated release control. TCG nanosuspension (TCG-NSP) was prepared by antisolvent precipitation using D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol 1000 succinate and polyvinyl alcohol as stabilizers, followed by spray drying. The resulting TCG-NSP exhibited a mean particle size of 188.8 ± 2.4 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.136 ± 0.003, and retained acceptable redispersibility after spray drying. Solid-state analyses indicated reduced crystallinity of TCG in the nanosuspension formulation. A D-optimal experimental design was applied to optimize the type and amount of matrix-forming polymer, and Metolose 4000 at 12.7% was selected as the optimal sustained-release polymer system. The optimized TCG-NSP@SMT showed pH-independent sustained release over 12 h, while TCG-NSP powder exhibited rapid dissolution. In rats, TCG-NSP@SMT at 10 mg/kg markedly increased systemic exposure, with a Cmax of 170.7 ± 28.8 ng/mL and an AUC0-24 of 2066.9 ± 1027.8 ng·h/mL, corresponding to a relative bioavailability of 795.6% compared with raw TCG. CT imaging supported prolonged gastrointestinal integrity of the matrix tablet, and PK/PD simulation predicted enhanced and sustained antiplatelet activity. These results suggest that TCG-NSP@SMT is a promising oral formulation strategy for improving the pharmacokinetic and predicted pharmacodynamic performance of poorly water-soluble antiplatelet drugs.

articles.title: Monoammonium glycyrrhizinate micellar systems loaded with curcuminoids: composition-dependent self-assembly, release, and ex vivo skin permeation.
articles.abstract: Monoammonium glycyrrhizinate (MAG) forms non-classical self-assembled micelles and serves as a drug-delivery agent with intrinsic pharmacological and permeation-enhancing properties. However, how drug-surfactant interactions influence micellar architecture and drug skin transport remains poorly understood. In this study, the influence of curcuminoids (CURD) encapsulated at three molar ratios (MAG:CUReq 22:1, 6:1, and 2:1) on MAG self-assembly and skin delivery was investigated. MAG-CURD micellar systems were successfully reconstituted from solvent-free amorphous solid dispersions. Mean micellar size decreased with higher CURD loads, while maintaining a stable ζ-potential (∼ -30 mV). TEM images and molecular dynamics simulations confirmed a structural transition from threadlike fibers to smaller, anisotropic aggregates driven by hydrophobic accommodation. Density and surface tension measurements revealed composition- and temperature-dependent critical aggregation concentrations, indicating a shift from entropy- to enthalpy-driven assembly at higher CURD ratios and temperatures. The micellar systems demonstrated good physical stability at 4 °C for 30 days, while Weibull modeling revealed a non-linear CURD release kinetics among MAG:CUReq ratios. Ex vivo skin permeation studies showed a 5-fold increase in the CURD permeation coefficient for the 22:1 compared with the control. ATR-FTIR analysis of porcine stratum corneum confirmed that MAG-CURD micelles induced less lipid disruption than pure MAG. These findings demonstrate that drug-carrier coupling modulates supramolecular architecture, aggregate stability, and skin barrier interactions, providing useful criteria for optimizing GA-based topical formulations.

articles.title: Intaermedin attenuates chronic intermittent hypoxia-induced renal fibrosis via SIRT1-mediated inhibition of the NOX4/ROS axis.
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) is characterized by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) and is an independent risk factor for chronic kidney disease (CKD); the underlying mechanism may involve oxidative stress. This study investigated the role of intermedin (IMD), a small antioxidant peptide, in CIH-induced renal fibrosis using complementary in vivo and in vitro models. Systemic IMD knockout (IMD-/-) mice and wild-type (IMD+/+) littermates were subjected to CIH for 12 weeks. Human proximal tubular epithelial cell (HK-2) was exposed to CIH for 48 h with or without exogenous IMD. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA) knockdown of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) was performed in IMD-/- mice, and the selective sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) inhibitor EX527 was used in HK-2 cells. We showed that CIH upregulated IMD and its receptors (calcitonin receptor-like receptor [CLR] and receptor activity-modifying proteins [RAMPs]) in both mouse kidneys and HK-2 cells. IMD deficiency exacerbated CIH-induced renal dysfunction, fibrosis, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, whereas exogenous IMD attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, IMD upregulated SIRT1 and suppressed NOX4 expression. NOX4 knockdown in IMD-/- mice partially reversed the aggravated renal injury and fibrosis. In HK-2 cells, EX527 abolished the IMD-induced downregulation of NOX4 and its protective effects against CIH-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, apoptosis, and collagen deposition, indicating that IMD inhibits NOX4 in a SIRT1-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that IMD mitigates CIH-induced renal fibrosis by upregulating SIRT1 and subsequently inhibiting the NOX4/ROS axis. This study identifies IMD as an endogenous renoprotective factor and suggests the SIRT1/NOX4/ROS pathway as a potential therapeutic target for OSAHS-associated nephropathy.

articles.title: Macrophage TBK1 promotes tubular endoplasmic reticulum stress via proinflammatory cytokines in cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is driven by inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, yet the upstream immune mechanisms remain unclear. Macrophages are keymediatorsof renal inflammation, and TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) is an important regulator of inflammatory signaling. However, whether macrophage TBK1 promotes tubular injury bydrivinga proinflammatory cascade has not been defined. We showed that TBK1 was robustly activated in the kidneys following cisplatin injury and predominantly co-localized with macrophages. Myeloid-specific TBK1 deficiency attenuated tubular damage, suppressed proinflammatory molecules expression, inhibited PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP ER stress pathway, and reduced apoptosis. Notably, cisplatin treatment sharply increased F4/80+-TNF-α+ cells in injured kidneys, a population markedly diminished in mice devoid of myeloid TBK1. In vitro, macrophages deficient in TBK1 secreted significantly lower levels of proinflammatory cytokines upon cisplatin stimulation, and their conditioned medium elicited less ER stress and apoptosis in HK-2 cells, with a concomitant suppression of the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP cascade. Critically, replenishment of exogenous TNF-α to this medium fully restored these deleterious effects, along with reactivation of this pathway. Finally, pharmacological TBK1 inhibition with GSK8612 similarly protected against cisplatin nephropathy, reducing kidney injury, ER stress, and apoptosis. In summary, macrophage TBK1 activation drives inflammatory crosstalk, promoting ER stress and apoptosis in tubular epithelial cells during cisplatin-induced AKI. Thus, targeting TBK1 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for cisplatin nephropathy.

articles.title: Heteronemin induces ROS-dependent apoptosis and mitophagy-associated responses through SDHB-associated mitochondrial Complex II dysfunction in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is difficult to treat because of its aggressive growth and limited therapeutic response. Heteronemin (HET), a marine sesterterpenoid, has anticancer activity, but its mitochondrial effects in OSCC remain incompletely defined. In this study, we investigated the relationship between HET-induced cytotoxicity, succinate dehydrogenase complex iron-sulfur subunit B (SDHB)-related Complex II dysfunction, and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent mitochondrial injury using OSCC cells (HSC-3 and Ca9-22), normal oral cells (HGF-1), and zebrafish xenografts. HET selectively suppressed OSCC cell viability and colony formation while inhibiting cell-cycle progression. HET increased intracellular ROS and mitochondrial superoxide, impaired mitochondrial respiration, reduced SDHB abundance, and decreased succinate dehydrogenase activity. SDHB knockdown altered HET-induced ROS accumulation and limited the additional cytotoxic effect of HET, supporting the functional involvement of SDHB-associated mitochondrial dysfunction. N-acetyl-L-cysteine and MitoTEMPO attenuated oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, apoptosis, and cell death. HET also increased mitophagy-associated proteins, including LC3B, PINK1, Parkin, BNIP3, and Nix, and promoted autophagosome/autolysosome formation. Transmission electron microscopy showed damaged mitochondria enclosed within autophagic vacuoles. Furthermore, NAC reduced these mitophagy-related changes, In zebrafish xenografts, HET reduced OSCC tumor without overt toxicity and increased mitophagy-associated markers. Together, these findings indicate that HET-induced OSCC cytotoxicity is associated with SDHB-related Complex II dysfunction, ROS accumulation, mitochondrial injury, intrinsic apoptosis, and mitophagy-associated responses.

articles.title: Dauricine induces programmed cell death protein 1 lysosomal degradation in T cells to enhance cytotoxicity against melanoma.
articles.abstract: Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) is an inhibitory receptor expressed on the surface of activated T cells and suppresses immune responses upon binding to programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Blockade of the PD-1/PD-L1 axis has emerged as a groundbreaking immunotherapeutic strategy for the clinical treatment of various cancers, including melanoma. Dauricine is a natural alkaloid with tumor-suppressing properties, although its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, biochemical and immunofluorescence analyses demonstrated that dauricine effectively reduced PD-1 levels in Jurkat T cells through the endosomal-lysosomal pathway, accompanied by enhanced ubiquitination. Dauricine-induced downregulation of PD-1 led to a marked increase in T-cell-mediated killing of melanoma cells. Furthermore, dauricine inhibited the growth and migration of malignant melanoma cells by inducing apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest at the G1 phase. In vivo studies using melanoma xenograft mouse models confirmed that dauricine enhanced T-cell infiltration into tumor tissues and suppressed melanoma growth. Our investigation revealed novel roles of dauricine in promoting T-cell infiltration into tumors and enhancing cytotoxicity against melanoma cells, thereby providing further evidence to support future clinical evaluation of dauricine as a potential therapeutic agent.

articles.title: Auriculasin induces LACTB expression to regulate colorectal cancer cell apoptosis, ferroptosis, invasion, and in vivo tumor growth.
articles.abstract: Previous studies have found that auriculasin isolated from Flemingia philippinensis has a significant anticancer effect in colorectal cancer (CRC), but there are few studies on its mechanism. Treatment of CRC cells with auriculasin showed that auriculasin promoted LACTB expression in a dose-dependent manner, thereby enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and inhibiting cell viability. Auriculasin significantly enhanced CRC cell apoptosis and caspase-3/8/9 activities, and overexpression of LACTB also increased the caspase activities, but LACTB siRNA or N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) significantly reduced the pro-apoptotic effects of auriculasin and LACTB. Auriculasin or LACTB overexpression significantly inhibited cell invasion, reducing the expression and secretion of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2/9, while LACTB siRNA or NAC restored cell invasion levels. Auriculasin also significantly increased the levels of Fe2+ and malondialdehyde (MDA), and inhibited the expression of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11), but these effects were suppressed by LACTB siRNA; meanwhile, the inhibitory effects of auriculasin, LACTB overexpression and ferroptosis inducer erastin on cell viability could be blocked by the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 or LACTB siRNA, indicating that auriculasin induced ferroptosis through LACTB. Further xenograft mouse model (the most commonly used animal model for tumor research) also showed that auriculasin suppressed tumor growth, increased Fe2+ and MDA levels, and inhibited GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, while LACTB knockdown restored tumor growth by reducing ferroptosis. Therefore, auriculasin enhances ROS production by inducing LACTB expression, thereby increasing apoptosis and ferroptosis, inhibiting cell invasion, and ultimately reducing tumor growth.

articles.title: Evaluation of anti-depressant, anxiolytic, and cognitive improvement effects of nanocurcumin using social isolation model in male mice: Behavioral and histopathological evaluation.
articles.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous mental illness that affects about 10% of people worldwide. Curcumin (Cur) is suggested as a treatment or adjunct treatment of MDD by multiple mechanisms of action. Its effectiveness is limited due to low solubility, poor bioavailability, and rapid metabolization. Different nano-formulations of Cur have been developed to boost its biological activity. The aim of this study was the evaluation of antidepressant/anxiolytic-like effects, and cognitive improvement of nanocurcumin (NCur) in male mice by post-weaning social isolation (PWSI) model to induce depressive/anxiety-like behaviors and cognitive deficits. Mice were housed either in a social group (SG) or an isolated group (IG) for four weeks. After two weeks, IG mice were treated intraperitoneally with NCur (5, 10, 20 mg/kg) and Cur (20 mg/kg) for two weeks. A battery of behavioral tests was used to evaluate depression, anxiety, and cognitive impairment. NCur (20 mg/kg) showed antidepressant-like effect in forced swimming test (P < 0.001) and tail suspension test (P < 0.05), anxiolytic-like effect in elevated plus maze (P < 0.05) and open filed test (P < 0.01), and improved the memory and cognition in passive avoidance test (P < 0.05), but Cur (20 mg/kg) had no effect. Histopathology results showed that NCur (5 mg/kg) led to optimal neuronal survival in CA1, improved cellular organization in CA3, and the highest count of normal neurons in the dentate gyrus. NCur demonstrated potential to treat the depressive/anxiety-like behaviors and impaired cognition induced by the PWSI model in male mice. Histopathological data also showed improvements in hippocampal regions.

articles.title: Survivin mRNA-lipid nanoparticles promote activation of CD8+Granzyme B+ T cells and effector memory formation for effective oral cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Effective cancer immunotherapy requires an understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME) to overcome immune suppression and provide a durable anti-tumor response. Here, we present preclinical evaluation of survivin antigen-encoded mRNA lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) in a murine oral cancer model. In vivo anti-tumor efficacy studies in early-stage tumors (induced by MOC1 cells, tumor volume ∼100 mm3) showed complete tumor elimination within 7-10 days after survivin mRNA-LNPs administration. The mechanistic studies performed to analyze immune cell (including dendritic cells and T cells) activation using flow cytometry and complementary cytokine profiling by ELISA revealed immune reprogramming. Survivin mRNA-LNP administration showed a broad, multi-compartmental T-cell immune response compared with control group. The treatment group showed significantly greater CD4+ and CD8+ T cell expansion in lymph nodes by day 3 (p<0.0001) and robust infiltration into the TME by day 14 (p<0.001) compared with control group. The survivin mRNA-LNPs promoted T cell activation (CD69+, CD28+) and increased cytotoxic CD8+Granzyme B+ T cells in the TME (p<0.001). The survivin mRNA-LNPs group showed controlled Treg levels in the TME providing a favorable effector to Treg ratio critical for superior anti-tumor efficacy. Furthermore, tumor rechallenge study showed formation of immunological memory against oral cancer cells. In conclusion, the present study provides a mechanistic understanding of survivin mRNA-LNP-mediated immune modulation in oral cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetic modeling of idarubicin and idarubicinol in Acute Myeloid Leukemia induction therapy: An Ancillary Study of the BIG-1 Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Idarubicin, a key anthracycline used in the induction treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), is characterized by large interindividual pharmacokinetic (PK) variability. This variability may impact both efficacy and toxicity, highlighting the need for a better understanding of exposure variability and its determinants. METHODS: A joint population PK model of idarubicin and its active metabolite idarubicinol was developed using data from 27 patients enrolled in the BIG-1 study. Plasma concentrations were measured on day 1 of induction therapy following intravenous idarubicin administration. Idarubicin and idarubicinol were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with fluorescence detection. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling was used to describe concentration-time profiles and explore associations with clinical and biological covariates. RESULTS: Among the structures evaluated, a three-compartment model for idarubicin coupled with a two-compartment model for idarubicinol provided the best fit to the observed concentration-time data within 24 hours following infusion. Body surface area and baseline lymphocyte count were identified as exploratory covariates associated with peripheral distribution volumes. CONCLUSIONS: This study describes idarubicin and idarubicinol concentration-time profiles over the observed 24-hour period in patients receiving AML induction therapy. Associations with body surface area and lymphocyte count require confirmation in an independent population. These findings provide a pharmacometric basis for future exposure-response investigations and prospective evaluation of model-informed therapeutic strategies approaches in AML.

articles.title: Serum Concentration Relationships of Candesartan in Migraine Prevention.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a common disabling disorder, and optimising affordable preventive treatments remains highly relevant. Candesartan is an effective and well-tolerated preventive treatment, but little is known about its dose-concentration-response relationships. We explored these relationships using data from the MigriNor study, a prospective observational cohort of adults with episodic or chronic migraine initiating oral preventive treatment. A total of 166 participants using candesartan were included (median age 35 years; 89% female). Participants completed a daily electronic headache diary during a 4-week baseline and 12-week follow-up period with accompanying blood sampling. Dosing regimen was flexible. No differences in adverse drug reactions (ADRs) or treatment acceptability were observed between participants starting 4 versus 8 mg. Substantial interindividual variability in serum concentrations was observed. Higher serum concentrations were associated with lower odds of headache attacks (OR = 0.97, 95% CI = 0.96-0.98, p < 0.001) and migraine attacks (OR = 0.98, 95% CI = 0.97-0.99, p = 0.005). Interquartile ranges of serum concentrations among ≥ 30% and ≥ 50% responders were 62.9-141.2 and 62.3-129.3 nmol/L, respectively, suggesting preliminary therapeutic reference ranges. Serum concentration was not associated with ADRs or treatment acceptability. Interpretation is limited by the flexible dosing design, and studies with fixed dosing regimens are warranted.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profile of high-dose D9-tetrahydrocannabinol in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: Cannabis products with elevated Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content are prevalent in parts of North America, yet their pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) properties remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the effects of a single administration of high-dose THC (10 and 30 mg/kg, intraperitoneal, IP) compared with a lower dose (3 mg/kg, IP) in male and female Long Evans rats. Plasma, brain, and white adipose tissue concentrations of THC and its metabolites 11-hydroxy-THC and 11-carboxy-THC were quantified over acute (up to 24 h) and prolonged (14 days) periods. Behavioral endpoints included ingestive behavior, pica, locomotor activity, anxiety-like and stress-coping responses, and nociception. Plasma concentrations of multiple cytokines were also assessed. PK results showed nonlinear disposition with disproportionate increases in maximal concentration at higher doses, greater systemic and tissue exposure in females, and extensive sequestration in adipose tissue. PD effects were also dose- and sex-dependent: suppression of food/water intake and body weight, transient locomotor stimulation in females at low dose and suppression at high doses, increased pica in females at 30 mg/kg, modest anxiety-like shifts, bidirectional stress-coping changes in males, and antinociception primarily in males at 1 hour and 24 hours postdosing. No meaningful changes in proinflammatory or anti-inflammatory cytokines were observed in either sex. The findings indicate that high-dose THC produces nonlinear sex-dependent PK with prolonged central and peripheral retention, alongside distinct acute PD profiles compared with lower doses. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: High-potency cannabis products are common, yet their impact on health remains poorly understood. This study shows that high-dose THC produces nonlinear, sex-dependent distribution and metabolism in rats, with females showing markedly greater systemic exposure, prolonged brain retention, and extensive adipose sequestration, alongside distinct acute pharmacological profiles. These findings show that high-dose THC generates disproportionate systemic and central exposure and distinct acute pharmacological profiles compared with lower doses.
