articles.title: Comparison of monosodium iodoacetate, medial meniscal transection, and partial medial meniscectomy in vivo rat models of osteoarthritis from the pain and industrial perspective.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a major global health burden marked by progressive cartilage degeneration and chronic pain with intertwined inflammatory and neuropathic mechanisms. This study compared three rat OA models, monosodium iodoacetate (MIA), medial meniscal transection (MMT), and partial medial meniscectomy (MNX), to assess their translational value, suitability for pharmaceutical research, and identify the most robust and reproducible model for preclinical OA pain research. OA was induced in male Wistar (MIA) or Sprague Dawley (MMT, MNX) rats, and pain progression was evaluated by testing mechanical sensitivity and dynamic weight-bearing. A single oral dose of pregabalin (30 mg/kg) was used for pharmacological validation. The MIA model produced a rapid, robust pain phenotype, with pronounced mechanical hypersensitivity and consistent weight-bearing deficits by day 21. Surgical models progressed more slowly and variably: hypersensitivity emerged by day 21 in MNX rats and by day 49 in MMT rats. Neither surgical model generated stable dynamic weight-bearing deficits, indicating limited sensitivity of current gait-analysis methods for detecting their subtler impairments. Pregabalin reduced mechanical hypersensitivity across all 3 models, confirming their pharmacological validity and utility for analgesic screening. Overall, the MIA model remains the most efficient and reliable for industrial research due to its strong behavioral window, whereas the MNX model offers greater translational relevance if paired with more sensitive and objective behavioral measures. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: By systematically comparing chemical and surgical rat models of osteoarthritis, this study clarifies their strengths and limitations for modeling chronic pain. The results demonstrate that, although the monosodium iodoacetate model delivers robust, reproducible behavioral outcomes, surgical models more accurately reflect disease progression but lack sensitive behavioral readouts. This work informs translational model selection and underscores the need for more objective pain assessment tools.

articles.title: Structurome-wide analysis reveals intracellular loop 2 folding as an activation-associated feature of class A G protein-coupled receptors.
articles.abstract: Activation of class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) is commonly described through rearrangement of the transmembrane-bundle and engagement of the Gα α5 helix, whereas the conformational behavior of intracellular loop 2 (ICL2) has not been examined systematically across the structural record. Here, I classified ICL2 as folded, unfolded, or disordered in 1358 experimental class A GPCR structures using a backbone-dihedral criterion and evaluated the classification against activation state, transducer class, crystallization fusions, ICL2-proximal modulators, and resolution. The assignment was additionally assessed using Dictionary of Secondary-Structure of Proteins and a literature-anchored benchmark set. In canonical fusion-free structures, ICL2 was folded in 84% of active structures compared with 53% of inactive structures [odds ratio, 4.74; two-sided Fisher exact test; descriptive P = 7 × 10-13]. The association remained evident after controlling for receptor overrepresentation, within receptors represented in both states, and among active structures without an annotated transducer. Crystallization fusions were associated with increased apparent ICL2 folding in inactive structures. Folded and unfolded ICL2 also showed distinct Gα contact patterns, while sequence features displayed only modest associations with folding. A geometrically compatible contact between ICL2 position 34.53 and the conserved D3.49 residue accompanied the folded state but was not universal. These exploratory structural analyses identify ICL2 folding as an activation-associated feature of class A GPCRs without establishing a causal mechanism or a determinant of transducer selectivity. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This structure-wide analysis shows that intracellular loop 2 (ICL2) folding is strongly enriched in active compared with inactive class A GPCR structures, identifying ICL2 as an intracellular structural readout of receptor activation. The association is retained across major structural controls, while transducer analyses show that ICL2 folding is most prevalent in Gs-bound complexes but does not by itself define coupling specificity.

articles.title: Dual targeting of cytochrome bd and bc1-aa3 terminal oxidases eradicates phenotypically diverse population of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Bedaquiline approval paved the way for the development of drug candidates against energy metabolism pathways of TB-causing organisms, and oxidative phosphorylation was proven to be a relevant target domain. While bedaquiline acts on the F1F0 ATP synthase, Q203 targets the cytochrome bc1-aa3 terminal oxidase, which mediates electron transport to O2 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. However, due to functional redundancies between cytochrome bc1-aa3 and a second terminal oxidase, the cytochrome-bd, the sterilization effect of Q203 is impaired. Here, we describe the identification of BD-2, a novel small molecule inhibitor of the cytochrome-bd in a cell-based screening campaign. Alone, BD-2 does not exhibit any significant activity. When paired with Q203, however, BD-2 strongly inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis respiratory chain function and ATP synthesis. Moreover, BD-2 combined with Q203 was shown to possess potent bactericidal effect on both replicating and nonreplicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including those living under nutrient starved and hypoxic conditions, representing the persistent forms found in granulomas of patients. Mechanistic analysis included molecular docking studies using the known structure of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome-bd, in vitro activity testing on purified enzyme, all of which confirmed that BD-2 is a direct cytochrome-bd inhibitor. Furthermore, the BD-2/Q203 combination was effective against intracellular bacteria in an in vitro macrophage infection model based on THP-1 cells, with over 90% reduction in bacterial load achieved at clinically relevant concentrations. This study supports the hypothesis of combining a cytochrome-bd inhibitor and Q203 in tuberculosis therapy as a rational, mechanistically driven approach that might result in more efficient treatment and overcome antibiotic tolerance.

articles.title: Enlicitide: The First Oral PCSK9i for Lowering Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This article describes pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy data of enlicitide, the first Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor (PCSK9i). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through July 17, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Clinical trials published in English were included. Relevant information from the methodology and results was extracted. DATA SYNTHESIS: Enlicitide received FDA approval on July 16, 2026, based on results from phase 2 and 3 trials showing a 57.1% to 64.6% reduction in low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) and reduced other atherogenic lipid particles at 24 weeks in patients with hypercholesterolemia, including those with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, while maintaining a favorable adverse effect profile. Enlicitide represents the fifth FDA-approved agent targeting PCSK9, having similar efficacy to other agents in class while having a novel macrocyclic peptide formulation with permeation enhancers, allowing for oral administration.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:As PCSK9is continue to be at the forefront of dyslipidemia guidelines, the approval of an oral agent is paramount in ensuring patient access. Enlicitide mirrors LDL-C lowering compared with existing PCSK9is and surpasses LDL-C lowering compared with non-statin options such as bempedoic acid and ezetimibe. Confirmation of cardiovascular outcomes data with enlicitide will solidify its role in reducing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. CONCLUSION: Enlicitide significantly lowered LDL-C similar to existing PCSK9is with few adverse effects. The oral formulation provides an essential option for LDL-C lowering, especially in patients adverse to injections.

articles.title: Ritlecitinib in Nonsegmental Vitiligo: A Systematic Review and Comprehensive Program Synthesis of Clinical Efficacy, Safety, and Biomarker Outcomes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of oral ritlecitinib, a selective Janus kinase 3 (JAK3) and tyrosine kinase expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (TEC) family kinase inhibitor, for the treatment of nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV). DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the Cochrane Library from inception through August 31, 2026. Search terms included combinations of "ritlecitinib," "JAK inhibitor," and "vitiligo.." STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Included studies were clinical trials evaluating ritlecitinib, monotherapy, or with narrowband ultraviolet B (nbUVB), in adults with NSV. Five interrelated studies from the ritlecitinib phase 2b program involving 364 participants were identified for qualitative synthesis. Data extraction included study design, participant demographics, efficacy indices (F-VASI[Facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index], T-VASI [Total Vitiligo Area Scoring Index], and PGIC-V [Patient Global Impression of Change-Vitiligo]), biomarker changes, and safety outcomes. Quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 tool. DATA SYNTHESIS: Ritlecitinib 50 mg daily demonstrated significant facial repigmentation at week 24, achieving a percent change from baseline (%CFB) in F-VASI of -18.5% to -21.2% compared with +2.1% for placebo. Adding nbUVB significantly enhanced efficacy (F-VASI %CFB: -69.6% vs -55.1%; P = .009) and total-body repigmentation. Darker skin phototypes (FST IV-VI) showed earlier and more robust responses (-37.4%) than lighter skin types (FST I-III; -15.2%). Safety outcomes were comparable with placebo, with overall adverse event rates between 60.0% and 86.2% and rare serious adverse events (≤2%). Biomarker analysis confirmed the downregulation of Th1-associated markers (CXCL9 and IFNG) and restoration of melanocyte markers like tyrosinase and Melan-A.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Ritlecitinib 50 mg daily provides a well-tolerated oral systemic option for active NSV. Efficacy is optimized when combined with nbUVB, and baseline skin phototype is a key predictor of the speed and extent of repigmentation. CONCLUSIONS: Oral ritlecitinib 50 mg daily is an effective systemic treatment for active NSV, demonstrating continuous repigmentation through 48 weeks with a favorable safety profile.

articles.title: Low-Dose Buprenorphine Initiation Strategies for Pain.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this review is to describe the common benefits and pitfalls of various low-dose buprenorphine initiation strategies for patients experiencing long-term pain without opioid use disorder (OUD). DATA SOURCES: A search of the primary literature was performed in PubMed using the following keywords: "Buprenorphine OR Buprenorphine-naloxone OR Belbuca OR Suboxone, Primary care OR Outpatient, Pain OR Pain management," from January 1980 to August 2, 2026. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Case reports involving the use of sublingual/buccal buprenorphine in outpatients for pain without OUD were included. DATA SYNTHESIS: Three low-dose buprenorphine initiation methods were evaluated, titrating buprenorphine from once to thrice-daily up to a total of 7 days. Two studies abruptly discontinued full μ-agonists prior to initiating buprenorphine, whereas 1 study tapered full μ-agonists by 25% weekly after day 7. Tapering full-agonist opioids after attainment of target buprenorphine dosing was well tolerated and potentially unneeded after steady-state levels were achieved; bridging analgesia with sufficient pharmacokinetic overlap between buprenorphine and full μ-agonist opioids appears tantamount to mitigating withdrawal symptoms. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: The ideal buprenorphine initiation method considers desired duration, whether to perform cross-titration, product pharmacokinetics, patient-specific factors, and goals of care. CONCLUSIONS: No data exist to support one low-dose buprenorphine initiation method over another. All methods discussed were highly successful at rotating patients to buprenorphine, that is, with equivalent or improved pain control with minimal to no withdrawal symptoms and may be used to build a methodology for starting buprenorphine in outpatients with sub-optimal pain regimens.

articles.title: Dexamethasone-mediated modulation of the renin-angiotensin system: current insights.
articles.abstract: Dexamethasone (DEX) exerts pleiotropic effects that extend beyond classical glucocorticoid receptor signaling and include interactions with the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). Growing evidence indicates that DEX regulates both systemic and tissue-specific RAS activity through genomic and non-genomic mechanisms, affecting the expression and activity of key components, including angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), and angiotensin receptors AT1 and AT2. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on DEX-induced RAS modulation and its physiological and pathological implications. Depending on dose, duration, and biological context, DEX may exert both beneficial and adverse effects. Short-term exposure can suppress renin activity and aldosterone secretion and may provide protective effects in selected acute pathological conditions. In contrast, prolonged or high-dose treatment may promote hypertension, electrolyte imbalance, cardiac remodeling, and tissue dysfunction through dysregulation of RAS signaling. DEX also alters local RAS activity in bone, contributing to osteoporosis and osteonecrosis by enhancing osteoclast activity and impairing osteoblast function. In the kidney and lung, DEX-mediated RAS modulation affects fluid homeostasis, inflammatory responses, and susceptibility to tissue injury. Prenatal exposure to DEX may further induce long-term RAS programming, increasing the risk of cardiovascular, renal, and skeletal disorders in adulthood. Collectively, DEX-RAS interactions represent an important but often overlooked aspect of glucocorticoid pharmacology and may contribute to both the therapeutic and adverse effects of DEX.

articles.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugate Manufacturing: Facility Design, Process Safety, and Regulatory Considerations.
articles.abstract: This paper presents an in-depth examination of the manufacturing, formulation, and fill/finish processes for traditional antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), with particular emphasis on cytotoxic ADCs and the unique risks associated with their production. ADCs inherent toxicity demands rigorous facility and equipment design, proactive risk assessment, and robust risk mitigation strategies. We describe the multiple processes and facility types involved in producing ADCs, with a more detailed focus on drug product facilities. In addition, we study the critical facility risk areas encountered and effective strategies for managing and overcoming those risks. While it is well understood that containment is a critical risk area in the ADC modality, there has been a significant amount of work published with respect to specific containment strategies and solutions for unique unit operations and this area has only been summarized in this review. The paper also addresses regulatory compliance-highlighting EU GMP Annex 1 expectations-and underscores the importance of robust containment strategies and holistic design elements for preventing cross contamination, personnel exposure, and mitigating environmental impact.

articles.title: Case Report: Dasatinib-associated chylothorax and occult Bartonella henselae infection in pediatric leukemia: a case report and systematic review.
articles.abstract: Dasatinib is a second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) used in Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and chylothorax is one of its rare but serious lymphatic complications. We encountered a 14-year-old boy with Ph + acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who developed bilateral chylothorax while on dasatinib, with concurrent B. henselae infection (cat-scratch disease) confirmed in the pleural fluid. Prompted by this index case, we performed a systematic review of the literature to explore the potential association between dasatinib-associated chylothorax and Bartonella henselae infection. We searched multiple databases up to March 2026 and identified 24 cases of TKI-associated chylothorax and 11 cases of leukemia-related cat-scratch disease. In our index case, the pleural fluid triglyceride concentration reached 20.40 mmol/L (≈1806 mg/dL)-the highest value reported to date-and mNGS detected B. henselae together with other organisms. After dasatinib was discontinued and the patient received chest drainage, somatostatin, fasting, and anti-infective therapy with doxycycline plus rifampicin, imaging showed near-complete resolution of the effusion, and repeat mNGS confirmed clearance of B. henselae. A formal causality assessment using the Naranjo scale gave a score of 7, indicating a "probable" adverse drug reaction. This case illustrates that lymphatic and infectious complications can coincide in the same patient. Dasatinib-mediated inhibition of Src family kinases may simultaneously impair lymphatic endothelial integrity and suppress T-cell-mediated immune surveillance, thereby facilitating both chylous leakage and opportunistic infection. Clinicians managing paediatric patients receiving long-term dasatinib therapy should remain vigilant for both lymphatic complications and atypical opportunistic infections.

articles.title: Cefepime-Zidebactam: Leveraging β-Lactam Enhancement Against Difficult-to-Treat and Metallo-β-Lactamase-Producing Gram-Negative Pathogens.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem resistance among Gram-negative bacteria remains a serious public health threat, with metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing organisms increasing substantially in prevalence and few therapeutic options available to adequately address these difficult-to-treat pathogens. Cefepime-zidebactam (FEP-ZID) is a novel β-lactam/β-lactam enhancer combination that offers a mechanistically distinct approach to overcoming resistance in Gram-negative organisms. Zidebactam contributes three complementary mechanisms: inhibition of Class A and C β-lactamases, direct antibacterial activity via PBP2 inhibition, and enhancement of cefepime activity through a reduction in the pharmacodynamic exposure required for bactericidal effect, allowing FEP-ZID to achieve substantial reductions in bacterial burden even in isolates with elevated minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). FEP-ZID was recently approved in the United States for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI), including acute pyelonephritis, caused by Enterobacterales and/or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. FEP-ZID demonstrates broad in vitro and in vivo activity against isolates producing Class A, B, C, and D β-lactamases, as well as organisms harboring PBP3 alterations that are otherwise associated with reduced susceptibility to currently available MBL-active therapies. This spectrum extends across carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, P. aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, and includes activity against isolates with porin loss and efflux upregulation, resistance mechanisms that commonly limit the utility of other β-lactam-based agents. In vivo infection models utilizing humanized regimens have demonstrated bactericidal activity against isolates with FEP-ZID MICs up to 64 μg/mL. The Phase 3 ENHANCE I trial demonstrated noninferiority and subsequent superiority over meropenem in cUTI (including acute pyelonephritis), driven primarily by microbiological response, with favorable outcomes observed across many baseline pathogens, including extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing isolates and patients with concomitant bacteremia. Compassionate use experience further suggests possible utility in severe multidrug-resistant infections across multiple infection types, including bloodstream, osteoarticular, and intra-abdominal infections caused by MBL-producing organisms. Collectively, available preclinical and clinical evidence positions FEP-ZID as a mechanistically distinct option for difficult-to-treat Gram-negative infections, with additional clinical study needed to define its role beyond the currently approved indication.

articles.title: Manufacturing Quality Issues in Healthcare and Cosmetics: An Analysis of FDA Surveillance Data.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Poor manufacturing quality in healthcare and cosmetic products expose people to danger and needs further categorization and assessment. OBJECTIVE: This study reviewed Food and Drug Administration (FDA) records to identify major types of quality issues, the type of products involved, and patterns occurring over time. METHODS: The "FDA Health Fraud Product" and "FDA Recalls, Market Withdrawals, and Safety Alerts" databases were assessed from June 4, 2010, through May 30, 2026. Drugs, cosmetics, and dietary supplements/quasi-legal products with verified manufacturing quality issues were included. Products were sorted by product type and FDA warning letters or official reports were reviewed and categorized. RESULTS: Of 266 reviewed entries, 195 manufacturing quality issues were elucidated from 184 unique products. Drugs accounted for 70% of issues, cosmetics for 21%, and dietary supplement/quasi-legal products for 9%, respectively. Overall, chemical contamination (30%), procedural or testing issues (29%), and microbial contamination (19%) comprised 78% of identified issues. Drug issues were primarily procedural/testing, chemical contamination, and microbial contamination; cosmetic issues were predominantly elemental impurities and chemical contamination; and dietary supplement/quasi-legal issues were mainly microbial contamination, procedural/testing, and elemental impurities. Particulate contamination occurred only in drugs. The number of issues per year showed no consistent trend, but spiked in 2020, 2022, 2024, and 2025. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Manufacturing quality problems varied substantially by product category and occurred in irregular clusters. Inconsistent FDA reporting practices and fluctuations in agency surveillance may have contributed to these patterns. Budgetary cuts to the FDA could increase consumer exposure to manufacturing issues.

articles.title: Editorial: Novel pharmacological interventions in emotional and neuropsychiatric disorders.
Dietary Acrylamide-Glycidamide Exposure and Metabolic Toxicity: Emerging Evidence in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acrylamide is present in a variety of cooked and processed foods, but its precise role in the biological mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains incompletely understood. This review aimed to comprehensively evaluate the relationship between dietary acrylamide exposure, T2D-related metabolic dysfunction, and the molecular mechanisms responsible for its adverse effects. METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted by searching PubMed®, ScienceDirect®, Google Scholar®, and MEDLINE® for English-language publications published between 2002 and 2025. The search strategy used the following Boolean search string: ("acrylamide" OR "glycidamide") AND ("diabetes" OR "type 2 diabetes" OR "insulin resistance" OR "β-cell dysfunction") AND ("oxidative stress" OR "glucose metabolism"). More than 100 relevant publications were identified and included in this review. RESULTS: Current evidence suggests that dietary acrylamide exposure contributes to metabolic dysfunction through multiple interconnected mechanisms, including oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, glycation, insulin resistance, and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Experimental and epidemiological studies indicate that acrylamide may impair glucose metabolism and insulin signalling, thereby contributing to the development and progression of T2D. However, the consistency of epidemiological evidence remains limited by methodological differences and potential confounding factors. DISCUSSION: The available evidence highlights the potential role of dietary acrylamide as a modifiable environmental risk factor for T2D. Strategies aimed at reducing dietary acrylamide exposure through improved food processing, cooking practices, and nutritional interventions may help mitigate metabolic risk. Nevertheless, further well-designed prospective studies and mechanistic investigations are needed to clarify the causal relationship and strengthen the current evidence base. CONCLUSION: Dietary acrylamide exposure may adversely affect glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and pancreatic β-cell function, thereby contributing to the development and progression of T2D. Although current evidence supports a potential association, further high-quality clinical and epidemiological studies are required to establish causality and inform evidence-based preventive strategies.

articles.title: Medicinal Plants in the Management of Anxiety Disorders: Clinical Evidence, Mechanisms, and Safety Considerations.
articles.abstract: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent neuropsychiatric conditions worldwide and represent a major public health burden. Although conventional pharmacological treatments are effective, their long-term use is often limited by adverse effects, including sedation, dependence, and cognitive impairment, prompting growing interest in medicinal plants as alternative or adjunct therapies. This review summarizes current evidence on selected medicinal plants, including Bacopa monnieri, Crocus sativus, Withania somnifera, and Piper methysticum, with emphasis on their pharmacological mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and safety profiles in anxiety management. Preclinical and clinical studies suggest that these plants exert anxiolytic effects through modulation of neurotransmitter systems, particularly γ-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), serotonin, and dopamine pathways, as well as regulation of the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis. In addition, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties may contribute to neuroprotection and improved stress resilience. Clinical findings indicate that certain herbal preparations may offer benefits comparable to conventional therapies for mild to moderate anxiety, often with fewer adverse effects. However, variability in study design, lack of standardized formulations, and insufficient long-term safety data remain significant limitations. Therefore, well-designed randomized controlled trials and mechanistic investigations are required to establish efficacy, safety, and standardization. Overall, medicinal plants show promising potential as complementary or alternative therapeutic options for anxiety disorders, provided their use is supported by rigorous scientific validation.

Lipid-based Nanocarriers for Atorvastatin Delivery: Current Developments and Clinical Translation Prospects.
articles.abstract: Atorvastatin is a well-established first-line medication for treating dyslipidemia, but has significant drawbacks of low aqueous solubility, extensive first-pass metabolism, and limited oral bioavailability. Over recent years, lipid-based nanocarriers have emerged as a viable platform to improve atorvastatin's pharmacokinetic profile by enhancing solubility, facilitating absorption via the lymphatic system, and providing a controlled drug release profile. This review provides a comprehensive overview of four primary lipid-based delivery systems: solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs), nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs), liposomes, and self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery systems (SNEDDS), and their specific application to atorvastatin. Each type of delivery system is reviewed in detail, including composition, drug loading and release mechanisms, encapsulation efficiency, physical characteristics (particle size, surface charge), and in vivo performance. Comparative evaluations indicate that NLCs and SNEDDS achieve the highest bioavailability enhancements (up to five-fold) via improved solubilization and lymphatic transport, whereas SLNs provide superior stability and controlled release, and liposomes offer versatile encapsulation yet limited shelf stability. Additionally, this review integrates current competitive patent opportunities, formulation optimization strategies, and translational research findings from both preclinical and clinical studies. Collectively, these findings show that thoughtful lipid-carrier design can significantly improve atorvastatin's pharmacokinetic profile and ultimately enable the development of large-scale, patient-focused oral lipid formulations.

articles.title: A Review on Mechanisms of Action and Signaling Pathways of Natural Anti-hyperpigmentation Agents.
articles.abstract: Hyperpigmentation is a dermatological condition characterized by excessive melanin production, resulting in skin darkening. Intrinsic and extrinsic mediators, including ultraviolet (UV) radiation, hormonal changes, inflammation, and genetic predisposition, contribute to hyperpigmentation pathogenesis. The current review thoroughly examines the biological processes involved in hyperpigmentation, with particular emphasis on its signaling pathways, particularly the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), wingless-related integration site (Wnt)/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby providing mechanistic insights that may facilitate the development of effective treatments. The review also evaluates the safety, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of TYR inhibitors, arbutin, azelaic acid, ellagic acid, kojic acid, resveratrol, and the melanosome inhibitor niacinamide, for managing hyperpigmentation. Additionally, the review summarizes the in vitro and in vivo studies of these agents and other emerging plant extracts. Recent advances in the use of plant extracts for hyperpigmentation have shown promising efficacy; nevertheless, their translation into clinical and commercial applications remains limited. This limited translation might be attributed to the challenges related to standardization and the paucity of clinical evidence regarding long-term safety. Moreover, ongoing studies on natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents have highlighted the critical role of patent analyses in the advancement of biomedical research. This review provides a strategic direction for researchers to assess the safety, efficacy, and toxicity profiles of natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents.

articles.title: Cannabinoids for Acute Pain Management: A Contemporary Scoping Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The global opioid crisis has intensified interest in non-opioid and opioid-sparing analgesic strategies, including cannabinoids. Despite the expanding legal landscape for cannabis and a rapidly growing cannabinoid market, the clinical evidence for cannabinoid use in acute pain management remains inconsistent and largely of low quality. METHODS: This contemporary scoping review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of six electronic databases (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalKey, EMBASE, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and BIOSIS) was performed for literature published between 1 January 2016 and 5 April 2026, with the final database search executed on 5 April 2026, addressing the pharmacology, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and perioperative implications of cannabinoids in acute and postoperative pain. Two blinded reviewers independently screened records and charted data against predefined eligibility criteria; discrepancies were resolved by a third author. Findings are summarized narratively and in tabular format, and the study selection process is depicted in a PRISMA flow diagram. RESULTS: Preclinical evidence supports robust antinociceptive effects of cannabinoids through multiple receptor pathways; however, these findings have not translated reliably into human acute pain models. Metaanalytic data demonstrate either no significant reduction in acute pain scores with cannabinoids versus placebo, or only small, clinically uncertain improvements. The opioid-sparing effect, while promising in preclinical and some chronic pain studies, has not been demonstrated for acute postoperative pain. A notable exception is a 2024 randomized trial showing a 40% reduction in opioid requirements with perioperative dronabinol after cardiac surgery. Safety data indicate that non-serious adverse events (dizziness, nausea, sedation) are consistently more frequent with cannabinoids than placebo. The 2023 American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (ASRA) consensus guidelines now formalize 21 recommendations for perioperative cannabinoid management. CONCLUSION: While the biological rationale for cannabinoid analgesia is compelling, the clinical evidence base for acute pain remains insufficient to support routine use. Cannabinoids may serve as adjuncts in specific populations, but require careful patient selection, dose titration, and safety monitoring. Well-designed, large randomized controlled trials targeting defined acute pain populations are urgently needed.

articles.title: Mechanistic attenuation by L-carnitine of trastuzumab-induced downregulation of adenosine monophosphate -activated protein kinase signal in cardiac H9c2 cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical usefulness of trastuzumab (TZ) is restrained owing to its cardiotoxic effect. This investigation was initiated to evaluate the potential protective impact of carnitine (CARN) against TZ-related cardiac influence; and to uncover the underlining mechanism. METHODS: Cytotoxic effect of TZ, CARN and their combination was assessed in cardiac H9c2 cells. Carnitine pamlitoyltransferase-1B (CPT1B) and adenosine monophosphate activated protein kinase-α2 (AMPK-α2) expression were investigated using quantitative real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR). Troponin I, creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), Adenosine triphosphate (ATP), malonyl-CoA, acetyl-CoA carboxylase-2 (ACC2) and autophagy protein 5 (ATG-5) were investigated using Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). RESULTS: Challenging cardiac cell with TZ resulted in concentration-dependent decrease in cell viability with inhibitory concentration 50 (IC50) of (1.21 uM). Combining TZ's IC50 and CARN (5 mM) resulted in the most profound drop of cardiac cellular toxicity. Trastuzumab elevated Troponin I, CK-MB, ACC-2 and Malonyl-CoA, while CARN counteracted this elevation. TZ decreased mRNA expression of AMPK-α2 and CPT1B; as well as ATP and ATG-5 levels, but combination of TZ and CARN counteracted this reduction. CONCLUSIONS: TZ disorders AMPK-α2 downstream signaling with the consequent decrease of ATP production and disturbs autophagy. Carnitine tempers TZ-related cardiotoxicity and acts as guard against TZ-related cardiac impact. The current findings are preliminary and highlight the need for additional studies to answer this current research question.

articles.title: Development of Polymeric Microneedles with Variable Lengths for Delivery of Ebselen in Sporotrichosis.
articles.abstract: Sporotrichosis is a subcutaneous mycosis of public health relevance due to the increased zoonotic transmission associated with felines. Ebselen (EB), a poorly water-soluble organic selenium compound, reacts with thiol groups of redox proteins, increases oxidative stress, and causes fungal death. Microneedles (MN) create microchannels in the skin, disrupting the stratum corneum and allowing the release and diffusion of the drug into deeper layers, potentially reaching blood capillaries. Sporotrichosis is typically treated with intravenous or oral therapies. Thus, this study developed polymeric MN for EB delivery, improving drug incorporation and dispersion while providing a minimally invasive topical alternative. A spectrophotometric method for EB analysis was validated. The molds (long and short microneedles) proved to be transparent, flexible, and easy to remove from the MN. The best formulations (F02, F09, F16, and F17) were selected. EB solubility was 0.15%. In light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), both MN types presented well-defined and intact structures. In the compression test, the best formulation (F17) was selected in both molds. In vitro evaluation of the EB release profile from F17 showed that the long mold formulation released the drug faster than the short mold one. In vitro analysis of antifungal activity showed that the formulation containing EB induced the formation of an inhibitory halo, demonstrating antifungal activity against the fungus Sporothrix brasiliensis. Thus, the current results suggest that the MN containing EB is a promising system. Additional biological studies are required to fully assess their safety and performance in the context of sporotrichosis.

articles.title: Risk-based governance of AI-tools used in health-based exposure limit derivation.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to toxicological assessment and health-based exposure limit (HBEL) derivation, offering potential gains in literature retrieval efficiency, methodological consistency, but introducing novel risks such as hallucinated citations, misattributed findings, and fluent yet scientifically shallow narratives. This article examines AI-assisted HBEL derivation through established HBEL quality framework and clarifies its regulatory expectations. HBEL monographs function as scientific expert assessments that inform GMP risk-management, rather than GxP records, a key distinction that is central to establishing proportionate GMP validation requirements. Building on EMA Annex 11 and draft Annex 22, FDA guidance on AI-supported decision-making, and ICH M7 model qualification principles, the article proposes a tiered, risk-proportionate validation framework. Full computerized system validation is not inherently required for AI tools supporting HBEL derivation. Instead, governance should focus on data limitations, and data source verification. Crucially, experienced human toxicologist review and peer review remain the primary, non-negotiable quality controls, ensuring scientific accountability and materially reducing the validation burden on AI components.
